title: `geom_ribbon`: aesthetics can not vary with a ribbon
description:
Hi! I ran across the error in the title when mapping `alpha` to an aesthetic in `geom_ribbon`. ggplot2 is a mature package, so I suspect there are well-founded reasons this isn't supported, but on the off-chance, is this something that can be considered in the future?

In my use case, I was mapping confidence interval around an estimate to `geom_ribbon`, and wanted to have it "fade out" as it projected beyond the current date. Here's a toy reprex with the error:

``` r
library(tidyverse)

pi <- 3.1415926

tibble(x = seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 100)) %>%
  mutate(estimate = sin(x),
         ci_hi = estimate + 0.1,
         ci_lo = estimate - 0.1,
         
         # decrease alpha from pi -> 2*pi
         alpha = if_else(x >= pi, 0.25 * (1 - (x - pi)/pi), 0.25)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = x,
             y = estimate,
             ymin = ci_lo,
             ymax = ci_hi)) + 
  geom_line() +
  geom_ribbon(aes(alpha = alpha))

title: Tear down geom_dotplot and start over
description:
geom_dotplot() is a neglected geom in {ggplot2}.
It does not really work well.

It could be a really useful geom for actually representing counts, and more visually accurate than a histogram, which **_appears_** to be continuous. 

The y-axis does not make sense (0-1??, it should be a count)
The y-axis does not scale properly
There is poor control of color
Grouping does not work
coord_flip does not work

But it is currently severely neglected, as issues #2203, #2868, and #3563 (and several others) have been met with a shrug and auto-closed. 

It might be better to deprecate it if everyone on the maintenance team is not that interested in a historical type of plot. 
Or perhaps, tear it down and start over. 
I think it is worth the effort to make it useful or kill it off.

Lots of apparently popular infographics use something like dot plots to represent counts.
It does seem that people want to use something like this.

It looks weak next to the other well-tended geoms.

Manually rename x axis labels in facet_grid
description:
Hi there. I'm looking at Bacterial relative abundance in restored forests with 3 remnant forests in a separate facet. However, the age for the restored facets is repeating automatically into the remnant facet when I use facet_grid. I want the x axis in the remnant facet to be blank. I could of course just edit over top of this in Inkscape but would like a way of coding this in. 

I;m using a phyloseq object called Bacteriaphyseq in this example containing Bacterial OTU data. The variable "restoration_status" in my excel sheet groups the sites into either the restored or remnant category. "Sample" contains the site codes and "level_order" is ordering them from youngest to oldest restored forests along the x axis. But I don't want to show the site codes on the graph, I want to show age along the x axis so it is simple to view, hence scale_x_discrete is labelling the site codes with their actual age in years, 

Any help would be greatly appreciated! Cannot for the life of me find a solution which involves removing the x axis labels/inputting  nothing into the x axis labels for just one facet.

title: log transform in scale_y_continuous unnecessarily drops negative values
description: Using log transformations for scale_y_continuous (ditto scale_x_continuous but less common a need) unnecessarily drops negative values. Using log(abs(y)) * sign(y) would avoid this issue. Not sure if this is intentional to bring people's attention to what log transformation does, but seems like it will just cause unnecessary extra labor of manually transforming y via dplyr::mutate in many use cases. Apologies if this is an intentional choice!

title: alpha legend keys darken when geom_ribbons share an alpha value
description:
One `geom_ribbon(aes(alpha = foo))` is OK with `scale_alpha_manual()`. Two or more ribbons with `alpha = foo` alters the legend keys. Is there a way to get ggplot 3.3.5 to draw the alpha legend correctly? `override.aes` doesn't work here.
```r
# insert reprex here
data = tibble(x = c(0, 1), confInt1Q025 = 0.025, confInt1Q25 = 0.25, confInt1Q75 = 0.75, confInt1Q975 = 0.975,
              confInt2Q025 = confInt1Q025 + x, confInt2Q25 = confInt1Q25 + x, confInt2Q75 = confInt1Q75 + x, confInt2Q975 = confInt1Q975 + x)
# behaves as expected
ggplot(data) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(x = x, ymin = confInt1Q025, ymax = confInt1Q975, alpha = "95% interval", fill = "confInt1")) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(x = x, ymin = confInt1Q25, ymax = confInt1Q75, alpha = "50% interval", fill = "confInt1")) +
  scale_alpha_manual(breaks = c("95% interval", "50% interval"), values = c(0.1, 0.5))
# produces overly dark alpha legend
ggplot(data) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(x = x, ymin = confInt1Q025, ymax = confInt1Q975, alpha = "95% interval", fill = "confInt1")) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(x = x, ymin = confInt1Q25, ymax = confInt1Q75, alpha = "50% interval", fill = "confInt1")) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(x = x, ymin = confInt2Q025, ymax = confInt2Q975, alpha = "95% interval", fill = "confInt2")) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(x = x, ymin = confInt2Q25, ymax = confInt2Q75, alpha = "50% interval", fill = "confInt2")) +
  guides(alpha = guide_legend(override.aes = list(alpha = c(0.1, 0.5)))) + # has no effect, which isn't surprising but was worth a try
  scale_alpha_manual(breaks = c("95% interval", "50% interval"), values = c(0.1, 0.5))
```
The first plot, where the alpha keys correspond adequately well to the shading in the plot:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/9359341/142503153-87b992ea-0c28-4673-845c-84e2ec48a8bd.png)
The second plot, where the alpha keys are have darkened even though they should be showing the exact same alpha values as in the first plot:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/9359341/142503179-36809ea0-9bdd-45c9-93a0-1141ffac4dd1.png)
The more ribbons the worse this gets. Since I have plots with 5+ overlapping confidence ranges shown this way the alpha keys get so dark they've basically nothing to do with the (correctly) displayed transparency of the ribbons. This reproduces across AGG, Cairo, and Windows so it doesn't look like a graphics device issue.

The least bad workaround I've identified so at the moment is kludgy but probably still better than manual fixup with an image editor (it's a lot messier to implement with the real tibbles than in the repex here).
```R
library(tidyr)
dataWorkaround = data %>% 
  pivot_longer(cols = starts_with("confInt"), names_to = c("confInt", "quantile"), names_pattern = "confInt([[:digit:]])(.*)") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = quantile, values_from = value)
ggplot(dataWorkaround) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(x = x, ymin = Q025, ymax = Q975, alpha = "95% interval", fill = confInt)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(x = x, ymin = Q25, ymax = Q75, alpha = "50% interval", fill = confInt)) +
  guides(alpha = guide_legend(override.aes = list(alpha = c(0.1, 0.5)))) +
  scale_alpha_manual(breaks = c("95% interval", "50% interval"), values = c(0.1, 0.5))
```

title: discarded breaks in scale_x_continuous(trans="log10") w/ min(x)==0
description:
`scale_x_continuous(trans="log10",...)` discards `breaks=` for values below first valid `log10` but within original data range. 

Despite the warning message
> Transformation introduced infinite values in continuous x-axis 

It's hard to debug/discover because the line or points still show a value at x=0.

Is it reasonable to have the default/unspecified limits when trans=log10 to include the min break?
Or warn that the breaks will not be shown because they are outside the plot's limits?


```r
library(ggplot2)
# generic line plot
explt <- function(d)
  ggplot(d) + 
   aes(x=x, y=y) + geom_line() + 
   ggtitle(paste0(min(d$x),'-1000'))

# generate data. i sets min x value
mkdata <- function(i) data.frame(x=seq(0, 1000, 100) + i, y=0:10)

# x axis break label for "1" is MIA
explt(mkdata(0)) + scale_x_continuous(breaks=c(1,1000),trans="log10") 

# 1 is labeled b/c log10(min(x)) is within plot
explt(mkdata(1)) + scale_x_continuous(breaks=c(1,1000),trans="log10") 

# 1 is labeled b/c limits explicitly set
explt(mkdata(0)) + scale_x_continuous(breaks=c(1,1000),trans="log10", limits=c(1,NA)) 
```

title: Is it possible to make the width of geom_boxplot and binwidth in geom_density, and position "mapable" in aes()?
description:
I wanted to draw histograms using the count scale overlapped with a density plot and add a boxplot below, and I want to repeat this over all faceted sub-graphs.

To calculate the proper height of the density, I need to multiply the ..count.. * appropriate binwidth for each sub-plot, which differs per each graph. There's no a universal common value valid for all histograms. I use the Freedman-Diaconis usually, but sometimes I want to provide my own choice. Similarly, to calculate the position and width of the boxplot, I need to know the maximum value of each chart (e.g. to put the boxplot at -10% of max with same width). But, again, this is different for each sub-plot (unless I use fixed Y scale with same limits per all graphs...)

Naively, I thought, that I could pre-calculate necessary values, store them in a data.frame and then map them in aes(). But the binwidth, width and position aren't supposed to be mapped.

One is allowed to provide only constants, but cannot take them from the corresponding dataset.

The only way was to split the dataset by the grouping columns, calculate the necessary values, make a list of per-group ggplots and then combine them via either patchwork (but this doesn't work with faceting and the author doesn't plan to fix it soon: https://github.com/thomasp85/patchwork/issues/277) or cowplot (this one works, but requires some additional coding).

My work could be much simplified, if only the binwidth and width could be parameterised, and the ..count..*column_from_dataset could be mapped.

Is there any chance to add it in future?

Below I show the exemplary code and the effect I wanted to achieve, but made "manually", step by step. Which is very tricky, because when I resize the plot, the layout changes (cowplot) by using relative scaling. I'd love to not have to doing this.

```
binwidth_diaconis_freedman <- function(x) {
    if(length(x) < 2) return(x/10)
    return(2 * IQR(x, na.rm = TRUE) / (length(x)^(1/3)))
}

graphs <- lapply(split(df, list(df$gr1, df$gr2)), function(l) {
    
    #l <- split(df, list(df$gr1, df$gr2))[[1]]
    bw <- binwidth_diaconis_freedman(l$values)

    ghist <- ggplot_build(ggplot(l, aes(x = values)) + geom_histogram(binwidth = bw)) 
    
    max_height <- max(ghist$data[[1]]$y)
    perc_height <- 0.1*max_height

    ggplot(l, aes(x = values)) + 
        facet_wrap(gr1~gr2, 
                   scales="free") + 
        geom_histogram(binwidth = bw, 
                       fill="white", 
                       col="black") + 
        geom_density(aes(y=..count.. * bw), 
                     fill="darkorchid1", 
                     alpha=0.2, 
                     col="darkorchid1") + 
        scale_y_continuous(name = "Count", 
                           labels = scales::label_comma(accuracy = 1)) + 
        geom_boxplot(aes(y = -1 * perc_height),
                     outlier.color = "gray50", 
                     width= perc_height, 
                     col="gray20",
                     size=.5, 
                     position=position_dodge(width=2*perc_height)) +
        
        geom_rug() +
        theme_bw() + 
        theme(axis.title.x=element_blank(),
              axis.title.y=element_blank(),
              plot.margin = unit(c(0,-.2,-1,-.2), "cm"))
})

grs <- cowplot::plot_grid(plotlist = graphs,scale=0.8, labels = rep("", 6), align = "hv") +
    theme(plot.margin = unit(c(0,0,1,1), "cm")) +
    draw_label("Value", x=0.5, y=  0, vjust=2, angle= 0) +
    draw_label("Count", x=  0, y=0.5, vjust= -0.5, angle=90)

title <- ggdraw() + 
              draw_label("Distribution of the vital signs at baseline", x = 0.05, hjust = 0)
cowplot::plot_grid(title, grs, ncol = 1, rel_heights = c(0.1, 1))
    
```
![obraz](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/47183766/140260050-381d282f-e72b-4c6a-bde4-30c4121e23b5.png)

Not to mention, that this looks very weird using facet_grid...

![obraz](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/47183766/140260155-00939284-1577-4642-9317-8ec647104c2c.png)

I'd love to keep my graphs consistent with the default ggplot2 styling when using facets.
To achieve this, all values in the aes() should come from the dataset, not from external single-value variable or hardcoded:

```
ggplot( my_dataset, aes(x = values)) + 

        facet_wrap(gr1~gr2, 
                   scales="free") + 

        geom_histogram(aes(binwidth = bw)) + 

        geom_density(aes(y=..count.. * bw)) +
 
        geom_boxplot(aes(y = -1 * perc_height, 
                               width = perc_height, 
                               position=position_dodge(width=2*perc_height))
       
```

This would be so simple and visually consistent.

title: Inconsistent setting of lineend in draw_key_*
description:
How lineend is set in the draw_key functions does not seem to be standardised and e.g. differs between `draw_key_polygon()` and `draw_key_path()`. In general this is not an issue when the linetype is solid as the ends of the lines are not visible, but once the line is non-solid the lineend will be applied to each segment in the line-pattern. This can result in some dramatic visual discrepancies between what is shown in different keys and in the plot itself.

Example of difference in look between plot and legend as well as difference between polygon and path key:

``` r
ggplot() + 
  geom_segment(
    aes(x = 0, y = 0:1, xend = 1, yend = 1:0, linetype = c('a', 'b')), 
    size = 1.5, 
    lineend = 'round'
  ) + 
  geom_polygon(
    aes(x = c(0.25, 0.75, 0.5), y = c(0.12, 0.12, 0.88), linetype = 'b'), 
    fill = NA, 
    size = 1.5, 
    colour = 'red'
  ) + 
  scale_linetype_manual(values = c('solid', '11'))
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/QCx4uu9.png)

title: `geom_contour()` documentation states false precedence of bin and binwidth parameters
description:
Right now the documentation for `geom_contour()` and friends states that the `bin` argument is overridden by the `binwidth` parameter. However, this seems not to be the case. 


``` r
library(ggplot2)


v <- ggplot(faithfuld, aes(waiting, eruptions, z = density)) 

# Defining bins
v + geom_contour(bins = 5)
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/1JuSkdp.png)

``` r
# Defining binwidth
v + geom_contour(binwidth = 0.001)
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/ab0NaMK.png)

``` r
# Defining both. Per documentation, binwidth should 
# take precedence and this should be the same as the second plot
v + geom_contour(binwidth = 0.001, bins = 5)
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/RiWyFc9.png)

<sup>Created on 2021-10-28 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v2.0.0)</sup>

The issue lays on the `contour_breaks()` function, which computes the binwidth from the bins if bins is not NULL: 

https://github.com/tidyverse/ggplot2/blob/759c63c2fd9e00ba3322c1b74b227f63c98d2e06/R/stat-contour.r#L158-L170 


I believe that previous versions of `geom_contour()` did respect the documentation. Should the documentation be changed to reflect the new precedence or should the code be changed to reflect the documentation?

title: Smarter axis label -- allow string manipulate function in `labs` or `theme`
description:
The current default behavior of ggplot2 is to use the column name as the axis label. This is usually bad as we tend to use lower-case character and '_' in the column name.

## Example

```
library(tidyverse)
tb = iris |>
  janitor::clean_names() |>
  as_tibble()

tb
```
```
# A tibble: 150 × 5
   sepal_length sepal_width petal_length petal_width species
          <dbl>       <dbl>        <dbl>       <dbl> <fct>
 1          5.1         3.5          1.4         0.2 setosa
 2          4.9         3            1.4         0.2 setosa
 3          4.7         3.2          1.3         0.2 setosa
 4          4.6         3.1          1.5         0.2 setosa
 5          5           3.6          1.4         0.2 setosa
 6          5.4         3.9          1.7         0.4 setosa
 7          4.6         3.4          1.4         0.3 setosa
 8          5           3.4          1.5         0.2 setosa
 9          4.4         2.9          1.4         0.2 setosa
10          4.9         3.1          1.5         0.1 setosa
# … with 140 more rows
```
### Default plot
```
p = tb |>
  ggplot(aes(sepal_length, sepal_width)) +
  geom_point() +
  theme_bw()

p
```

title: Use label-attribute as default axis/legend title
description:
Currently, axis and legend titles default to the column names of the data.frame. There are several packages that provide functions to attach more comprehensive variable labels to data.frame columns (e.g., `Hmsic`, `tinylabels`, `labelled`, and `sjlabelled`). While these packages differe with respect to the specific implementation, all implementations are compatible in the sense that they attach the variable labels to the data.frame colums via the `label` attribute. I think it would be useful to use such labels, if available, as they can probably be expected to be more informative than the bare column names.

Consider the following example. First, I'll create some labelled data (I think `tinylabels` provides the safest implementation, but any of the below will work).

~~~r
library("dplyr")
library("ggplot2")

# Set up data & labels using {tinylabels}
library("tinylabels")
mtcars2 <- mtcars |>
  mutate(gear = factor(gear)) |>
  label_variables(
    wt = "Weight (1000 lbs)",
    gear = "Gears",
    vs = "Engine"
  )

# # Set up data & labels using {Hmisc}
# library("Hmisc")
# mtcars2 <- mtcars |>
#   mutate(gear = factor(gear)) |>
#   within({
#     label(gear) <- "Gears"
#     label(wt) <- "Weight (1000 lbs)"
#     label(vs) <- "Engine"
#   })
# 
# # Set up data & labels using {sjlabelled}
# library("sjlabelled")
# mtcars2 <- mtcars |>
#   mutate(gear = factor(gear)) |>
#   var_labels(
#     wt = "Weight (1000 lbs)",
#     gear = "Gears",
#     vs = "Engine"
#   )
~~~

For demonstration purposes I slightly change `ggplot_add.labels` to use the `label` attribute, if available:

~~~r
ggplot_add.labels <- function (object, plot, object_name) {
  object <- add_variable_labels(object, plot) # Newly added code
  ggplot2::update_labels(plot, object)
}

add_variable_labels <- function(labels, plot) {
  vars <- sapply(plot$mapping, function(x) rlang::as_name(rlang::f_rhs(x)))
  
  if(length(vars) == 0) {
    return(labels)
  }
  
  variabel_labels <- lapply(plot$data, attr, "label")[vars]
  
  # Add variable labels
  to_add <- !names(vars) %in% names(labels)
  
  for(i in vars[to_add]) {
    if(!is.null(variabel_labels[[i]])) {
      labels[[names(vars[vars == i])]] <- variabel_labels[[i]]
    }
  }
  
  labels
}

assignInNamespace("ggplot_add.labels", ggplot_add.labels, "ggplot2")
~~~

With this change axis and legend labels will default to the `labels` attribute when `labs()` is called:

~~~r
p <- ggplot(mtcars2, aes(x = wt, y = mpg, colour = gear)) +
  geom_point()

# Standard behavior (uses column names)
p 

# Uses labels, where available
p + labs()

# Overwrite defaults
p + labs( 
  y = "Fuel economy (mpg)"
  , color = "Bears"
)
~~~

I think this would be very nice feature and I'd be happy to take a stab at it.

If this is of interest, I see three options for a proper implementation:

1. Always default to using labels (after some exploration, the required changes seem managable).
2. Only default to using labels when `labs()` is called (pretty much what I have implemented above).
3. Only default to using labels when `labs()` is called and labels are requested (e.g., `use_labels = TRUE`).

There are probably other sensible options that I'm not seeing. Either way, I'd be very interested to know if this would be a PR you would be willing to consider and in any thoughts you may have on this.

title: `alpha` in `geom_raster()` overrides `na.value = "transparent"` in `scale_fill_continuous()`
description:
## Description

I'm trying to produce figures with `geom_raster()` that have:

- 0% opacity for `NA` values; and
- 50% opacity for finite values; with
- fill colors for (continuous) finite values varying by value.

I thought that the code below would achieve that, but supplying `alpha = I(0.5)` in `geom_raster(...)` seems to override the intent of supplying `na.value = "transparent"` in `scale_fill_continuous(...)`.

My expectation is that "50% opaque 'transparent'" should be identical to "transparent", not to "50% opaque white".

## Reprex

```r
library(tidyverse)

# use `faithfuld` but substitute `NA` for values less than 0.01
df <- mutate(faithfuld, density = if_else(density < 0.01, NA_real_, density))
p <- ggplot(df, aes(waiting, eruptions)) 

# - as expected: all NAs are 0% opacity
p + geom_raster(aes(fill = density)) + scale_fill_continuous(na.value = "transparent")

# - as expected: finite values are 50% opacity
# - not as expected: NAs are 50% (?) white rather than fully transparent
p + geom_raster(aes(fill = density), alpha = I(0.5)) + scale_fill_continuous(na.value = "transparent")
```

title: Weights unaccounted for in geom_violin when scale = "counts"
description:
Current ggplot geom_violin fails to account for weighting when scaling violins by counts. Currently the scale = "counts" only uses the vector length of the values, rather than a normalized values*weights measure.

```r
# Test geom_violin

library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)

df <- tibble(name = factor(rep(c("a", "b"), 10)), value = runif(20), weights = rep(c(1, 10), 10))
print(df)

base_w <- ggplot(data = df,
       mapping = aes(x = name, y = value, weights = weights, color = name))

print(base_w +  geom_violin()                + ggtitle("Weighted 10x, scale = ''"))
print(base_w +  geom_violin(scale = "area")  + ggtitle("Weighted 10x, scale = 'area'"))
print(base_w +  geom_violin(scale = "width") + ggtitle("Weighted 10x, scale = 'width'"))
print(base_w +  geom_violin(scale = "count") + ggtitle("Weighted 10x, scale = 'count'", "Fails to account for weighted counts!"))

# Convert to unweighted form by replicating weighted "b" data
# Not when weights are in the millions :-(

dfa <- df %>% filter(name == "a")
dfb <- df %>% filter(name == "b")

df_replicated <- bind_rows(dfa, dfb, dfb, dfb, dfb, dfb, dfb, dfb, dfb, dfb, dfb)
df_replicated$weights <- NULL
print(df_replicated)

base_r <- ggplot(data = df_replicated,
               mapping = aes(x = name, y = value, color = name))

print(base_r +  geom_violin()                + ggtitle("Replicated 10X Unweighted, scale = ''"))
print(base_r +  geom_violin(scale = "area")  + ggtitle("Replicated 10X Unweighted, scale = 'area'"))
print(base_r +  geom_violin(scale = "width") + ggtitle("Replicated 10X Unweighted, scale = 'width'"))
print(base_r +  geom_violin(scale = "count") + ggtitle("Replicated 10X Unweighted, scale = 'count'", "Works correctly"))

```

title: Feature Request: Warn when axis title or axis label goes outside of the plot area
description:
This repeats #3282 as it is not a duplicate of #3281, and PR #3322 works on a related but separate issue.

When text goes outside of the plot area, usually the plot is less readable. It would help to have a warning when text goes outside of the plot area. In the example below, the x-axis labels appear to start at "b" and end at "I" because the text is cut off. It would help find unreadable figures if this resulted in a warning-- especially with automated reporting (like in knitr documents).

I've written the below `no_clipping()` function and added a `makeContent.text()` function to make it warn for any grid graphics text outside of the device.  Adding it to `makeContent.text()` may be more extreme than desired, but it shows at least that the warning is feasible to generate.

``` r
library(grid)
library(ggplot2)

data_with_long_names <-
  data.frame(
    A=c(paste0(rep(LETTERS, 3), collapse=""), paste0(rep(letters, 3), collapse="")),
    B=1
  )

# Feature request: This gives a warning
ggplot(data_with_long_names, aes(x=A, y=B)) +
  geom_point()
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/pGgHVob.png)

``` r
# The no_clipping function indicates if a shape is clipped in any cardinal or
# diagonal direction relative to the entire device.  It should work for any
# rectangular shaped grob.
no_clipping <- function(x) {
  # Check the cardinal directions and corners to allow for any rotation
  angles <- seq(0, 3.5, by=0.5)*90
  if ("rot" %in% names(x)) {
    # At least text grobs have a "rot" attribute
    angles <- angles + (x$rot*pi/180)
  }
  edges_raw <-
    grid::deviceLoc(
      x=grid::grobX(x, theta=angles),
      y=grid::grobY(x, theta=angles)
    )
  edges <-
    list(
      x=grid::convertX(edges_raw$x, unitTo="cm", valueOnly=TRUE),
      y=grid::convertY(edges_raw$y, unitTo="cm", valueOnly=TRUE)
    )
  d_size <- dev.size(units="cm")
  c(
    bottom=0 <= min(edges$y),
    top=max(edges$y) <= d_size[2],
    left=0 <= min(edges$x),
    right=max(edges$x) <= d_size[1]
  )
}

makeContent.text <- function(x) {
  if (!all(no_clipping(x))) {
    warning(
      "Graphics text is outside of the device: ",
      paste0("'", x$label, "'", collapse=", ")
    )
  }

title: alpha aesthetic not plotting consistently with geom_tile()
description:
I am trying to use geom_tile() to shade frequency cells in a matrix that tracks category changes between two time points. This has worked effectively when doing a single plot with a single dataframe, but I've discovered inconsistencies in the alpha aesthetic when combining multiple plots with patchwork.

In this example, I want to combine the plot below with four others, keeping the transparency scale consistent across them all. In my previous efforts, I created a "wt" column that scaled each tile's alpha value to the max frequency in the matrix (which gets alpha= 1). In this case, my max frequency across all plots is 8, so values of 1 should plot with an alpha of 0.125. But I get different results when I feed this value in using that column (the transparency is much darker than it should be) versus specifying 0.125 as a constant outside the aes() function within geom_tile(). I have no idea why there would be this discrepancy, or how to change my code to make sure 1-8 gets mapped to 0.125-1 consistently.

If requested, I'm happy to include more reprex for the other plots, which also are not consistently plotting the alpha values contained in the "wt" column. This was just the simplest example in the 5 plots.

```r
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

# Data
reprex('d <- tibble(
  dim1 = factor(c("R", "S", "S"), levels = c("Q","R","S","T")),
  dim2 = factor(c("Q", "R", "T"), levels = c("Q","R","S","T")),
  chg = factor(c("Lower", "Lower", "Higher"), levels = c("Lower","Higher")),
  n = 1
) %>% 
  mutate(wt = n/8)')

# See data, all 3 values of "wt" are 0.125
d
#> # A tibble: 3 x 5
#>   dim1  dim2  chg        n    wt
#>   <fct> <fct> <fct>  <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1 R     Q     Lower      1 0.125
#> 2 S     R     Lower      1 0.125
#> 3 S     T     Higher     1 0.125

# Example 1 (fail, alpha in plot is not actually 0.125)
ggplot(d, aes(x = dim1, y = dim2)) +
  geom_tile(aes(fill = chg, alpha = wt)) +
  geom_text(aes(label = n)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#B50A2AFF", "#0E84B4FF")) +
  scale_x_discrete(drop=FALSE) +
  scale_y_discrete(drop=FALSE) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

```r

title: Issue with scale_color_manual
description:
I have just updated to the most recent `ggplot2` version (somewhat belatedly) and have noticed a change in how `scale_colour_manual` behaves. This seems along the same lines as #4511 but with a different issue. 

The reprex below generates a plot where the legend order follows the values of y for the most recent date. This works as expected plot 1 below, where `scale_colour_brewer` is used to define the palette. 

Until I upgraded `ggplot2`, I had the same result with `scale_colour_manual`. Now, however, the legend items are ordered alphabetically instead. This is reproduced in plot 2 below.

I can't find anything to suggest that this was an intended change - apologies if I have missed that. I really appreciate folks taking a look at this and helping sort out what is going on here!

``` r
# dependencies
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(dplyr)
  library(forcats)
  library(ggplot2)
  library(readr)
  
  library(RColorBrewer)
})
  
# load data
metro_data <- read_csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/slu-openGIS/MO_HEALTH_Covid_Tracking/master/data/metro_all/metro_full.csv")
#> Rows: 4792 Columns: 14
#> ── Column specification ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> Delimiter: ","

#> 
#> ℹ Use `spec()` to retrieve the full column specification for this data.
#> ℹ Specify the column types or set `show_col_types = FALSE` to quiet this message.
# prep data
## subset
metro_data <- filter(metro_data, report_date >= "2020-03-10")

## create factors
metro_data <- mutate(metro_data, factor_var = fct_reorder2(short_name, report_date, case_rate))

# plot data
## define colors
pal <- brewer.pal(n = 8, name = "Set1")
cols <- c("Cape Girardeau" = pal[6], "Columbia" = pal[3],

title: Axis labels accept plotmath expressions
description:
This is a doc suggestion.

The axis labelling functions like `scale_y_continuous()` have a `labels` argument.  This argument accepts plotmath expressions, but is not documented to do so.

```r
df <- data.frame(x=1:3, y=c(1,10,100))
library(ggplot2)
ggplot(df, aes(x=x, y=y)) +
  geom_point() +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks=c(1,10,100),
                     labels=expression(10^0, 10^1, 10^2))
```

The docs say

labels  
One of:
 - NULL for no labels
 - waiver() for the default labels computed by the transformation object
 - A character vector giving labels (must be same length as breaks)
 - A function that takes the breaks as input and returns labels as output. Also accepts rlang lambda function notation.

I'd add

 - An expression vector (must be the same length as breaks).  See ?plotmath for details.

title: Inconsistent behavior of `strip.switch.pad.grid` and `strip.switch.pad.wrap` in ggplot 3.3.3
description:
---

According to `?theme`, `strip.switch.pad.grid` and `strip.switch.pad.wrap` have the same effect, _i.e._ "space between strips and axes when strips are switched (unit)". My intuitive understanding was to use `strip.switch.pad.wrap` with `facet_wrap` and `strip.switch.pad.grid` with `facet_frid`. However this is wrong according to the reprex below:

```r
    library(ggplot2)
    p <- ggplot(data = iris, aes(x = Sepal.Length, y = Petal.Length)) + theme(strip.placement = "outside")
```
```r

title: `geom_sf()` misaligns aesthetics for partially empty polygon geometries
description:
Aesthetics applied to sf POLYGON geometries become misaligned when an empty
polygon exists in the dataset. This issue was brought up by a student of mine (@myan0065)
who noticed that an area on the map had a fill colour that did not match the
data passed to the fill aesthetic.

This behaviour is tested with dev and CRAN versions of ggplot2 and sf.

``` r
library(ggplot2)
library(sf)
#> Linking to GEOS 3.8.0, GDAL 3.0.4, PROJ 6.3.1
# MULTIPOLYGON of nc from sf package
nc_mp <- st_read(system.file("shape/nc.shp", package = "sf"), quiet = TRUE)
# Cast to POLYGON of nc from sf package
nc_p <- st_cast(nc_mp, "POLYGON")
#> Warning in st_cast.sf(nc_mp, "POLYGON"): repeating attributes for all sub-
#> geometries for which they may not be constant
```

Plotting complete geometry of MULTIPOLYGON and POLYGON versions works great 🎉

``` r
# MULTIPOLYGON
ggplot(nc_mp) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = AREA))
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/UP4XNqr.png)

``` r
# POLYGON
ggplot(nc_p) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = AREA))
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/7nYWmhV.png)

When the dataset contains an empty POLYGON the misalignment occurs

``` r
# EMPTY MULTIPOLYGON gives the expected result (a missing polygon in the plot)
nc_mp$geometry[1] <- st_multipolygon()
ggplot(nc_mp) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = AREA))
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/clsXi9O.png)

``` r
# EMPTY POLYGON misaligns the fill aesthetic across different polygons
nc_p$geometry[1] <- st_polygon()
ggplot(nc_p) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = AREA))
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/bi0hqUr.png)

The fill colour no longer matches the data's provided AREA 😱
This also applies to other aesthetics such as colour.

``` r
nc_p %>% 
  dplyr::filter(!st_is_empty(geometry)) %>% 
  ggplot() + 
  geom_sf(aes(fill = AREA))
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/75mpobV.png)

Removing the empty geometries fixes the issue 😌

title: Unclear documentation: geom_label, geom_text, and others: position argument
description:
# Problem

The documentation for `geom_label()` and `geom_text()` (and many other geoms) is unclear about the `position` argument. It says, “Position adjustment, either as a string, or the result of a call to a position adjustment function”. Nothing in that description is helpful to a user like me. I am left wondering what strings are options and what a “position adjustment function” is.

# Additional issues

Sure, there is an online reference that explains this if the user knows to look for it and knows where to look within it, but if that is something the user needs to know, it needs to be documented. The user should also not have to already know the names of the position functions to be able to get to their documentation from the position argument of a geom documentation page.

I also get that it is not sufficient to simply list off some strings and functions because someone could make a custom position function. However, this does not justify giving no information at all about existing functions that are built-in to the `ggplot2` package (and their string handles, I suppose) or on the conditions that custom position functions must meet.

# Proposed solution:

The documentation should 
1. list every available position string and position adjustment function that is built-in to the `ggplot2` package
2. state that custom position adjustment functions may also be used
3. describe exactly what a “position adjustment function” is (i.e. what conditions would my own custom function have to satisfy?)

On points 1 and 3, if the implementation is likely to change over time, it may be best to link to another page of documentation that lists the current functions and strings (and what is a valid position function) in order to avoid having to update the documentation for many geoms every time the position options change. This content has already been written and included in the reference manual, so it only needs to be ported into the documentation somewhere (maybe at the package level).

title: `ggsave` jpg reversed black-white values with `theme_minimal()`
description:
When using `ggsave` to save a `.jpg` file of a plot that uses `theme_minimal` the image has reversed black and white values in a sort of photo negative effect. It appears that this issue can be resolved by `bg="white"` into the ggsave call or adding `theme(plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA))` to the plot. It would be better to fix this directly. 

The issue does not occur when not using a theme, nor when using `theme_bw`. I have produced the problem on macos 10.15.7 running R 4.0.2. 

I created a [stack overflow post ](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/69067985/ggsave-jpg-reversed-black-white-values-with-theme-minimal) which received comments with the two work around posted above. 

This is the example I included with the stackoverflow post. Because I have not isolated what is causing the unwanted saving behavior, this may or may not reproduce on your machine. At least [one other SO user reports seeing the same behavior](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/69067985/ggsave-jpg-reversed-black-white-values-with-theme-minimal#comment122070155_69067985). 

```r
library(ggplot2) 
ggplot(diamonds, aes(x = cut, y = clarity)) + 
  geom_point() + 
  theme_minimal() 

ggsave("test_minimal.jpg")

```

> Fucking passive aggressive console messages. Also, the code was fine, no errors. 
>
> I'm waiting for the one that says "You don't seem to know what you're doing, just give up." (https://twitter.com/Arfness/status/1433073006939607047)

title: Improve behaviour when `labeller()` does not find a match in lookup table
description:
Currently, `ggplot2::labeller()` silently labels the facets with "NA" if the user supplies unnamed character vectors.

``` r
library(ggplot2)
ggplot(ToothGrowth, aes(y = len)) + 
  geom_boxplot() +
  facet_wrap(vars(supp), labeller = labeller(supp = c("orange juice yum", "vitamin C yuck")))
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/hwFq0rw.png)

If there is a typo in the name (or if there just isn't a new label defined in the vector), the same thing happens: "NA" is given as a title.

``` r
library(ggplot2)
ggplot(ToothGrowth, aes(y = len)) + 
  geom_boxplot() +
  facet_wrap(vars(supp), labeller = labeller(supp = c("OJ" = "orange juice yum", "vC" = "vitamin C yuck")))
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/8mY9fdy.png)

I am not sure what would be most appropriate, but I would have expected to get something like this:

```
Warning: labeller() could not match one or more of the original labels. The facets were titled "NA".
ℹ: did you forget to provide a named character vector, or are some labels missing from the lookup table?
```

The function allows using lookup tables that include _superfluous_ data, which is probably good for flexibility, but I think that naming a facet with "NA" should throw a warning, or at least a message, when the is _not enough_ data.

Or should the default behaviour change to using the original label if no match is found, allowing the use of partial lookup tables? I can see people wanting to only cherry pick a couple of labels to replace.

Using: 
* ggplot2 3.3.5
* R 4.1.1

Most alpha-related bugs seem to be caused by actually drawing the line/object multiple times, but I don't _think_ this is one of those - unless it's an artifact of how the hex drawing code works?

(I'm also perfectly fine with the answer being "then don't do that".)

```r
library(ggplot2)

(df <- data.frame(x=1:10, y=1:10, z=1:10*1:10))
ggplot(df, aes(x=x, y=y, z=z)) + 
  stat_summary_hex(aes(color=..value.., alpha=..value..),
    fun=mean, bins=2, size=2)

```

the red dotted line should be the same as the solid green:

install.packages("ggplot2") 
  library(ggplot2)

    OL = c (2,7),

  )
  ggplot(grafiek,mapping=aes(x=OL))+
    xlim(0,NA)+
    geom_point(aes(y=TT), size=5, shape=8)+

    geom_smooth(aes(y=TT),method = "lm", fullrange=TRUE, linetype="dotted", size=4, col="RED"  ,formula=y~0+splines::ns(x,df=1,intercept=FALSE), se=F)+

title: Feature Request: Warn when axis title or axis label goes outside of the plot area
description:
This is re-opening #3282 as the fix in #3398 was for a related, but distinct, issue.  The reprex from #3282 has been updated with the feature added in #3398 to clarify why this is distinct.  I have also updated the reprex to make more parts of the issue clearer.

When text goes outside of the plot area, usually the plot is less readable. It would help to have a warning when text goes outside of the plot area. In the example below, the x-axis tick labels appear to start at "b" and end at "I" because the text is cut off. It would help find unreadable figures if this resulted in a warning-- especially with automated reporting (like in knitr documents).

I have also added an example where the x-axis label goes off the side since that is a distinct element which would need similar management.

``` r
library(ggplot2)

data_with_long_names <-
  data.frame(
    A=c(paste0(rep(LETTERS, 3), collapse=""), paste0(rep(letters, 3), collapse="")),
    B=1
  )

# Feature request: This gives a warning due to tick labels going off the side
ggplot(data_with_long_names, aes(x=A, y=B)) +
  geom_point() +
  scale_x_discrete(guide=guide_axis(n.dodge=2))
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/AV5whH4.png)

``` r
# Feature request: this gives a warning due to the axis label going off the side
# (and the tick labels going off the side)
ggplot(data_with_long_names, aes(x=A, y=B)) +
  geom_point() +
  scale_x_discrete(guide=guide_axis(n.dodge=2)) +
  labs(
    x=paste(rep(paste0(LETTERS, collapse=""), 4), collapse=" ")
  )
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/WsSnQP5.png)

title: Permit guide_axis() angle heuristics in guide_legend(), etc.
description:
cf. https://stackoverflow.com/questions/68925483/overlapping-labels-in-legend-in-ggplot

The `guide_axis()` function has helpful heuristics in the `angle` function to automatically set the `hjust` and `vjust` parameters. It would be really nice if these heuristics were also available in `guide_legend()`, `guide_colorbar()`, etc. to rotate legend labels. These could be provided with a `label.angle` argument to accompany the existing `label.theme`, `label.vjust`, and `label.hjust` arguments.

Example:
```r
library(ggplot2)
df <- expand.grid(X1 = 1:10, X2 = 1:10)
df$value <- df$X1 * df$X2

ggplot(df, aes(X1, X2)) + geom_tile(aes(fill = value)) +
    scale_fill_continuous(guide = guide_colourbar(direction = "horizontal", label.angle = 30))
```

title: Geom_smooth with binomial GLM doesn't work with log scale
description:
Consider the following example:

``` r
library(ggplot2)
tb1 <- data.frame(x = runif(100)*100, success = rbinom(100, 100, 0.1), failure = rbinom(100, 100, 0.8))

p1 <- ggplot(tb1, aes(x, y=success/(success+failure), succ=success, fail=failure)) +
  geom_point() + geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x)
p1
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/040jPin.png)

``` r
p1 + scale_y_log10()
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/nKmczr2.png)

<sup>Created on 2021-08-24 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v2.0.1)</sup>

Everything works fine, both for the original and for the log-scale.

However, all else equal, but using Binomial GLM instead of LM, this is what we get:

``` r
library(ggplot2)
tb1 <- data.frame(x = runif(100)*100, success = rbinom(100, 100, 0.1), failure = rbinom(100, 100, 0.8))
p2 <- ggplot(tb1, aes(x, y=success/(success+failure), succ=success, fail=failure)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method="glm", method.args=list(family="binomial"), formula = cbind(succ, fail) ~ x)
p2
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/kTuwm9a.png)

``` r
p2 + scale_y_log10()
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/cnAPxMm.png)

<sup>Created on 2021-08-24 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v2.0.1)</sup>

I.e., it seems it doesn't really like the log scale for some reason.

title: `ggplot_build()` modifies the input plot and also any clones.
description:
In trying to cache ggplot2 plots I stumbled this unintuitive behaviour

``` r
library(ggplot2)

N <- 1000
plot <- ggplot(diamonds[sample(nrow(diamonds), N), ], aes(price, x*y*z)) +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess")

clone <- ggplot2:::plot_clone(plot)

rlang::hash(plot)
#> [1] "5ba9bc5515f606e36209cd718b6ecdd8"
rlang::hash(clone)
#> [1] "b5e50b1b1598a86fe45e8bdf24dcb80d"

invisible(ggplot_build(plot))
#> `geom_smooth()` using formula 'y ~ x'


rlang::hash(plot)
#> [1] "336102f77437e4d772ee4ba09bd6c49b"
rlang::hash(clone)
#> [1] "5ca7bfd3ebd2be8c9e41885de22e9a41"
```

<sup>Created on 2021-08-20 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v2.0.0)</sup>

In particular, in this case `ggplot_build()` is modifying the layers

``` r
library(ggplot2)

N <- 1000
plot <- ggplot(diamonds[sample(nrow(diamonds), N), ], aes(price, x*y*z)) +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess")

original_hash <- vapply(plot, rlang::hash, "a")

invisible(ggplot_build(plot))
#> `geom_smooth()` using formula 'y ~ x'

new_hash <- vapply(plot, rlang::hash, "a")

original_hash[original_hash != new_hash]
#>                             layers 
#> "5b210f0aa90f18830eac0a088d0133aa"
```

Cloning the layers with the `ggproto(NULL, x)` trick does the... trick.

``` r
library(ggplot2)

N <- 1000
plot <- ggplot(diamonds[sample(nrow(diamonds), N), ], aes(price, x*y*z)) +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess")


clone_deep <- function (plot) {
  p <- plot
  p$layers <- lapply(plot$layers, function(x) ggproto(NULL, x))
  p$scales <- plot$scales$clone()
  p
}

original_hash <- vapply(plot, rlang::hash, "a")

plot2 <- clone_deep(plot)

invisible(ggplot_build(plot2))
#> `geom_smooth()` using formula 'y ~ x'

new_hash <- vapply(plot, rlang::hash, "a")


original_hash[original_hash != new_hash]
#> named character(0)
```

But in my real case, coordinates and scales are also modified. Cloning coords with the same method works to protect them, but scales are a lost cause. In particular, what's being changed on my more real example is the environment of the `palette()` and `rescaler()` functions of some scales.

title: Misleading error message when plotting with empty data.frame
description:
When plotting with an empty data (which may happen when filtering goes wrong), there is an error if constant aesthetics are mixed with column names, and the error message is a little confusing.

Example:
```r
> ggplot(head(mtcars, 0)) + geom_point(aes(x = hp, y = mpg)) # no error here, plot is empty
> ggplot(head(mtcars, 0)) + geom_point(aes(x = 3, y = 4))        # no error here, plot contains one point
> ggplot(head(mtcars, 0)) + geom_point(aes(x = 3, y = mpg))   # error!
 Fehler: Aesthetics must be either length 1 or the same as the data (1): y
Run `rlang::last_error()` to see where the error occurred. 
```

Taken literally, the error message is wrong: Aesthetics `y` does have the same length as the data (0).

Expected behaviour: No error message, return an empty plot.

title: allow `coord_fixed()` with `facet_grid(..., scales = "free", space = "free")` when x and y scales are discrete
description:
It makes sense that it’s not possible to mix `facet_grid(..., scales = "free", space = "free")` with `coord_fixed()` in most situations. However, I think that it should be possible and makes sense to allow this when both, x and y, scales are discrete.

For example, a use case in this reprex with `ggplot2` version 3.3.4:

``` r
library(tidyverse) # with ggplot2 v3.3.4
set.seed(1)
df <- expand_grid(x = letters[1:6], y = LETTERS[1:2]) %>% 
  mutate(w = case_when(x %in% letters[1:2] ~ "1",
                       x %in% letters[3:6] ~ "2")) %>% 
  mutate(value = rnorm(6*2))

gg <- ggplot(df) +
    geom_point(aes(x, y, color = value)) +
    facet_grid(cols = vars(w), scales = "free", space = "free")

gg
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/oHWJLHO.png)

Here, we have different numbers and levels of factors in x scale, so it’s necessary to use `scales = "free"` and `space = "free"` for efficient use of space.

When I make plots like this one, I like to make sure that the breaks on x and y axes are placed equidistantly (so the background grid is made of squares), which would generally be accomplished with `coord_fixed()` but not possible in this case since we are using free scales and space.

``` r
gg + coord_fixed()
#> Error: coord_fixed doesn't support free scales
```

As of version 3.3.3 of `ggplot2` it was possible to still accomplish this without `coord_fixed()` by the (perhaps hacky and off-label) use of `theme(aspect.ratio = 1)`, also pointed out in this [SO post](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/16258095/facet-with-free-scales-but-keep-aspect-ratio-fixed/44271207#44271207). See reprex below with version 3.3.3. This is however no longer possible since this bug was fixed (\#4432).

``` r
library(tidyverse) # with ggplot2 v3.3.3
set.seed(1)
df <- expand_grid(x = letters[1:6], y = LETTERS[1:2]) %>% 
  mutate(w = case_when(x %in% letters[1:2] ~ "1",
                       x %in% letters[3:6] ~ "2")) %>% 
  mutate(value = rnorm(6*2))

gg <- ggplot(df) +
  geom_point(aes(x, y, color = value)) +
  facet_grid(cols = vars(w), scales = "free", space = "free")

gg + theme(aspect.ratio = 1)
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/fSXCgUS.png)

It would be great if this can be accomplished legitimately with `coord_fixed()` rather than by using hacks. Based on my admittedly superficial understanding, I think that the use of `coord_fixed()` when faceting with free scales and space should be legitimate as long as the x and y scales are discrete.

title: Using `alpha` in `geom_line` and `clip="off"` in the same plot makes the line disappear when viewed in RStudio
description:
When specifying ` alpha` in `geom_line()` and using `coord_cartesian(clip='off')` together in the same plot, the line disappears when viewed in RStudio.  I'm not sure if this is a `ggplot` bug or RStudio bug. Here is a (mostly) reproducible example. It's possible that this isn't fully reproducible.  

1. Here is a plot with `alpha` in `geom_line()`. There is a line. 
  
```r
library(ggplot2)
df = mtcars[1:2,]
ggplot(df, aes(wt, mpg))+
  geom_point(alpha=0.7)+
  geom_line(alpha=0.7) + 
  ggtitle("With geom_line(alpha=0.7)")
```
![geom_line and alpha](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/41492363/127577236-b8e4dd53-5eb9-4f47-b6e2-c142ac613f19.jpeg)


2. Here is a plot with `coord_cartesian(clip='off')`. There is a line. 

```r
ggplot(df, aes(wt, mpg))+
  geom_point()+
  geom_line()+
  coord_cartesian(clip='off')+
  ggtitle("With coord_cartesian(clip='off')")
```
![clip off](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/41492363/127577253-1d6fff50-d24f-4c71-a085-898574f60b88.jpeg)

3. Here is a plot with both `geom_line(alpha=0.7)` and `coord_cartesian(clip='off')`. The line disappears when viewed in RStudio. 

```r
ggplot(df, aes(wt, mpg))+
  geom_point(alpha=0.7)+
  geom_line(alpha=0.7)+
  coord_cartesian(clip='off')+
  ggtitle("With geom_line(alpha=0.7) and coord_cartesian(clip='off')")
```

![screenshot with alpha and clip off](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/41492363/127578484-67699c92-64d5-4262-a7b6-71aec6d3d036.JPG)

The line re-appears when saving the image to a file.  

It's not just because the line in thin.  This code 

```r
ggplot(df, aes(wt, mpg))+
  geom_point(alpha=0.7)+
  geom_line(alpha=0.7, size=10)+
  coord_cartesian(clip='off')+
  ggtitle("With geom_line(alpha=0.7) and coord_cartesian(clip='off')")
```
with `size=10` in `geom_line()` added produces the same result that there is no line when viewed in RStudio. 

### Versions
ggplot2 - 3.3.5
RStudio - 1.3.1093

title: misleading error message in geom_dotplot
description:

```r
library(ggplot2)
d <- data.frame(A = rep(1:3, times = 10))

ggplot(d, aes(x = A)) +
  geom_dotplot()
## No error here. Neither does y seem to be required.

# Now map y to something spurious and inappropriate:
ggplot(d, aes(x = A, y = A + 1)) +
  geom_dotplot()
```
```
Error: geom_dotplot requires the following missing aesthetics: y
```

I guess this is a very minor issue. But I have really come to appreciate the tidyverse's informative error messages, so I thought I'd report this in case there is an easy fix.

title: [feature request] Add positional arguments to `guide_legend()` and `guide_colourbar()`, just like `guide_axis()`
description:
When making a plot with `geom_point()` that has both `color = column_1` and `size = column_2` arguments in the aesthetics, `ggplot` provides two separate legends. One for the `color` column and one for the `size`.

It would be great to have the ability to change the location of these legends independently, e.g. to have the `color` legend at the top running horizontally and the `size` legend on the right stacked vertically.

I've searched for a quick solution to this, but there doesn't seem to be one. I have, however, found a number of Stackoverflow posts (going back to 2012) which present the same hack solution: 

1. make a version of the plot without any legend,
2. make separate plots for the `size` and `color` arguments, 
3. use `cowplot::get_legend()` to pull out the legends from the plots that have them,
4. use `cowplot::plot_grid()` to combine objects together and position legends independently.

Here are a few examples of SO posts which show this approach, and (arguably) demonstrate demand for this feature.  

- [ggplot - Multiple legends arrangement](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/52060601/ggplot-multiple-legends-arrangement)
- [How to place legends at different sides of plot (bottom and right side) with ggplot2?](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/68369581/how-to-place-legends-at-different-sides-of-plot-bottom-and-right-side-with-ggp/68369737#68369737)
- [How do I position two legends independently in ggplot](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/13143894/how-do-i-position-two-legends-independently-in-ggplot?noredirect=1&lq=1)
- [Different legend positions on plot with multiple legends](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/68497565/different-legend-positions-on-plot-with-multiple-legends)

The suggested syntax for interacting with this feature could be to add positional arguments to `ggplot()`'s `guide_legend()` and `guide_colourbar()`, just like `guide_axis()`

### Code for best known approach to position legends independently in graph region:
```
library(cowplot) 
library(ggplot2)

 # plot without legend
main_plot <-  ggplot(data = df) + 
    geom_point(aes(x = factor(season_num), y = rating, size = count, color = doctor)) +
    labs(x = "Season", y = "Rating (1-10)", title = "IMDb ratings distributions by Season") +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(legend.position = 'none',
          legend.title = element_blank(),
          plot.title = element_text(size = 10),
          axis.title.x = element_text(size = 10),
          axis.title.y = element_text(size = 10)) +
    scale_size_continuous(range = c(1,8)) +
    scale_y_continuous(limits=c(1, 10), breaks=c(seq(1, 10, by = 1))) +
    scale_x_discrete(breaks=c(seq(27, 38, by = 1))) +
    scale_color_brewer(palette = "Dark2")

# color legend, top, horizontally
color_plot <-  ggplot(data = df) + 
  geom_point(aes(x = factor(season_num), y = rating, color = doctor)) +
  theme(legend.position = 'top',
        legend.title = element_blank()) +
  scale_color_brewer(palette = "Dark2")

color_legend <- cowplot::get_legend(color_plot)

# size legend, right-hand side, vertically
size_plot <-  ggplot(data = df) + 
  geom_point(aes(x = factor(season_num), y = rating, size = count)) +
  theme(legend.position = 'right',
        legend.title = element_blank()) +
  scale_size_continuous(range = c(1,8))

size_legend <- cowplot::get_legend(size_plot)

# combine all these elements
cowplot::plot_grid(plotlist = list(color_legend,NULL, main_plot, size_legend),
          rel_heights = c(1, 5),
          rel_widths =  c(4, 1))
```

[![enter image description here][1]][1]

  [1]: https://i.stack.imgur.com/Opa2M.png

It feels like the above graph requires an unnecessarily large amount of code repetition to achieve independent legend placement. There's also good logic to why one would want to do that; in the above instance, for ex., size should run vertically and the doctor's name should run horizontally as that's how the data are presented so I feel it corresponds better to the natural eye movement of the reader

title: Allow functions in `breaks` argument to `stat_bin()`
description:
Allowing `breaks` in `stat_bin()` to accept functions would be useful in the context of grouping structures.

The changes would also enable facet histograms for estimators with variable bin width, e.g, equal area of all blocks, or the "essential histogram" (doi:10.1093/biomet/asz081). The same effect (with `facet_*`) is of course already possible using `geom_rect()`.

The required code additions would be minimal and follow the same idea as #1890

A simple illustration how this could work is given below:

```
df <- data.frame(
    x = c(rexp(1000), rexp(1000, 5)),
    study = c(rep("A", 1000), rep("B", 1000))
)
ggplot(df, aes(x)) +
    geom_histogram(aes(y = ..density..), breaks = function(x) qexp(c(0, .25, .5, .75, .95, .99), 1/mean(x))) +
    facet_wrap(vars(study))
```

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/8480406/126669301-3f1c2fca-6a47-480b-8cb0-5023d1529c17.png)

title: Setting `size = NA` on a geom causes error in legend generation
description:
This is a bit of a weird corner case I think, but I've found (on CRAN and on the github version as of today) that setting `size = NA` on several geoms causes guide generation to fail and therefore the plot to fail to generate. 

I'll use this data:

```r
df = data.frame(
  x = c(1, 2),
  group = c("a","b")
)
```

First, a reprex with `geom_tile()` (the `fill` mapping is needed so that a guide is generated):

``` r
library(ggplot2)
df = data.frame(
  x = c(1, 2),
  group = c("a","b")
)
ggplot(df, aes(y = 0, x = x, width = 1, height = 1, fill = group)) +
  geom_tile(size = NA)
#> Error in grid.Call.graphics(C_setviewport, vp, TRUE): non-finite location and/or size for viewport
```
<sup>Created on 2021-07-20 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v2.0.0)</sup>

I would expect behavior more like setting `color = NA`; i.e. geoms (or outlines of geoms) would not be drawn but the plot would still generate. I've tracked this down to *somewhere* in the guide generation code. If you turn the legend off, you get a plot:

``` r
ggplot(df, aes(y = 0, x = x, width = 1, height = 1, fill = group)) +
  geom_tile(size = NA, show.legend = FALSE)
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/xC2G4Vf.png)

Which is what I would expect. Similar problems occur in other geoms; e.g. `geom_point()`:

``` r
ggplot(df, aes(y = 0, x = x, color = group)) +
  geom_point(size = NA)
#> Warning: Removed 2 rows containing missing values (geom_point).
#> Error in grid.Call.graphics(C_setviewport, vp, TRUE): non-finite location and/or size for viewport
```

Here the warning is expected, but I think the error is not --- I would have expected output like what happens if you set `color = NA`; i.e. a blank plot:

``` r
ggplot(df, aes(y = 0, x = x, color = group)) +
  geom_point(color = NA)
#> Warning: Removed 2 rows containing missing values (geom_point).
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/TgvTkgg.png)

I believe the problem may be related to this line: https://github.com/tidyverse/ggplot2/blob/13c07309e5d6798277d5d0c6f76ead88b6112e40/R/guide-legend.r#L385

As when `size = NA` this will result in `key_size_mat` being all `NA`s, and then key widths and heights downstream end up all `NA`s. However I don't know enough about the surrounding code/context to suggest an appropriate solution.

Thanks!

title: drop=TRUE does not drop unused values (after recent update)
description:
Thank you for amazing packages. I am working on a series of reports, each report containing a different dataset and multiple plots, and I need colors to match between plots and reports. I am avoiding RColorBrewer (e.g. myColors <- brewer.pal(5,"Set1") ) because we have already published some of the first reports using other colours that we want to keep. 

This was my original good function:

scale_color_test <- function(...){
  ggplot2:::manual_scale(
    "color",
    values = setNames(c("grey50","gold", "blue2" ,"green3" ,  "red3"),
                      c("color_grey","color_gold","color_blue","color_green","color_red")),
    labels = setNames(c("color grey","color gold","color blue","color green","color red"),
                      c("color_grey","color_gold","color_blue","color_green","color_red")),
    drop=TRUE)
}

But this function recently stopped dropping unused values in the legends (exact same script run before and after a recent update).

Here is my reproducible example, and some of the things I have tried to fix this issue:

df.temp1<-data.frame(var1=factor(c("color_grey","color_gold","color_blue","color_green","color_red")),
                    var2=c(1,2,3,4,5),
                    var3=c(9,8,6,5,4),
                    var4=c("these colors","these colors","these colors","those colors","those colors"))

df.temp2<-data.frame(var1=factor(c("color_gold","color_blue","color_red")),
                    var2=c(2,3,5),
                    var3=c(8,6,4),
                    var4=c("these colors","these colors","those colors"))

# My old approach that used to work (second plot not dropping unused values in legend anymore):

scale_color_test <- function(...){
  ggplot2:::manual_scale(
    "color",
    values = setNames(c("grey50","gold", "blue2" ,"green3" ,  "red3"),
                      c("color_grey","color_gold","color_blue","color_green","color_red")),
    labels = setNames(c("color grey","color gold","color blue","color green","color red"),
                      c("color_grey","color_gold","color_blue","color_green","color_red")),
    drop=TRUE)
}

ggplot(df.temp1, aes(x=var2, y=var3,color=var1))+
  geom_point(shape=21,stroke=1,size=4)+
  scale_color_test()+
  facet_grid(rows = vars(var4))+
  theme_bw()
  
ggplot(df.temp2, aes(x=var2, y=var3,color=var1))+
  geom_point(shape=21,stroke=1,size=4)+
  scale_color_test()+
  facet_grid(rows = vars(var4))+
  ggtitle("This plot should have gold, blue and red")+
  theme_bw()

# Using scale_color_manual (drops, but colors not assigned to values):
## note: if I add setNames to values, then I am back to not droppping unused levels.
scale_color_test <- scale_color_manual(
    name = factor(c("color_grey","color_gold","color_blue","color_green","color_red")),
    values = c("grey50","gold", "blue2" ,"green3" ,  "red3"),
    labels = setNames(c("color grey","color gold","color blue","color green","color red"),
                      c("color_grey","color_gold","color_blue","color_green","color_red")),
      drop=TRUE)

ggplot(df.temp1, aes(x=var2, y=var3,color=var1))+
  geom_point(shape=21,stroke=1,size=4)+
  scale_color_test+
  facet_grid(rows = vars(var4))+
  theme_bw()

ggplot(df.temp2, aes(x=var2, y=var3,color=var1))+
  geom_point(shape=21,stroke=1,size=4)+
  scale_color_test+
  facet_grid(rows = vars(var4))+
  ggtitle("This plot should have gold, blue and red")+
  theme_bw()

# Then I tried creating a custom palette following this example:
## https://drsimonj.svbtle.com/creating-corporate-colour-palettes-for-ggplot2
## I simply don't know what pattern it follows, it is just not working as it should:

mycolors <- c(color_grey = "#7F7F7F", color_gold = "#FFD700", 
                           color_blue = "#0000EE", color_green = "#00CD00",
                           color_red = "#CD0000")

mypalette <- function(...) {
  cols <- c(...)
  if (is.null(cols))
    return (mycolors)
  mycolors[cols]
}

my_palettes <- list(
  `main`  = mypalette("color_grey","color_gold","color_blue","color_green","color_red"))


my_pal <- function(palette = "main", reverse = FALSE, ...) {
  pal <- my_palettes[[palette]]
  
  if (reverse) pal <- rev(pal)
  
  colorRampPalette(pal, ...)
}

scale_color_test <- function(palette = "main", discrete = TRUE, reverse = FALSE, ...) {
  pal <- my_pal(palette = palette, reverse = reverse)
  
  if (discrete) {
    discrete_scale("colour", paste0("my_", palette), palette = pal, ...)
  } else {
    scale_color_gradientn(colours = pal(256), ...)
  }
}

ggplot(df.temp1, aes(x=var2, y=var3,color=var1))+
  geom_point(shape=21,stroke=1,size=4)+
  scale_color_test(palette="main")+
  facet_grid(rows = vars(var4))+#scales = "free", space = "free"

title: X-axis placement with `facet_wrap(.., dir = "v", as.table = FALSE)`
description:
Hello there,

I was comparing the output of `facet_wrap()` with an extension thereof I'm trying to make, and I found that there is this one case when the placement of the x-axis is unexpected. In the first row of facets, I would have expected that in the 2nd and 3rd columns of panels, there would be no x-axes, because the bottom row already has these axes.
``` r
library(ggplot2)

ggplot(mpg, aes(displ, hwy)) +
  geom_point() +
  facet_wrap(vars(class), 
             dir = "v", as.table = FALSE)
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/yblqk2G.png)

<sup>Created on 2021-07-10 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v1.0.0)</sup>

I think I might have narrowed the scope of this glitch down to the lines below, but found it hard to figure out what exactly would need to change. I suspect that in the example above, `first_col` evaluates to 0, which might violate some assumptions later. Any other combination of the `dir` and `as.table` parameters don't have empty panels in the first column, as far as I know.

https://github.com/tidyverse/ggplot2/blob/acaa98e4cfcd922a737f35c16ec3dd6079aab3dc/R/facet-wrap.r#L315-L341

I don't think this crucial to fix, as this combination of parameters might not be widely used, but I thought the ggplot2 developers might like to know about this.

Thanks for reading!

title: Feature request: Plot pre-existing models with geom_smooth
description: **Background:** We can use `geom_smooth` to fit (e.g.) an `lm` to the data shown in a plot. However, it's often useful to show models that were fit on a different data set. For instance a model is fit on the training set but plotted on top of the evaluation set. To my knowledge, there is currently no concise way to do this in ggplot2. **Example:** Currently, the default solution seems to be: ```r library(tidyverse) set.seed(1) tibble( x = runif(20, 0, 10), y = 1 + 0.5 * x + rnorm(20, 0, 3)) -> d lm(y~x, slice(d, 1:10)) -> m slice(d, 11:20) %>% ggplot(aes(x,y)) + geom_point() + geom_abline( intercept = coef(m)[1], slope = coef(m)[2]) ``` **Proposal:** Allow users to pass a pre-existing model (`lm` or otherwise) to `geom_smooth` (e.g., `geom_smooth(model=m)`). Then `geom_smooth` uses the model's `predict` function to evaluate it for the x-range shown in the plot and displays the results. You can probably think of a better solution but I provide the proposal above for clarification and as a starting point for discussion.

title: `ggsave` returning filename string breaks unintended usage with `+`
description:
There previously was an unintended or undocumented usage of `ggsave()` where it could be added to a `ggplot()` using `+`. This depended on `ggsave()` returning `NULL`, which appears to have been changed in #3379 to where it now returns the filepath of the saved graphic. This matter is discussed some [here](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/68003633/error-cant-add-ggsave-to-a-ggplot-object) on StackOverflow and I thought I would mention it here since it appeared no one had yet. 

The #3379 discussion suggested some ambivalence about needing ggsave() to return filepaths, so to the extent that it is breaking some folks code I wondered if reverting might be worth consideration, even if this usage was not intended to begin with. From my experience the below code actually works and saves the image still, though it provides an error `Error: Can't add `ggsave(filename = "./blah.png")` to a ggplot object.`. Either breaking this functionality completely or reverting to it being OK despite being unorthodox seems like it would help clarify acceptable ways of using this function.

```r
library(ggplot2)

ggplot(iris, aes(x = Sepal.Length, y = Petal.Length)) +
  geom_point() +
  ggsave(filename = "./blah.png")
```

title: Unused levels persist in legends from version 3.3.4
description:
It appears a bug was introduced in version 3.3.4. When using `scale_fill_manual()`, unused levels persist in the legend. Here is some example data.

``` r
library(tidyverse)

set.seed(123)
dat <- tibble(var = paste("Group", 1:9),
              val = runif(9),
              grp = sample(LETTERS[1:4], 9, replace = TRUE))
```

When all levels are present, things work as expected:

``` r
dat %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = val, y = var)) +
  geom_col(aes(fill = grp)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("A" = "red", "B" = "blue", "C" = "orange",
                               "D" = "black"))
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/vxhItX1.png)

But when `grp = "C"` is no longer in the data, that value still persists in the legend.

``` r
dat %>%
  filter(grp != "C") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = val, y = var)) +
  geom_col(aes(fill = grp)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("A" = "red", "B" = "blue", "C" = "orange",
                               "D" = "black"))
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/UwQLbrZ.png)

From [this thread on StackOverflow](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/68278895/suppress-unused-fill-levels-in-ggplot2-legend), it appears that this worked as expected in version 3.3.3. I have tested version 3.3.4 and the development version from GitHub, and the unused level persists in the legend for both.

title: Use devEMF::emf instead of grDevices::win.metafile for .wmf/.emf
description:
Currently, `ggsave()` uses the `grDevices::win.metafil()` device for output to .wmf/.emf. This device doesn't seem to work very well—when I use it, the actual plot is rendered at half the size of the canvas in the upper left corner. Like this:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/4773225/124364003-a459d100-dc0c-11eb-8ba4-43b580ba90b0.png)

The `devEMF::emf()` device seems to work much better:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/4773225/124364014-ade33900-dc0c-11eb-8d94-9cca77699c7a.png)

I think it would be better to render wmf/emf files using the *devEMF* device. It would add a dependency (perhaps in Suggests with a warning or error to prompt installation?), but would be worth it for much better emf generation. If that would be acceptable, I can make a PR.

Example emf files for the two devices are attached.
[emf_output.zip](https://github.com/tidyverse/ggplot2/files/6758890/emf_output.zip)

Reprex:
``` r
library(ggplot2)
g <- ggplot(cars, aes(x = speed, y = dist)) +
  geom_point()
ggsave("grDevices.emf", g, height = 7, width = 7)
ggsave("devEMF.emf",    g, height = 7, width = 7,
       device = {\(filename, ...) devEMF::emf(file = filename, ...)})
```

title: stat_function that accepts different *functions* for each facet (or other aesthetics)
description: Would it be possible to add functionality to stat_function that accepts the function .f from the data.frame? That would allow the treatment of functions in the same way that other data are treated. Imagine a tibble in which each element of column 'function' is a different function (e.g., dnorm, dt, etc.). Ideally, stat_function would also allow arguments of the function to eb specified by other columns in the tibble (e.g., the tibble could have columns .1, .2, etc. for the first, second, etc. argument). title: values vector in scale_color_manual
description:
The behavior of `scale_color_manual(values = ...)` seems to have changed recently and broke many of my plots. 

Consider this example:

```R
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(ggplot2)
  library(dplyr)
})

color_map <- list(r = "red", g = "green", b = "blue")

randu %>%
  mutate(color_key = as.factor(if_else(x > y, "r", "g"))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = x, y = y, fill = color_key)) + 
  scale_fill_manual(values = color_map) +
  geom_point(shape = 21, size = 7)
```

It now produces a figure with the blue color _also_ in the legend. 
I find that the following works (blue does not appear in the legend):

```R
randu %>%
  mutate(color_key = as.factor(if_else(x > y, "r", "g"))) %>%
  {
    ggplot(., aes(x = x, y = y, fill = color_key)) + 
      scale_fill_manual(values = color_map, breaks = .$col) +
      # scale_fill_manual(values = color_map[.$col]) +  # Alternative
      geom_point(shape = 21, size = 7)
  }
```

But this code looks unhappy. Is there a more robust way, in particular without extra temporary variables?

Is there somethin like `breaks = .df$fill`? This would be useful in many contexts.


Sidenote. This would make more sense to me:
```R
scale_fill_manual(values = color_map)  # no blue in the legend
scale_fill_manual(values = color_map, breaks = names(color_map))  # with blue in the legend
```

==

For lols, this works, too:

```R
gglast <- function(what) {
  p <- ggplot2::last_plot()
  q <- p$mapping[[deparse(substitute(what))]]
  rlang::eval_tidy(q, data = p$data)

randu %>%

title: axis.text.y and "Vectorized input to `element_text()` is not officially supported" - is there any smart way to address it?
description:
Is there any way to achieve the effect presented on the screenshot, made with the instructions I show below - which triggers a warning?

**Description of the effect to achieve:**
There is a set of faceted Kaplan-Meier curves. The study sponsor wants each panel to have it's own risk table (it cannot be negotiated - the risk table must be shown there and not elsewhere).

                     labels = c("Resectable", "Unresectable", "0", "0.2", "0.4", "0.6", "0.8", "1"),

title: Odd behavior when grouping values for geom_ribbon
description:
I've accidentally discovered some odd behavior with grouping variables with geom_ribbon.  

I am graphing regression outputs, where the value of y varies based on two different factor variables.  I'm visualizing these effects with lines, using a `color` aesthetic for one variable (`var1`), and a `linetype` aesthetic for the other variable (`var2`).  

I also have error bands that I am visualizing with `geom_ribbon`, and I want these error bands to be colored by `var1`, but have a separate error band for both `var1` and `var2`.

The problem is, only adding a `fill` aesthetic for `var1` makes a bad graph.  So I added a `group` aesthetic corresponding to `var2`, except I made a typo and only wrote "`grou`".  This somehow worked and only threw a warning.  But then, when I fixed the typo, it failed with an "Aesthetics can not vary with a ribbon" error!

I guess since the code works with a typo, this isnt an issue for me, but I figured it was something you all should know about!

I have ggplot 3.3.2.  Below should be a suitable reprex.

```r
library(tidyverse)

df <- expand.grid(var1=c("A", "B", "C"), var2=c("a", "b", "c"), x=seq(1, 100))

df <- df %>%
  mutate(y = x*case_when(var1 == 'A' ~ 1,
                        var1 == 'B' ~ 2,
                        var1 == 'C' ~ 3) + 
             x*case_when(var2 == 'a' ~ 10,
                        var2 == 'b' ~ 20,
                        var2 == 'c' ~ 30),
         ymax = y + y*0.01,
         ymin = y - y*0.01)

#This makes a bad ribbon
ggplot(df) + 
  geom_line(aes(x=x, y=y, color=var1, linetype=var2)) + 
  geom_ribbon(aes(x=x, ymin=ymin, ymax=ymax, fill=var1), alpha=0.2)

#This fails with "Error: Aesthetics can not vary with a ribbon"
ggplot(df) + 
  geom_line(aes(x=x, y=y, color=var1, linetype=var2)) + 
  geom_ribbon(aes(x=x, ymin=ymin, ymax=ymax, fill=var1, group=var2), alpha=0.2)

#This works (!?), but gives a warning for unknown aesthetic 'grou'
ggplot(df) + 
  geom_line(aes(x=x, y=y, color=var1, linetype=var2)) + 
  geom_ribbon(aes(x=x, ymin=ymin, ymax=ymax, fill=var1, grou=var2), alpha=0.2)

```

title: scale_*_steps (presumably binned_scales) doesn't like 0.01 with trans="log10"
description:
I would like to bin my colors using a log10 transformation, and it seems that if the number 0.01 is included in the data, the scaling breaks with a warning:
```
Warning message:
In self$trans$transform(limits) : NaNs produced
```
This causes the transformation to happen, but the legend doesn't show up.

Here is an example of what doesn't work:
```r
ggplot(data = data.frame(x = 1:5, 
                         y = c(0.01, 0.43, 0.46,
                               0.05, 0.17))) +
  geom_point(aes(x = x, y = y, color = y)) +
  scale_color_steps(trans = "log10")
```

Here are 3 examples that do work, which makes me suspect it is a bug:

```r
ggplot(data = data.frame(x = 1:5, 
                         y = c(0.0101, 0.43, 0.46,
                               0.05, 0.17))) +
  geom_point(aes(x = x, y = y, color = y)) +
  scale_color_steps(trans = "log10") 

ggplot(data = data.frame(x = 1:5, 
                         y = c(0.00999, 0.43, 0.46,
                               0.05, 0.17))) +
  geom_point(aes(x = x, y = y, color = y)) +
  scale_color_steps(trans = "log10")

ggplot(data = data.frame(x = 1:6, 
                         y = c(0.01, 0.43, 0.46,
                               0.05, 0.17, 0.09))) +
  geom_point(aes(x = x, y = y, color = y)) +
  scale_color_steps()
```
I can speculate on why this is happening, but I'm unclear if there's an easy way to eliminate this problem. 

One fix is to use "log1p" instead of "log10". It took awhile for me to pinpoint the issue and discover the solution. Even if a fix for 0.01 can't be included, it would be helpful to add some language in the binned_scale (or scale_*_steps) documentation.

title: empty plot with secondary axis fails
description:
Hi,

I randomly encountered a bug while working with the ggplot package. I was trying to create an empty plot with secondary (so other functions in my package can fill it up later). However, adding the secondary axis to an empty ggplot object throws an error if the object is called.

E.g.,:
```r
plot <- ggplot2::ggplot() 
plot <- plot + ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(
  name = "ylab", limits = c(0, 1), 
  sec.axis = ggplot2::sec_axis(~ ., name = "ylab2", breaks = c(0, 1), labels = c(0, 2)))
```
which throws this error when calling ``plot``
> Error in seq.default(range[1], range[2], length.out = self$detail) :
