description:
### Summary of issue

An example similar to `p2` is used in the {ggformula} package but is now breaking.  It appears that when rendering the plot, `as_string(as_name())` fails on the geometry aesthetic when it has the form `data$variable`.  Simply storing the variable as a vector "solves" the problem; see `p1`.

Is this a bug or an intended change in behavior?

### ggplot2 examples

``` r
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(ggplot2))
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(sf))
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(ggformula))
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(dplyr))
MI <- sf::st_as_sf(maps::map("county", "michigan", plot = FALSE, fill = TRUE))
MIgeom <- MI$geom

# this works
p1 <- 
  ggplot(ggformula::MIpop %>% arrange(county)) + 
  geom_sf(aes(fill = log10(population), geometry = MIgeom), color = "white") 
p1
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/DM62EAS.png)

``` r

# this fails
p2 <- 
  ggplot(ggformula::MIpop %>% arrange(county)) + 
  geom_sf(aes(fill = log10(population), geometry = MI$geometry), color = "white") 
p2
#> Error: Can't convert a call to a string
```

### ggformula examples

For completeness, here are the {ggformula} examples that led to this.  I see that these are not quite identical (although the same issues arise).  See the geometry aesthetics displayed near the end.

```{r}
p3 <- gf_sf(
  data = MIpop %>% dplyr::arrange(county),
  fill = ~ log10(population), 
  geometry = ~ MIgeom, color = "white")
p3
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/IIHYkQo.png)

``` r
p4 <- gf_sf(
  data = MIpop %>% dplyr::arrange(county),
  fill = ~ log10(population), 
  geometry = ~ MI$geom, color = "white")
p4
#> Error: Can't convert a call to a string
```

``` r
p1$mapping
#> Aesthetic mapping: 
#> <empty>
p2$mapping
#> Aesthetic mapping: 
#> <empty>
p3$mapping
#> Aesthetic mapping: 
#> * `fill`     -> `log10(population)`
#> * `geometry` -> `MIgeom`
p4$mapping
#> Aesthetic mapping: 
#> * `fill`     -> `log10(population)`
#> * `geometry` -> `MI$geom`

rlang::as_string(rlang::as_name(p3$mapping$geometry))
#> [1] "MIgeom"
rlang::as_string(rlang::as_name(p4$mapping$geometry))
#> Error: Can't convert a call to a string
```

title: Feature request: Combined colour and fill aesthetic mapping
description:
**tl;dr** Would it be possible to add a convenience `colfill` aesthetic that controls both the colour and fill scales simultaneously?

I often find that I am mapping colour and fill scales to the exact same values (variables). When using the default **ggplot2** colour palettes and assuming no other scale transformations, this involves only a little extra typing.

``` r
library(ggplot2)

ggplot(diamonds, aes(depth, col = cut, fill = cut)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.3)
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/zDqSH22.png)

However, as soon as one ventures beyond the defaults, then you end up having to write out quite a lot of duplicate text which is only distinguished by the "col(our)" or "fill" prefixes. 

``` r
ggplot(diamonds, aes(depth, col = cut, fill = cut)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.3) +
  scale_colour_brewer(palette = 'Set2', name = 'Diamond Cut') +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = 'Set2', name = 'Diamond Cut')
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/DuOxFl5.png)

While the above example is somewhat contrived, it's easy to think of real-life cases that would involve even more duplication. For example, if specifying custom breaks and labels, and/or a manual scale.

One potential solution would be to add a combined "colfill" aesthetic that jointly controls both colour and fill scales. Something like:

``` r
ggplot(diamonds, aes(depth, colfill = cut)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.3) +
  scale_colfill_brewer(palette = 'Set2', name = 'Diamond Cut') 
```

Does that seem feasible or useful?

title: Feature request: quantiles based on observations instead of density estimates with geom_violin
description:
geom_violin uses density estimate to plot quantiles, which doesn't align with box plot.

This has already been asked and is document: [https://stackoverflow.com/questions/36033341/differing-quantiles-boxplot-vs-violinplot](url)
issue: #2088

I think it would be useful to have an optional parameter to choose quantiles computed based on actual observations instead of density estimates. violin plots are useful to see rough distribution of the data but quantiles of actual observations also matter. Therefore, I think it would be great to have such an option without breaking existing behaviour.

PS: reprex didn't work for me but here is a simple reproducible code.
```r
library(ggplot2)
set.seed(5)
type1 = rnorm(n = 20, mean = 5)
type2 = c(10, 9, 9, 9, 9, 7, 7, 6, 5, 4, 1)
type3 = c(rnorm(n = 10, mean = 2.5), rnorm(n = 10, mean = 7.5, sd = 0.5))

#median(example1)
#median(example2)

df = data.frame(type = c(rep("Type 1", length(type1)), rep("Type 2", length(type2)), rep("Type 3", length(type3))), 
				val = c(type1, type2, type3))

ggplot(df, aes(x = type, y = val)) + theme_classic() + 
	geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.5) + 
	geom_violin(scale = "area", alpha = 0.5, draw_quantiles = c(0.25, 0.5, 0.75)) +
	geom_dotplot(binaxis = "y", stackdir = "center", alpha = 0.3, dotsize = 0.4)
```

title: Suppress multiple warnings in tests in response to the testthat's new behaviour

At minimum, probably we should place `suppressWarnings()` here and there...

title: Option to turn strip clipping off
description:
Hi everyone,

I recently found the need to turn the clipping off, but I can't easily do that without either (1) writing a new facet function that builds strips as I want or (2) edit the strips in the gtable.

I found a similar question [here on so](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/49740215/ggplot-facet-grid-label-cut-off/49744051#49744051).
A while back, there was a move to make clipping more configurable (#2536), but this has not been extended to strips. Also there was an issue with strip clipping (#2772), which turned it on for all strips; however my intention would be to make this configurable from e.g. the theme.

One reason besides turning off label clipping is to make the strips flush with either axis lines, panel backgrounds and panel borders (the latter two when the coord clipping is turned off).

An example of the behaviour I love to see configurable is below. The intersection between the strip and the axis line is not ideal, and the `size` parameter appears halved for the strip.

``` r
library(ggplot2)

ggplot(mpg, aes(displ, hwy)) +
  geom_point() +
  facet_wrap(~ drv) +
  theme(
    strip.background = element_rect(colour = "red", size = 5),
    axis.line.y.left = element_line(colour = "blue", size = 5)
  )
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/96k25Fk.png)

Thanks for considering!

title: stat_density_2d() and geom_density_2d() output differs between ggplot2 v. 3.2.1 and v. 3.3.2
description:
Some changes introduced between ggplot2 version 3.2.1 and version 3.3.2 (I did not check version 3.3.0, but I reckon it has the same problem) have lead to weird outputs when using stat_density_2d() and geom_density_2d().

I have asked this question before (https://github.com/tidyverse/ggplot2/issues/4110), but I have been asked to provide a standard reprex using the reprex package. Here I report a standard reprex, that allows reproducing this issue.

My questions are:
1) Are the differences in output between ggplot2 v. 3.2.1 and v. 3.3.2 when using `stat_density_2d(aes(fill = stat(nlevel)), geom = "polygon")` or `geom_density_2d(aes(colour = cut))` intended? Or is this a bug?
2) If they are intended: Is there a way to generate a figure using v. 3.3.2 that is similar to what v. 3.2.1 produced when using `stat_density_2d(aes(fill = stat(nlevel)), geom = "polygon")`? For more details see the reprex below.

title: stat_density2d computes bins on entire data, not on groups
description:
This is kind of a follow up from issue #4003 

When using bins argument, the bins seem to be calculated on the entire data, but not on the groups as defined per aes. I am not sure that this is what one expects when using this argument. 

The below example shows this on the iris dataset, with bins = 5. - not showing 5 bins for each group. But I guess it calculates 5 bins for the absolute density values for the whole data. I am not sure if this is very helpful, because one does not get a real idea which bin is shown and also it is difficult to compare the groups. 

I believe it would make more sense if bins would be calculated by group, because I guess one wants to compare probability distributions rather than absolute densities (?). The second plot shows what I believe one would rather expect when using `bins`. The function to calculate is ([modified function from this SO answer](https://stackoverflow.com/a/59173290/7941188))
``` r
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

ggplot(iris, aes(Sepal.Length, Sepal.Width, color = Species)) +
  geom_density2d(bins = 5) +
  geom_point()
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/Clv2ZIi.png)

The following is more what one would expect (at least I would do so). For the generation of `man_calc_dens` data frame, see below. 

``` r
ggplot(mapping = aes(color = Species)) +
  geom_point(data = iris, aes(Sepal.Length, Sepal.Width, )) +
  geom_polygon(data = man_calc_dens, aes(x = x, y = y, group = interaction(Species, prob)), fill = NA) 
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/4OJG3m5.png)

**functions and manually calculated density**

```
probc <- function(data, x = NULL, y = NULL, n = 50, prob = 0.95, ...) {
  
  post1 <- MASS::kde2d(data[[x]], data[[y]], n = n, ...)
  
  dx <- diff(post1$x[1:2])
  dy <- diff(post1$y[1:2])
  sz <- sort(post1$z)
  c1 <- cumsum(sz) * dx * dy
  
  levels <- sapply(prob, function(x) {
    approx(c1, sz, xout = 1 - x)$y
  })
  
  df <- as.data.frame(grDevices::contourLines(post1$x, post1$y, post1$z, levels = levels))
  df$x <- round(as.numeric(df$x), 3)
  df$y <- round(as.numeric(df$y), 3)
  df$level <- round(as.numeric(df$level), 2)
  df$prob <- rep(as.character(prob), nrow(df))
  
  
  df
}

man_calc_dens <- 
  iris %>% 
  split(., .$Species) %>%
  
  purrr::map(., .f = function(u) {dplyr::bind_rows(
  purrr::map(seq(0.2, 0.8, 0.2), function(p) 
    probc(data = u, x = "Sepal.Length", y = "Sepal.Width", prob = p))
  )}
) %>% 
  bind_rows(.id = "Species")
```

title: No warning in stat_ydensity when dropping groups
description:
Hi,

I noticed the following behavior in `geom_violin` when there are fewer than three data points in a given violin. In this scenario, one of the violins gets dropped without a warning. 

``` r

library(ggplot2)
table(mtcars$cyl, mtcars$am)
#>    
#>      0  1
#>   4  3  8
#>   6  4  3
#>   8 12  2
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = factor(cyl), y = mpg)) + 
  geom_violin(scale = "width", aes(fill = factor(am))) 
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/ocdl3XP.png)

<sup>Created on 2020-07-01 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v0.3.0)</sup>

It seems a related issue was addressed in `stat_density` in https://github.com/tidyverse/ggplot2/pull/2142 . I would propose that `stat_ydensity` be updated similarly here https://github.com/tidyverse/ggplot2/blob/cb0cfd2aea18ee4ebf671bed52dbd566ebeaf7ea/R/stat-ydensity.r#L74  Happy to put together a small PR for this if people agree.

title: stat_density_2d() and geom_density_2d() appear bugged/produce weird output
description:
Some changes introduced between ggplot2 version 3.2.1 and version 3.3.1 (I did not check version 3.3.0, but I reckon it has the same problem) have lead to weird outputs when using `stat_density_2d()` and `geom_density_2d()`.

Here a minimum reproducible example:
1) Dataset:
[problem.df.RData.zip](https://github.com/tidyverse/ggplot2/files/4858590/problem.df.RData.zip)

2) Code:
```
# #Load ggplot2
library(ggplot2)

# #Load dataset
# setwd(readClipboard())
# save(problem.df, file = "problem.df.RData.zip")
load(file = "problem.df.RData.zip")

# #Recreate problem
problem.facet <- ggplot(data = problem.df, aes(X, Y))
problem.facet <- problem.facet + geom_point(color = "lightgray", alpha = 0.1)
# #If we use geom_density_2d we already see a difference between different ggplot2 versions
problem.facet + geom_density_2d(aes(colour = Facet.Groups)) + facet_grid(. ~ Facet.Groups)

# #If we use stat_density_2d() different ggplot2 versions result in different plots which look even weirder
problem.facet <- problem.facet + stat_density_2d(aes(fill = stat(nlevel)), geom = "polygon") +
  facet_grid(. ~ Facet.Groups) + scale_fill_viridis_c()
problem.facet
# #Check the differences in "Group3", "Group4", and the "NA" column
# #Based on visual inspection of the data (see also the geom_density_2d() plot) the behavior of
# #ggplot2 version 3.2.1 should be the correct one
```


Using the same dataset and the same code, ggplot2 version 3.2.1 produces the following two figures:
[ggplot2_321_geom_density_2d.pdf](https://github.com/tidyverse/ggplot2/files/4858600/ggplot2_321_geom_density_2d.pdf)
[ggplot2_321_stat_density_2d.pdf](https://github.com/tidyverse/ggplot2/files/4858601/ggplot2_321_stat_density_2d.pdf)


Using the same dataset and the same code, ggplot2 version 3.3.1 produces the following two figures:
[ggplot2_331_geom_density_2d.pdf](https://github.com/tidyverse/ggplot2/files/4858607/ggplot2_331_geom_density_2d.pdf)
[ggplot2_331_stat_density_2d.pdf](https://github.com/tidyverse/ggplot2/files/4858608/ggplot2_331_stat_density_2d.pdf)

Using the same dataset and the same code, ggplot2 version 3.3.2 produces the following two figures:
[ggplot2_332_geom_density_2d.pdf](https://github.com/tidyverse/ggplot2/files/4858610/ggplot2_332_geom_density_2d.pdf)
[ggplot2_332_stat_density_2d.pdf](https://github.com/tidyverse/ggplot2/files/4858611/ggplot2_332_stat_density_2d.pdf)

Notice, how weird the colouring/breaks in the newer ggplot2 versions look like ("Group3", "Group4", and "NA" column). Also note, that the left lower peak in "Group4" appears to have disappeared in the newer ggplot2 versions using `stat_density_2d()` (it is still visible, however, if we use `geom_density_2d()`). Since the issue appears in both version 3.3.1 and 3.3.2, it is probably not connected to these (solved) problems (?):
https://github.com/tidyverse/ggplot2/pull/3976
https://github.com/tidyverse/ggplot2/issues/4004

Is this intended behaviour? To me the output looks like either the result of changed defaults (I know, that version 3.3.0 changed quite a bit here relative to version 3.2.1) or a bug.

title: Connecting points jittered by position_jitterdodge
description:
Hello,
I am attempting to combine boxplots and points, and connect points together. There are some old discussions saying that the input data needs to be sorted to ensure that geom_line and geom_point receive the same jittering, but this does not seem to work when there is a nested grouping:

```r
library(tidyverse)
set.seed(77)
a1 <- tibble(ID=factor(letters[1:10]), y=runif(10), TP="A", Grp=rep(c("C","P"), 5))
a2 <- tibble(ID=factor(letters[1:10]), y=runif(10), TP="B", Grp=rep(c("C","P"), 5))
a1 <- bind_rows(a1, a2)
a1 <- mutate(a1, TP=factor(TP), Grp=factor(Grp))
a1 <- arrange(a1, ID, TP)

pj <- position_jitter(width=0.2, seed=9)
ggplot(a1, aes(x=TP, y=y, fill=Grp)) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha=0.2, outlier.colour = NA) +
  geom_point(position=pj, aes(colour=Grp, group=ID)) +
  geom_line(position=pj, aes(group = ID, colour=Grp))
```
![p1](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/780449/86237911-f58d4a00-bbdf-11ea-87ba-0e2997648c06.png)

This is performing as expected. However the jittering is not separated per group (i.e pink points are not lined up with the pink boxplot). Lets use jitterdodge to achieve that.

```r
pj <- position_jitterdodge(jitter.width=0.4, seed=9)
ggplot(a1, aes(x=TP, y=y, fill=Grp)) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha=0.2, outlier.colour = NA) +
  geom_point(position=pj, aes(colour=Grp, group=Grp))
```
![p2](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/780449/86238287-954ad800-bbe0-11ea-9e63-f52370f53cfe.png)

Now the colours are lined up, attempt to connect together.

```r
ggplot(a1, aes(x=TP, y=y, fill=Grp)) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha=0.2, outlier.colour = NA) +
  geom_point(position=pj, aes(colour=Grp, group=Grp)) +
  geom_line(position=pj, aes(group = ID, colour=Grp), alpha=0.3)
```
![p3](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/780449/86238458-df33be00-bbe0-11ea-8f8e-03e4d3a5f134.png)

As far as I can tell, none of the following combinations of sorting the input data fix the problem of lines being connected to the points:

```r
a1 <- arrange(a1, ID, TP, Grp)
a1 <- arrange(a1, ID, Grp, TP)
a1 <- arrange(a1, Grp, ID, TP)
a1 <- arrange(a1, Grp, TP, ID)
a1 <- arrange(a1, TP, ID, Grp)
a1 <- arrange(a1, TP, Grp, ID)

```

title: ggplot2 does not use globally set palette when using indices for colors
description:
May be completely intentional, but I was wondering about the following behaviour: 

ggplot2 doesn't change the default palette when setting it with `palette()`. 

It's also not really a big issue, and I personally would probably rather not use indices for colors, [but some people seem to](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/62665407/single-integer-color-input-what-color-space-how-to-enter-greyscale/62665969#62665969).
``` r
library(ggplot2)

palette()
#> [1] "black"   "#DF536B" "#61D04F" "#2297E6" "#28E2E5" "#CD0BBC" "#F5C710"
#> [8] "gray62"
plot(1:8, col = 1:8, pch = 16)
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/zCCOogB.png)

``` r
#change the palette to "Reds"
palette(RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(8, "Reds"))
plot(1:8, col = 1:8, pch = 16)
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/iQRHZ5t.png)

``` r

  geom_point() +
  scale_color_identity()
```

title: Allowing guide_colorbar to draw guides with custom aesthetics.
description:
This is more of a feature request than an issue and is related to [#2345](https://github.com/tidyverse/ggplot2/issues/2345). Currently `guide_colorbar()` defines `available_aes = c("colour", "color", "fill")`. This restricts the drawing of a guide to these aesthetics when using a continuous color scale. @clauswilke first noting this issue in reference to `ggridges`. For example with the definition `scale_point_fill_gradient`, no color bar guide is drawn because `scale_point_color_gradient` defaults to `guide = "none"`.


```r
library(ggplot2)
library(ggridges)
ggplot(iris, aes(x = Sepal.Length, y = Species)) +
  geom_density_ridges(
    aes(point_color = Sepal.Width, point_shape = Species),
    alpha = .2, point_alpha = 1, jittered_points = TRUE
  ) +
  scale_point_color_gradient(low = "#FF0000", high = "#0000FF")
```
![NoGuideggriges](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/30324172/86160371-a8bf4b80-bad9-11ea-90cf-ce1fbbeadc1e.png)

If we set `guide = "colorbar"` we get an error.

```r
ggplot(iris, aes(x = Sepal.Length, y = Species)) +
  geom_density_ridges(
    aes(point_color = Sepal.Width, point_shape = Species),
    alpha = .2, point_alpha = 1, jittered_points = TRUE
  ) +
  scale_point_color_gradient(low = "#FF0000", high = "#0000FF", guide = "colorbar")

#Error: Guide 'colorbar' cannot be used for 'point_colour'
```
However if the following lines of code were changed in `ggplot2`

![Screen Shot 2020-06-30 at 1 57 01 PM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/30324172/86160444-c1c7fc80-bad9-11ea-8e95-5069c88d7e6f.png)

Then `guide = "colorbar"` works as you would expect

```r
ggplot(iris, aes(x = Sepal.Length, y = Species)) +
  geom_density_ridges(
    aes(point_color = Sepal.Width, point_shape = Species),
    alpha = .2, point_alpha = 1, jittered_points = TRUE
  ) +
  scale_point_color_gradient(low = "#FF0000", high = "#0000FF", guide = "colorbar")
```

![Guideggriges](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/30324172/86161636-88908c00-badb-11ea-8eb1-3ee414bfdd4e.png)


The two lines of code that were modified was in `guide-colorbar.r` and `guides-.r`, each within `guide_train.colorbar` and `guide_train` functions respectively. The condition would depend on a partial match of the predefined `required_aes = c("color", "colour", "fill")`, so as long as the developer's custom aesthetics contains either `color`, `colour` or `fill`, then the guide is drawn.

title: Accept tidyverse tilde functions
description:
It would be neat to be able to use the same "short" version of defining function as in `purrr` in `ggplot2` as well.

---

Example would be to be able to write:

```r
ggplot(mtcars, aes(drat, qsec)) + 
  geom_line() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = ~format(., nsmall = 1))
```

Today you need to do like this:

```r
ggplot(mtcars, aes(drat, qsec)) + 
  geom_line() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = function(x) format(x, nsmall = 1))
```

Thanks! :)

title: Can we deprecate guides(... = FALSE)?
description:
I happened to know `guides()` accepts `FALSE` as an option not to show the legend. e.g https://stackoverflow.com/a/14604540

``` r
p + guides(colour = FALSE)
```

I think none of the official documentation refers to this usage, and no test is broken if I remove this `isFALSE(guide)`, so I think this is safe to remove. At least we should start encouraging people to use `"none"` as it is the supposed way. The only concern is that I cannot understand what this comment exactly means.... This has been here for 9 years since the point where the S3 guide system was born (https://github.com/tidyverse/ggplot2/commit/0795c6f1e3f3d4d3b9afc0aaea176d3e7a24a7f0)...

title: Feature request: Extended palettes for brewer scales
description:
I think it would be great to allow an easy extension of the brewer palettes to "more colors" especially for the new binned scales. 

1. The palettes look great
1. They are commonly used and recognised
1. The bins in sequential data may frequently exceed the maximum colors given by the original palettes.

Below one suggestion how this could look like. This is also part of [this thread on Stackoverflow.](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/62543112/how-to-make-discrete-gradient-color-bar-with-geom-contour-filled/62571158#62571158) I have added a warning in order to make the user aware of the "breach" of the original palette.

There may be this option out there already? Note that a gradient creating function such as `colourspace::scale_fill_continuous_sequential` does not work in this example, because it does not result in a binned scale. 


I'd also be happy to create a pull request for this one, if the package maintainer should like this concept :)

``` r
library(ggplot2)

ggplot(mtcars, aes(mpg, disp, fill = hp)) +
  geom_point(shape = 21) +
  scale_fill_craftfermenter(
    breaks = seq(0,520,40),
    limits = c(0,520),
    palette = "Spectral",
    guide=  guide_colorsteps(even.steps = FALSE, # workaround for issues #4019/#4100
                             barheight = 15) 
  )
#> Warning: 13 colours used, but Spectral has only 11 - New palette created based
#> on all colors of Spectral
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/TxsPfuj.png)

<sup>Created on 2020-06-28 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v0.3.0)</sup>

**The modified functions**
```r
# modified brewer_pal()
craftbrewer_pal <- function (type = "seq", palette = 1, direction = 1) {
  pal <- scales:::pal_name(palette, type)
  force(direction)
  function(n) {
    n_max_palette <- RColorBrewer:::maxcolors[names(RColorBrewer:::maxcolors) == palette]
    
    if (n < 3) {
      pal <- suppressWarnings(RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(n, pal))
    } else if (n > n_max_palette){
      rlang::warn(paste(n, "colours used, but", palette, "has only",
                        n_max_palette, "- New palette created based on all colors of", 
                        palette))
      n_palette <- RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(n_max_palette, palette)
      colfunc <- grDevices::colorRampPalette(n_palette)
      pal <- colfunc(n)
    }
    else {
      pal <- RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(n, pal)
    }
    pal <- pal[seq_len(n)]
    if (direction == -1) {
      pal <- rev(pal)
    }
    pal
  }
}

# modified scale_fill_fermenter

scale_fill_craftfermenter <- function(..., type = "seq", palette = 1, direction = -1, na.value = "grey50", guide = "coloursteps", aesthetics = "fill") {
  type <- match.arg(type, c("seq", "div", "qual"))
  if (type == "qual") {
    warn("Using a discrete colour palette in a binned scale.\n  Consider using type = \"seq\" or type = \"div\" instead")
  }
  ggplot2:::binned_scale(aesthetics, "craftfermenter", ggplot2:::binned_pal(craftbrewer_pal(type, palette, direction)), na.value = na.value, guide = guide, ...)
}
```

title: Nothing plotted with manual_scale when a named vector is used as the input.
description:
When building a manual_scale ggplot shows no data when the number of colours <= the number in the scale when a named vector is used. Strangely the colours work when the number of colours > the number in the scale. This seems to be fixed by using an unnamed vector.

``` r
library(dplyr)
#> 
#> Attaching package: 'dplyr'
#> The following objects are masked from 'package:stats':
#> 
#>     filter, lag
#> The following objects are masked from 'package:base':
#> 
#>     intersect, setdiff, setequal, union
library(scales)
library(ggplot2)
library(tibble)


named_vec <- c("teracota" = "#d18975", 
                 "green" = "#8fd175",
                 "purple" = "#3f2d54")

scale_colour_named <- function(...)
{ discrete_scale("colour", "test_pal",
                 manual_pal(named_vec)) }

scale_colour_unnamed <- function(...)
{ discrete_scale("colour", "test_pal",
                 manual_pal(unname(named_vec))) }


  #Works when n > than pallet
USArrests %>%
  rownames_to_column("State") %>%
  slice(1:4) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = State, y = Murder, col = State)) +
  geom_point(size = 10, show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_colour_named()
#> Warning: This manual palette can handle a maximum of 3 values. You have supplied
#> 4.
#> Warning: Removed 1 rows containing missing values (geom_point).
```

``` r
USArrests %>%
```

title: Cannot override.aes with guide_bins?
description:
Controlling the appearance of the geoms within a scale_size_binned legend using `guide_bins()` doesn't seem to operate in the same fashion as `guide_legend()` - or rather, there appears to be no overriding the `aes()` despite the documentation implying no difference. 

To illustrate, this:

```r
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = drat, y = wt, size = hp, fill = cyl)) + 
geom_point(shape = 21) + 
scale_size_binned(guide = guide_legend(override.aes = list(colour = "red", shape = 21, fill = "blue")))
```
...works as expected, while this:

```r
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = drat, y = wt, size = hp, fill = cyl)) + 
geom_point(shape = 21) + 
scale_size_binned(guide = guide_bins(override.aes = list(colour = "red", shape = 21, fill = "blue")))
```
...does not.

title: Combined facet labels aren't parsed when .multi_line = FALSE
description:
(previously: https://github.com/tidyverse/ggplot2/pull/4032#issuecomment-643531350)

Facet labels that are combined with `.multi_line = FALSE` don't show up as parsed when using `label_parsed`:

``` r
library("ggplot2")

dat <- data.frame(x = 1, y = 1, a = "a", b = 1)

ggplot(dat, aes(x, y)) +
  geom_point() +
  facet_grid(
    ~ a + b,
    labeller = labeller(
      a = c("a" = "a^2"),
      .default = label_parsed,
      .multi_line = FALSE
    )
  )
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/wvYpdlF.png)

<sup>Created on 2020-06-22 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v0.3.0)</sup>

Compare to `.multi_line = TRUE`, which looks as it should:

``` r
ggplot(dat, aes(x, y)) +
  geom_point() +
  facet_grid(
    ~ a + b,
    labeller = labeller(
      a = c("a" = "a^2"),
      .default = label_parsed,
      .multi_line = TRUE
    )
  )
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/5BBVBTM.png)

One issue is the `.multi_line` argument doesn't get passed along here: https://github.com/tidyverse/ggplot2/blob/7d05fa3b6cda40fe645fe04090485275a0666979/R/labeller.r#L440

However changing that line alone makes things worse:

``` r
ggplot(dat, aes(x, y)) +
  geom_point() +
  facet_grid(
    ~ a + b,
    labeller = labeller(
      a = c("a" = "a^2"),
      .default = label_parsed,
      .multi_line = FALSE
    )
  )
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/ZNsdETD.png)

title: Unexpected warning about missing values when setting xlim and ylim

``` r
library(ggplot2)
packageVersion("ggplot2")

ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = mpg)) +
```

title: coord_proj is throwing a "Not implemented error"
description:
Below is some simplified code to plot a world map using ggplot2. This code was working fine for me until April, at which point I started getting `Error: not implemented`. Line by line testing links this outcome to the `coord_proj()` line. There was some discussion of this on [stackoverflow](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/61104707/why-does-coord-proj-and-ggplot2-give-me-this-error), but no definitive solution was found. Reproducible example and error messages below.

```r
world <- ggplot2::map_data("world")
world <- world[world$region != "Antarctica",]
gg <- ggplot()
gg <- gg + geom_cartogram(data=world, map=world,
                          aes(x=long, y=lat, map_id=region))
gg <- gg + coord_proj("+proj=wintri")
gg
```

Error messages:
```
Error: Not implemented
Run `rlang::last_error()` to see where the error occurred.
> rlang::last_error()
<error/rlang_error>
Not implemented
Backtrace:
  1. (function (x, ...) ...
  2. ggplot2:::print.ggplot(x)
  4. ggplot2:::ggplot_gtable.ggplot_built(data)
  5. base::Map(...)
  6. base::mapply(FUN = f, ..., SIMPLIFY = FALSE)
  8. l$draw_geom(d, layout)
  9. ggplot2:::f(..., self = self)
 10. self$geom$draw_layer(data, self$geom_params, layout, layout$coord)
 11. ggplot2:::f(..., self = self)
 12. base::lapply(...)
 13. ggplot2:::FUN(X[[i]], ...)
 16. ggalt:::f(...)
 17. ggplot2::coord_munch(coord, map, panel_scales)
 18. coord$backtransform_range(range)
 19. ggplot2:::f(..., self = self)
Run `rlang::last_trace()` to see the full context.
```

title: `coord_polar` causes error with `ggtext::element_markdown`
description:
Originally reported as a [`ggtext` issue here](https://github.com/wilkelab/ggtext/issues/42) I was advised by @clauswilke  to flag this here as well.

Using `coord_polar` with `ggtext::element_markdown` to theme x-axis labels causes an error 

> Error in grid.Call.graphics(C_setviewport, vp, TRUE) :
  non-finite location and/or size for viewport

with the plot still drawn correctly.

----

A minimal & reproducible example:

```r
df <- data.frame(name = sprintf("**%s**", LETTERS[1:4]), value = 1:4)

library(ggplot2)
library(ggtext)

ggplot(df, aes(name, value)) +
    geom_point() +
    coord_polar() +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_markdown())
```

Removing `coord_polar` gets rid of the error.

title: undefined columns selected with groupS aes in custom geom
description:
Hi again. I'm the maintainer of directlabels::geom_dl and I'm trying to figure out a way to let the user optionally specify a grouping variable to use, and to detect when the user specifies that in my draw_panel method. Originally I was trying to use aes(group) for this purpose but that does not work, see #4070.

Now I am considering using another aes for this purpose, like aes(groupS), but I'm observing the following error:
```
Error in `[.data.frame`(data, "group") : undefined columns selected
```
I expected that I could use any custom aes, but this one is not working.

This happens because of a bug in grouping.r, which currently tests for absence of group column via
```
  if (is.null(data$group)) {
```
however that test will not work if there is another column/aes (like groupS) that starts with group. The fix is to change it to 
```
  if (is.null(data[["group"]])) {
```
Here is a reprex using a standard ggplot2 geom 
```
library(ggplot2)
ggplot()+
  geom_point(aes(
    Petal.Length, Petal.Width, groupS=1),
    data=iris)
#> Warning: Ignoring unknown aesthetics: groupS
#> Error in `[.data.frame`(data, "group"): undefined columns selected
```

title: group column in built data even when aes(group) absent
description:
Hi all. First of all thanks for maintaining ggplot2, it is so useful.

I maintain directlabels::geom_dl which provides a custom geom with a draw_panel method. I was expecting that the built data that I get in the first argument of the draw_panel method should only have a "group" column if I specify aes(group). However I am observing that there is a "group" column even when aes(group) is not specified. Is that normal? 

When aes(group) is not specified by the user I would like to be able to assign a default value for group in my draw_panel method, but I can't do that by testing for presence/absence of the group column (it is always there). Is there another way for me to test whether or not the user has specified aes(group), and assign a default?

Furthermore I observe that group is a vector of -1 if aes(y=numeric_var) but it is a vector with values matching y if aes(y=factor_var). Is that normal? I was expecting that the group column should only depend on aes(group), not aes(y).

Here is a reprex showing what happens when aes(y=numeric_var)
```r
library(ggplot2)
p <- ggplot()+
  geom_text(aes(
    deaths, age, label=sex),
    data=data.frame(
      deaths=1:4,
      age=rep(5:6, each=2),
      sex=rep(c("M", "F"), 2)))
ggplot2::ggplot_build(p)$data[[1]][, c("x", "y", "label", "group")]
#>   x y label group
#> 1 1 5     M    -1
#> 2 2 5     F    -1
#> 3 3 6     M    -1
#> 4 4 6     F    -1
```

Here is a reprex showing what happens when aes(y=factor_var)
```r
library(ggplot2)
p <- ggplot()+
  geom_text(aes(
    deaths, age, label=sex),
    data=data.frame(
      deaths=1:4,
      age=factor(rep(5:6, each=2)),
      sex=rep(c("M", "F"), 2)))
ggplot2::ggplot_build(p)$data[[1]][, c("x", "y", "label", "group")]
#>   x y label group
#> 1 1 1     M     1
#> 2 2 1     F     1
#> 3 3 2     M     2
#> 4 4 2     F     2
```

Thanks in advance for any help you can provide.

title: Annotate all facets with axis ticks and labels for fixed scales
description:
By default, interior facets are not drawn with axis ticks or labels.

``` r
library(ggplot2)

df <- data.frame(
  x = rnorm(900),
  y = rnorm(900),
  a = rep(letters[1:9], each = 10)
)

ggplot(df, aes(x, y)) +
  geom_point() +
  facet_wrap(vars(a))
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/t3JJimc.png)

However, if we set `scales = "free"`, we do get per-facet axis ticks and labels, but now each facet also has its own scale range.

``` r
ggplot(df, aes(x, y)) +
  geom_point() +
  facet_wrap(vars(a), scales = "free")
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/hyS4ECI.png)


I find that it's often desirable to have fixed scales but have each facet have its own axis annotations. This can currently be achieved by setting `scales = "free"` but then manually setting the scale limits.

``` r
ggplot(df, aes(x, y)) +
  geom_point() +
  facet_wrap(vars(a), scales = "free") +
  xlim(-4, 4) + ylim(-4, 4)
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/PnjPESc.png)

I think it would be a good idea to add an option that draws axis annotations for all facets even if scales are fixed. I routinely wish I had this option.

title: Breaks become identical when range is small and closest int is non-zero
description:
I ran into this breaks issue when plotting some values that are all very close to one. The axis breaks are shown as exactly 1, which is non-informative. If the closest int is zero, breaks are displayed as expected. See reprex.

I realise this is a bit of an edge case so not terribly high priority, but I'm flagging it in case anybody else runs into it. A fix might be to figure out what the closest int is, and then add that to the correctly-formatted values you'd get if zero-centred. eg, `1 + 1e-08` etc in this case.

``` r
library("ggplot2")
set.seed(42)
make_plot <- function(mean = 0, sd = 1e-8, n = 100) {
    ggplot() + aes(rnorm(n, mean = mean, sd = sd)) + geom_histogram()
}
make_plot()
#> `stat_bin()` using `bins = 30`. Pick better value with `binwidth`.
```
![](https://i.imgur.com/PcaZrrG.png)

``` r
make_plot(mean = 1)
#> `stat_bin()` using `bins = 30`. Pick better value with `binwidth`.
```
![](https://i.imgur.com/UoySAa8.png)

title: theme_void() removes geom_segments (at least visually) when an alpha aesthetic is used
description:
theme_void() removes geom_segments when an alpha aesthetic is used - or at least they are no longer visible 

```r
#Set up a data frame representing three line segments (same problem happens for geom_curve())
ct=data.frame(list(x=c(2,3,4),y=c(0,0,0),xend=c(2,3,4),yend=c(3,3,3),w=c(1,1,.8)))
# basic plot (size is just there to make the line segments more visible)
ggplot(ct)+geom_segment(aes(x=x,y=y,xend=xend,yend=yend),size=2)
# Add theme_void()
ggplot(ct)+geom_segment(aes(x=x,y=y,xend=xend,yend=yend),size=2)+theme_void()
# Add theme_void and alpha - the line with weight 0.8 disappears
ggplot(ct)+geom_segment(aes(x=x,y=y,xend=xend,yend=yend,alpha=w),size=2)+theme_void()+scale_alpha(guide=F)
# Just have alpha - the line segments come back
ggplot(ct)+geom_segment(aes(x=x,y=y,xend=xend,yend=yend,alpha=w),size=2)+scale_alpha(guide=F)
# Other themes don't have the same  problem
ggplot(ct)+geom_segment(aes(x=x,y=y,xend=xend,yend=yend,alpha=w),size=2)+theme_bw()+scale_alpha(guide=F)


# Change the weights - now the lines with the lower two weights disappear
ct2=data.frame(list(x=c(2,3,4),y=c(0,0,0),xend=c(2,3,4),yend=c(3,3,3),w=c(1,.9,.8)))
ggplot(ct2)+geom_segment(aes(x=x,y=y,xend=xend,yend=yend,alpha=w),size=2)+theme_void()+scale_alpha(guide=F)

# The line segment with the maximum weight (even if not 1) is retained
ct3=data.frame(list(x=c(2,3,4),y=c(0,0,0),xend=c(2,3,4),yend=c(3,3,3),w=c(.7,.9,.8)))
ggplot(ct3)+geom_segment(aes(x=x,y=y,xend=xend,yend=yend,alpha=w),size=2)+theme_void()+scale_alpha(guide=F)

```

title: ggplot2 plots can include large extraneous objects
description:
There are some use cases for serializing ggplot2 objects to disk (e.g. `saveRDS()`, `qs::qsave()`) (https://github.com/tidyverse/ggplot2/issues/3619#issuecomment-628021555).  However, the plots may bundle up extraneous environmental objects resulting in large serialized files.  In the reprex below, a function generates a plot from a `dt` object which is 0.2Mb; however, multiple copies of / pointers to the matrix `mat` are bundled into the ggplot object `p` such that its compressed serialized size is 1.4Gb.

The `mat` is included in mapping and layer quosure environments and in `p$plot_env`.  The latter can be cleaned with `p$plot_env <- rlang::new_environment()` (https://github.com/tidyverse/ggplot2/issues/3994#issuecomment-628082518); however, cleaning the large `mat` out of the quosure environments is more involved.

Would appreciate any suggestions on trimming these objects or ideas to avoid this in the first place.

Thanks

``` r

mat <- outer(1:20000,1:20000) # 3.2Gb matrix

plot_fn <- function(mat) {
  dt <- data.frame(x = 1:dim(mat)[1], y = rowSums(mat))
  p <- ggplot2::ggplot(dt, ggplot2::aes(x, y)) +
    ggplot2::geom_point() +
    ggplot2::geom_point(ggplot2::aes(x = x+1, y = y+1))
}

p <- plot_fn(mat)

butcher::weigh(p)
#> # A tibble: 12 x 2
#>    object             size
#>    <chr>             <dbl>
#>  1 mapping.x   3201.      
#>  2 mapping.y   3201.      
#>  3 layers2     3201.      
#>  4 plot_env    3201.      
#>  5 layers1        0.367   
#>  6 facet          0.172   
#>  7 data.y         0.160   
#>  8 coordinates    0.118   
#>  9 data.x         0.0800  
#> 10 scales         0.0426  
#> 11 labels.x       0.000112
#> 12 labels.y       0.000112
saveRDS(p, "p.rds")
file.info("p.rds")
#>             size isdir mode               mtime               ctime
#> p.rds 1423868059 FALSE  644 2020-06-10 09:45:49 2020-06-10 09:45:49
```

UPDATE:  As the referenced environment is identical for the mapping/layer quosures and also for `p$plot_env`, a quick fix is to remove the large object/s from the referenced environment.  The previous fix of `p$plot_env <- rlang::new_environment()` was leaving the quosure env's intact.

```
butcher::weigh(p)
#> # A tibble: 12 x 2
#>    object             size
#>    <chr>             <dbl>
#>  1 mapping.x   3201.      
#>  2 mapping.y   3201.      
#>  3 layers2     3201.      
#>  4 plot_env    3201.      
#>  5 layers1        0.367   
#>  6 facet          0.172   
#>  7 data.y         0.160   
#>  8 coordinates    0.118   
#>  9 data.x         0.0800  
#> 10 scales         0.0426  
#> 11 labels.x       0.000112
#> 12 labels.y       0.000112
p$plot_env$mat <- NULL
butcher::weigh(p)
#> # A tibble: 12 x 2
#>    object          size
#>    <chr>          <dbl>
#>  1 mapping.x   0.855   
#>  2 mapping.y   0.855   
#>  3 layers2     0.855   
#>  4 plot_env    0.855   
#>  5 layers1     0.367   
#>  6 facet       0.172   
#>  7 data.y      0.160   
#>  8 coordinates 0.118   
#>  9 data.x      0.0800  
#> 10 scales      0.0426  
#> 11 labels.x    0.000112
#> 12 labels.y    0.000112
```

Perhaps a long-term solution would involve ggplot omitting unrelated objects from its environments'.

title: scale_fill_viridis_d associated to hang and 100% CPU
description:
I'm running R 4.0.0 and ggplot 3.3.0 on Ubuntu 20.04. When executing the code shown below to create a stacked bar graph with the viridis palette, I get different results depending on how I run it:

(1) From R Studio, it runs fine in the console.
(2) From R alone, running in a terminal, an empty graphics window pops up, the process appears to hang, and the CPU sits at 100%.
(3) When knitting to various output formats, either from inside RStudio or from the command line, (I've tried beamer and ioslides), I get a hang as well.
(4) If I remove the scale_fill_viridis_d line, it runs fine everywhere, creating a bar graph as expected.

I've verified that this example code works on R 3.6.1 and ggplot2 3.2.0, and this example was based on an actual document that used to compile just fine on previous Linux, R and RStudio versions.

I didn't see a similar report, but I apologize if this is a duplicate.

```r
library(tidyverse)
set.seed(1234)
example.data <- data.frame(
  cat.x = sample(1:2, 50, replace=TRUE),
  cat.y = as.factor(sample(1:5, 50, replace=TRUE))
)
ggplot(example.data) + 
  geom_bar(aes(x=cat.x, fill=cat.y), position="fill") + 
  scale_fill_viridis_d()
```

title: coord_fixed doesn't trigger warning when clipping data
description:
When coord_fixed sets the scale limits a warning is not generated when points are removed from the plot. This can lead to clipping of data without the user knowing.

Maybe this has something to do with the "clip" option in coord_fixed causing unwanted behavior?

```r
library(tidyverse)

# Warning generated with scale_y_continous
#
#>Warning message:
#>  Removed 1 rows containing missing values (geom_point). 
data.frame(x = c(1,10), y = c(1,10)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x,y)) +
  geom_point() +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0,2))



# Warning not generated, datapoint silently clipped
data.frame(x = c(1,10), y = c(1,10)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x,y)) +
  geom_point() +
  coord_fixed(ylim = c(0,2))
```


This was performed with ggplot2 3.3.0

title: Inf is evaluated relative to the panel rather than the scales
description:
Infinite values `Inf` and `-Inf` seem to be evaluated relative to the panel rather than the scale.  When the scales aren't the same, this can have surprising effects.

```r
library(tidyverse)

# Different angles either side of x = 0
ggplot() +
  geom_line(data = tibble(x = c(-Inf, 0, Inf), y = x),
            mapping = aes(x, y)) +
  xlim(c(-1, 1)) +
  ylim(c(-1, 2))
```

![Line graph](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/3522552/84057895-4aa6b900-a9b0-11ea-908a-3d38436df042.png)

Originally discovered by @catatk.

4. When I add ```scale_y_discrete``` with label text as I want them I keep getting this error:

title: geom_line() vs geom_point()
`ggsave()` produces aliased png files on Windows
description:
When using `ggsave()` to save a plot as `png` on Windows the resulting image is quite aliased (zoom in to see the ragged line).

```r
library(ggplot2)
data(gapminder, package = "gapminder")
china <- gapminder[gapminder$country == "China", ]

ggplot(china, aes(year, lifeExp)) + geom_line()
ggsave("test.png")
```
![test](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/11788080/83419300-2afa1880-a425-11ea-91bc-6e5610b81485.png)

This is a [known issue](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/2142) of the `png()` graphics device on Windows. To mitigate this one has to use `cairo` and set the `antialias` argument like so.
```r
ggsave("test2.png", type = "cairo-png", antialias = "subpixel")
```
![test2](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/11788080/83419312-2f263600-a425-11ea-9ba0-1f71068daba9.png)

This is easy enough *if* you know this trick. I'd suggest to automatically set `type = 'cairo-png'` and `antialias = 'subpixel'` on Windows if these arguments have not been explicitly set. I've recently implemented something along those line in the `{hexSticker}` package which uses `ggsave()`. Have a look [here](https://github.com/GuangchuangYu/hexSticker/blob/bc9330a5f6a20d72de98c7d6ace49f0074c984c2/R/sticker.R#L323-L330).

I'd be happy to create a pull request.

title: facet labellers not calling default
description:
I have a plot using facet_grid, that I want to set the facet labels with.
The faceting variables are stored as integers, and I am trying to use lookup tables to specify some expressions, and then pass those to label_parsed.

As I read the docs for labeller(), the lookup table should be passed to .default.

`.default  Default labeller for variables not specified. Also used with lookup tables or non-labeller functions.`

However, this doesn't seem to be happening (note labels on rows.)

I'm not sure if this is a documentation problem, me misunderstanding something, or a problem with the labeller.

---

``` r
library(ggplot2)
tdf <- data.frame(x=c(1,2,3,4), y=c(4,3,2,1), a=c(0,1,0,1), b=c(1, 2, 2, 1))
ggplot(tdf, aes(x, y))+geom_point()+
  facet_grid(a~b, labeller=labeller(a=c(`0`="a^2", `1`="a[2]"), b=c(`1`="One", `2`="Two"), .default=label_parsed))
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/oy3YHWL.png)

<sup>Created on 2020-05-27 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v0.3.0)</sup>


---

If I instead use `.rows` and `.cols` to name the arguments to labeller, I get the expected result.
(The labels on the rows are now passed to label_parsed)

``` r

library(ggplot2)
tdf <- data.frame(x=c(1,2,3,4), y=c(4,3,2,1), a=c(0,1,0,1), b=c(1, 2, 2, 1))
ggplot(tdf, aes(x, y))+geom_point()+
  facet_grid(a~b, labeller=labeller(.rows=c(`0`="a^2", `1`="a[2]"), .cols=c(`1`="One", `2`="Two"), .default=label_parsed))
```

title: Can geom_abline() draw lines a bit longer than the actual Coord range?
description:
Someone told me `geom_abline()` doesn't look nice when we increase the `size`. To be fair, `geom_function()` seems better at the first example, but it has the same problem when the range of the scale is shorter or equal to the coord's range. I think this is intentional, but it might be nice if there's some option to draw lines to outside of the plot area.

(Btw, maybe this is a good chance to replace `GeomAbline` with `GeomFunction`...?)

``` r
library(ggplot2)
library(tibble)
library(patchwork)

p <- ggplot(tibble(x = c(-5, 5), y = c(-4, 6))) +
  geom_line(aes(x, y), size = 10, color = "#cc0000") +
  coord_fixed(xlim = c(-1, 1), ylim = c(-1, 1), expand = FALSE) +
  theme_bw()

p1 <- p +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 1, size = 10, color = "#000088", alpha = 0.7) +
  ggtitle("abline")

p2 <- p +
  geom_function(fun = ~ .x + 1, size = 10, color = "#000088", alpha = 0.7) +
  ggtitle("function")

p1 * p2
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/QmTMIQP.png)

title: munched_lines warning from geom_area()
description:
I am receiving this warning when plotting `geom_area()` with polar coordinates. A few other have reproduced the warning on other systems.

``` r

ggplot() +
  geom_area(aes(x = c(1, 2), 
                y = c(3, 4))) +
  coord_polar()
#> Warning in munched_lines$id + rep(c(0, NA), each = length(ids)): longer object
```

title: scale_x_reverse( ) in renderPlot ( ) or renderPlotly( )
description:
Since I updated R to version 4.0 the scale_x_reverse () function has stopped working together with renderPlot () or renderPlotly( ), which I use in a shiny app that I develop ...
However when I test scale_x_reverse () out of the render it works fine. It is worth mentioning that in all other versions of R it was working normally in both Windowns (7, 8 and 10) and Linux (Ubunto, mint, Debian, Suse). Now I am use Windowns 10, R (4.0), RStudio (1.2.5042).

Can someone help me?

---

Brief description of the problem

```r
`library(shiny)
library(ggplot2)
library(plotly)


ui <- fluidPage(
        fluidRow(align = "center",
          mainPanel(
           plotly::plotlyOutput("plot_multi")
          )
        )
)
  

server <- function(input, output) {

# Data.frame
z <<- runif(1001, min=0, max=1000000)
f <<- seq(0,10,0.01)
testy_multi <<- data.frame(Chemical_Shift=f,Spectrum=z)
ranges_multi <- reactiveValues(x = c((min(testy_multi$Chemical_Shift)), max(testy_multi$Chemical_Shift)), y = c(-100,1000000))
spectrums_multi <- reactiveValues(dat = data.frame(Chemical_Shift=f,Spectrum=z))

# Plot
output$plot_multi <- plotly::renderPlotly({
  
  ggplot2::ggplot(spectrums_multi$dat,ggplot2::aes(Chemical_Shift,Spectrum)) + ggplot2::geom_line(color='blue') + 
    
    ggplot2::coord_cartesian(xlim = ranges_multi$x, ylim = ranges_multi$y, expand = FALSE) + ggplot2::scale_x_reverse() +
    
    ggplot2::theme(axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_text(size = 12, color = "#000000"),
                   axis.text.y = ggplot2::element_text(size = 12, color = "#000000"),
                   title = ggplot2::element_text(face = "bold", color = "#000000", size = 17),
                   axis.title = ggplot2::element_text(face = "bold", color = "#000000", size = 15)
    ) +
    
    ggplot2::labs(x = "Chemical Shift", y = "Intensity")
  
})

}

shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)
`
```

title: Justifying the legend with respect to the full plot area rather than the panel
description:
Now that the plot titles and captions can be aligned with respect to the full plot area, it would be great if the same was true for the legend. At the moment, if the legend is positioned at the top of the plot below the title it is aligned to the plot panel, making it misaligned with the title:

``` r
library(ggplot2)

ggplot(data = diamonds, mapping = aes(x = carat, y = price, color = cut)) +
  geom_point() +
  labs(title = "A plot title") +
  theme(plot.title.position = "plot",
        legend.position = "top",
        legend.justification = "left")
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/WGxMzJw.png)

<sup>Created on 2020-05-22 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v0.3.0)</sup>
  
Experimenting with negative values in `legend.justification = c(x,y)` can get the legend to align with the title, but the value is dependent on the size of the y-axis labels

title: [Feature request] Setting axis intervals with automatic range
description:
Right now, the breaks of an axis can be set up using breaks. e.g. 
`scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 100, by=20)) `

However, this is tedious as the range of the breaks are always requried. Is it possible to have:
`scale_x_continuous(interval=20) `? Then let ggplot automatically calculate the breaks from the range of the data. e.g. `scale_y_continuous(interval=20) ` outputs the breaks 0, 20, 40, 60, 80, and 100,  if the x-axis variable ranges from 0 to 100. 

This feature can be very helpful in piping into ggplot. Right now, we have to use this code to specify the interval to plot a processed dataframe:

`df <- df %>% fun(.)   ; df %> ggplot()+scale_x_continuous (breaks=seq(min(df$x), max(df$x), by=20))
`

Once that feature becomes available, the code can be simplified to:

`df %>% fun(.) %>% ggplot()+scale_x_continuous(interval=20)`

Thanks.


title: Add 'reverse' option to scale_y_date?
description:
---

Hi folks. It seems various people have been confounded by trying to reverse the order of date scales in ggplot2. The scale_x_date family of functions is great, but their presence seems to have made reversing scales even less intuitive/possible.

By way of example, I convert dates into yeardays (1:366) and project on the Y axis, with values going from bottom to top, Jan to Dec (various irrelevant code lines removed e.g. theme, title etc):

```r
mydata %<>% mutate(Day = yday(Date))
ggplot(mydata, aes(x = toppid, y = as.Date(Day, origin = as.Date("2018-01-01")))) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = MarineArea), size = 0.25) +
  facet_wrap(.~Stock, scales = "free") +
  scale_y_date(date_breaks = "1 month", date_labels = "%b")
```
![MarineAreaEntryYDayStock](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/4599748/82375323-456bd500-99d5-11ea-80c1-1bc2cb696d02.png)

It occurred to me that I could reverse the data themselves for Day:

`mydata$Day2 <- 367 - mydata$Day`

But this only affects the plotted points, not the scale.
Given the [existing solutions](https://github.com/tidyverse/ggplot2/issues/956) to this issue seem hacky, if applicable to the above formulation at all, is there any chance that a future release could see a `reverse` or `trans` parameter added into `scale_x/y_date`?

Thanks in advance.

title: Issue with `geom_rect` and `alpha` on faceting
description:
If using `geom_rect` in connection with faceting, not all manual controls are used across panels.
In order to avoid expansion of the plotting region, the use of `geom_rect` with manually specified coordinates (`xmin`, `xmax`, `ymin` and `ymax`) and appearance parameters (e.g. `fill` or `alpha`) is useful. However, I have experienced that changing `alpha` only affects one of the panels. 

```r
mtcars %>% 
  ggplot(aes(y = mpg, x = wt)) + 
  geom_point() + facet_wrap(~gear) + 
  geom_rect(xmin = 2, xmax = 4, ymin = 15, ymax = 30, alpha = 0.1, fill = "#004400")
```

The opacity only applies to a single panel:
![Rplot](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/8102518/82296939-3c1d4100-99b2-11ea-9e59-8474a348e9f7.png)

title: timezone parameter for scale_x_datetime has no effect
description:
I am trying to use the `timezone` parameter to `scale_x_datetime` to control how the tick labels are displayed, but I can't get it to work. Changing the timezone does not seem to make a difference to plot output. This probably applies equally to `scale_y_datetime`. Potentially I am not using the correct syntax and the documentation could be expanded.

```r
library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)

plotdata <- tribble(
  ~t_stamp, ~value,
  "2019-08-17T06:00:00", 1,
  "2019-08-17T07:00:00", 2,
  "2019-08-17T08:00:00", 3
)

plotdata <- plotdata %>% 
  mutate(t_stamp=force_tz(ymd_hms(t_stamp),tzone="US/Mountain"))

ggplot(plotdata) +
  geom_point(mapping=aes(x=t_stamp, y=value)) +
  scale_x_datetime(timezone = "US/Mountain")

ggplot(plotdata) +
  geom_point(mapping=aes(x=t_stamp, y=value)) +
  scale_x_datetime(timezone = "US/Eastern")

# both plots are the same
```

title: ggplot2:::contour_breaks makes one bin less than expected
description:
Likely related, yet not quite the same: https://github.com/tidyverse/ggplot2/issues/3824 Following up on this Stackoverflow thread: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/61817440/follow-up-to-stat-contour-2d-bins-interpretation?noredirect=1#comment109350645_61817440 A previous version of ggplot2 3.2.1 seemed to have worked as expected with the correct number of bins. **This does make one bin less than expected:** ``` r library(ggplot2) set.seed(1) n=100 foo <- data.frame(x=rnorm(n, 0, 1), y=rnorm(n, 0, 1)) ggplot() + stat_density_2d(data = foo, aes(x, y), bins = 5, color = "black") + geom_point(data = foo, aes(x = x, y = y)) ``` ![](https://i.imgur.com/jiPwDHO.png) Created on 2020-05-15 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v0.3.0) **The following fix results in expected behaviour:** in `ggplot2:::contour_breaks`, changing bins-1 to "bins" : ``` contour_breaks2 <- function (z_range, bins = NULL, binwidth = NULL, breaks = NULL) { if (!is.null(breaks)) { return(breaks) } if (is.null(bins) && is.null(binwidth)) { breaks <- pretty(z_range, 10) } if (!is.null(bins)) { binwidth <- diff(z_range)/(bins) } if (is.null(breaks)) { breaks <- fullseq(z_range, binwidth) } breaks } StatContour$compute_group <- function (data, scales, bins = NULL, binwidth = NULL, breaks = NULL, na.rm = FALSE) { z_range <- range(data$z, na.rm = TRUE, finite = TRUE) breaks <- contour_breaks(z_range, bins, binwidth, breaks) isolines <- ggplot2:::xyz_to_isolines(data, breaks) path_df <- ggplot2:::iso_to_path(isolines, data$group[1]) path_df$level <- as.numeric(path_df$level) path_df$nlevel <- scales::rescale_max(path_df$level) path_df } ggplot() + stat_density_2d(data = foo, aes(x, y), bins = 5, color = "black") + geom_point(data = foo, aes(x = x, y = y)) ```

title: using weights with stat_summary()
description:
Currently, a variable mapped to `weight` aesthetic is not taken into account by `stat_summary()`. In such a situation, maybe a warning should be displayed as some users will expect that these weights will be taken into account in the computation.

In addition, considering a version of `stat_summary()` able to deal with weights could be relevant.

Regards

title: Integrating new grid features in ggplot2
description:
Hi Team

The graphic engine and grid is getting some love lately and we will look into a future where gradient + image fill and non-rectangular clipping is available on the devices that supports it. I think both have interest from the ggplot2 side.

While we are not there yet, @pmur002 has a working implementation and I think we may just as well begin discussing to what extend and how we may use this in ggplot2. I think the most interesting (seeing as ggpattern exist) possibility is gradient fill. This will most definitely be a challenge to integrate into the scale system because gradients depend on multiple values. Should the scaling happen from discrete values to a set of predefined gradients? or should each stop be mapped to different values. Lots of things to discuss!

Non-rectangular clipping also opens up a lot of possibilities, some not having a clear parallel in the current API (e.g. clipping groups or layers to certain areas)

@clauswilke @karawoo @Hadley @yutannihilation @paleolimbot please join the discussion 🙂

description:
---

As others have pointed out (https://github.com/tidyverse/ggplot2/issues/688), having a position_dodge option such as `drop = FALSE` would be really helpful for plots like this:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/40525022/81197406-74b62700-8f7d-11ea-81d1-be79aa24d27e.png)

I know Hadley has given some helpful workaround suggestions (e.g. faceting) and has mentioned that this isn't within the scope of position_dodge but I am hoping that one more person raising the issue might help to make the change. 

What's happening for some of my plots' x-categories is that there are only 2 data points (e.g. cases in Homozygous Alt in my plot), which is enough to generate a boxplot, but not a violin plot

```r
geom_violin(alpha=0.4, position = position_dodge(width=0.9))
```

Because the 3rd green violin plot doesn't have a counterpart to "dodge", the violin plot is centered and therefore wider and not aligned with its corresponding boxplot which is quite sad to look at.

While faceting works to an extent:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/40525022/81197745-e2625300-8f7d-11ea-8868-96d0149c9dab.png)

It would look much cleaner for publication if I could do `position = position_dodge(width=0.9), drop = FALSE)`

I hope this suggestion is taken seriously and I really appreciate your help & time.

Chris

title: Missing generic `+` method
description:
(cc @clauswilke  https://github.com/tidyverse/ggplot2/pull/3818#issuecomment-623055651)

## Context

Let's say `foo` is a class defined by a package other than ggplot2 (Ex: `patchwork` or `GGally`). `foo` objects also inherit from `gg`. `bar` objects do not inherit from `gg`

You can currently perform `gg_obj + foo_obj` as both objects inherit from `gg` and would produce the same `+.gg` method from Opt's double dispatch.

Currently, to control how the right-hand-side (`foo` objects) are added, we can define `ggplot_add.foo`. 

## Problem

However, currently we can not customize how left-hand-side objects (ex: `foo_obj + gg_obj`) are added to `gg` objects.  

Ex: left hand side structures are not ggplot2 objects and will not work with ggplot2 internal methods
```r
x <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(wt, mpg)) + geom_point()
foo_obj <- structure(
 list(x, x), 
  class = c("foo", "gg")
)
# can not customize how the theme is added
foo_obj + theme_bw()
```

Ex: conflicting `+` methods make addition impossible
```r
x <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(wt, mpg)) + geom_point()
bar_obj <- structure(
 list(x, x), 
  class = c("bar") # does not inherit from 'gg'
)
`+.bar` <- function(e1, e2) {
  # only add to second plot
  e1[[2]] <- e1[[2]] + e2
  e1
}
# Conflicting `+` methods
bar_obj + theme_bw()
#> Error in bar_obj + theme_bw() : non-numeric argument to binary operator
#> In addition: Warning message:
#> Incompatible methods ("+.bar", "+.gg") for "+" 
```

### Real life situation

* To get around this in `GGally`, I overwrite the `+.gg` method.  Unfortunately, this produces a warning and does not dispatch to the next available plus method.
I am open to other options, but I don't know how to produce one that would play well with other packages.

* I would like to be able to add a scale to a `ggmatrix` object in appropriate places only (Ex: `ggmatrix_obj + gg_scale_obj`). With the current methods, I don't know how I can do this cleanly.





## Goal

Define a generic add method (ex: `add_gg(e1, e2)`).  This generic add method should be called within `+.gg` to avoid double dispatch confusion involving `+`.    

`ggplot2`'s `+.gg` is not commutative. So I believe this situation has merit. 

Using the implementation in https://github.com/tidyverse/ggplot2/pull/3818 , I would be able to define how a theme object is added to a custom object. 
``` r
library(ggplot2)
x <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(wt, mpg)) + geom_point()
foo_obj <- structure(
 list(x, x), 
  class = c("foo", "gg")
)
`add_gg.foo` <- function(e1, e2) {
  # only add to second plot
  e1[[2]] <- e1[[2]] + e2
  e1
}
print.foo <- function(x, ...) {
  gridExtra::grid.arrange(x[[1]], x[[2]], ncol = 2)
}

foo_obj + theme_bw()
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/BsACzIL.png)

<sup>Created on 2020-02-11 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v0.3.0)</sup>

`strip.text.y.left` is not documented. This issue becomes a documentation one.

## Original issue raised:

When facet labels are on the right, they can be rotated:

```r
d2 <- diamonds[sample(seq_len(nrow(diamonds)), 1000), ]
```

title: Misaligned date axis for some custom breaks functions
description:
A custom breaks function on the date axis seem to mis-align the breaks and labels.  Another does not.  But corresponding date vector inputs for both functions work fine.  

Not sure if this has already been reported - I've looked and found [this issue](https://github.com/tidyverse/ggplot2/issues/814), but it's old.

Reproducible example - note how the 30 March break shifts off the maximum data point it should align with.

```
require(tidyverse)

set.seed(pi)
df <- data.frame(date = Sys.Date() - 0:29, price = runif(30))
p <- ggplot(df, aes(date, price)) + geom_line() +  geom_point() + coord_fixed(ratio=5)

# max price is 0.9101477 on 30 March
df %>% filter(price == max(price))
#>         date     price
#> 1 2020-03-30 0.9101477

weekend_breaks_correct <- function(x) {
  mondays <- scales::fullseq(x, "1 week")
  fridays <- mondays - lubridate::days(3)
  sort(c(mondays, fridays))
}

weekend_breaks_misaligned <- function(x){
  x <- seq(x[1], x[2], by=1)
  x[weekdays(x) %in% c('Monday','Friday')]
}

( breaks_cor = weekend_breaks_correct(range(df$date)) )
#>  [1] "2020-03-20" "2020-03-23" "2020-03-27" "2020-03-30" "2020-04-03"
#>  [6] "2020-04-06" "2020-04-10" "2020-04-13" "2020-04-17" "2020-04-20"
#> [11] "2020-04-24" "2020-04-27"
( breaks_mis = weekend_breaks_misaligned(range(df$date)) )
#> [1] "2020-03-30" "2020-04-03" "2020-04-06" "2020-04-10" "2020-04-13"
#> [6] "2020-04-17" "2020-04-20" "2020-04-24"

# correct function
p + scale_x_date(date_labels = "%a %b %d", breaks = weekend_breaks_correct)
```
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1282581/80304289-cbb54280-87ac-11ea-86ed-841f91d1a297.png)

```
# misalisgned function
p + scale_x_date(date_labels = "%a %b %d", breaks = weekend_breaks_misaligned)
```

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1282581/80304312-d8d23180-87ac-11ea-85a8-626132b36ecd.png)

```
# vectors are both correct
p + scale_x_date(date_labels = "%a %b %d", breaks = breaks_cor)
p + scale_x_date(date_labels = "%a %b %d", breaks = breaks_mis)
```

title: Shortcut for `scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(c(0, 0.05))`
description:
When creating histogram or bar charts the standard expansion factor of  `0.05` creates an unsighty gap between the bars and the x axis.

```
library(ggplot2)
data(mtcars)
ggplot(mtcars, aes(hp)) +
  geom_histogram()
```

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/11788080/80287984-0ed3cf00-8735-11ea-8f62-96140c2788a4.png)

To remove this gap currently one has to add `scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(c(0, 0.05))` to the plot. This is cumbersome to type, easy to forget and hard to grasp for beginners.

I'd love to have a shortcut for that, something like:
```
scale_y_tight <- function(...) {
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(0, 0.05), ...)
}
```

This is in the same spirit as `ylab()` or `ylim()`.

Thinking a bit further maybe this could even be an option:

```
exact_ylim <- function(...) {
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(...), expand = expansion())
}
```
This would force the axis limits to be exactly those requested which is not the case currently with `ylim()`.

title: Smarter axes limits around stat_density_2d polygons
description:
Axes limits are based on points rather than on the computed contour lines/shapes. This  leads to some weird cropping of polygons:

```r
faithful %>%
  mutate(gr = if_else(row_number()%%2==0,1,2)) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = eruptions, y = waiting)) +
  stat_density_2d(aes(alpha = after_stat(level)), geom = "polygon")+ 
  geom_density2d(color="black")+
  facet_wrap(~gr)+
  theme_classic()
```
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/42210264/80209077-ab14ad80-8631-11ea-8388-d1bce0c72198.png)




A fiddly way around this is to change the limits manually with blank layers:

```r
faithful %>%
  mutate(gr = if_else(row_number()%%2==0,1,2)) %>% 
  mutate(miny=waiting-10,maxy=waiting+10,minx = eruptions-1,maxx=eruptions+1) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = eruptions, y = waiting)) +
  geom_density2d(color="black")+
  stat_density_2d(aes(alpha = after_stat(level)), geom = "polygon")+ 
  facet_wrap(~gr)+
  theme_classic()+
  geom_blank(aes(y = miny)) +
  geom_blank(aes(y = maxy)) +
  geom_blank(aes(x = minx)) +
  geom_blank(aes(x = maxx))
```
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/42210264/80209130-c5e72200-8631-11ea-8480-888861367834.png)

but this becomes quickly a nightmare if one has to do it often (even without hardcoding values). It would be nice to have the axes automatically adjust to the size of the largest polygon. Alternatively, polygon cropping should be handled differently.
Thank you, and apologies if this is already well known and/or has a solution already!

title: Remove stat and position arguments from qplot() and formaly deprecate the function
description:
`stat` and `position` were deprecated 4.5 years ago ([v2.0.0](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/news/index.html#deprecated-features)), so I think it's time to remove them. I think we have no development bandwidth to fix such tricky bugs like https://github.com/tidyverse/ggplot2/issues/3670.

Also, can we agree on deprecating `qplot()` itself? Though we've never discussed this formally, I believe the use of `qplot()` is discouraged, which virtually means it's deprecated.

title: Suggestion: `rel`-class can inherit value from `unit`-class theme elements
description:
I know `rel` objects are not really supported as theme elements on their own, but since the `size` argument in `element_line/rect/text()` can take a `rel` object and inherit the (modified) value from the parent, it doesn't seem like too far a stretch to have child `rel` theme elements.

Suppose you'd like your legend keys to be half as tall as usual, it would be neat if you could do the following:

``` r
library(ggplot2)

ggplot(iris, aes(Sepal.Length, Sepal.Width)) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = Species)) +
  theme(legend.key.height = rel(0.5))
#> Error: Theme element `legend.key.height` must be an `unit` object.
```
<sup>Created on 2020-04-18 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v0.3.0)</sup>

I think it would require changes at these locations.

* This check would have to allow `rel` classes for `unit` elements

https://github.com/tidyverse/ggplot2/blob/7e6d1259237d9a2b48b8156e62ada2c47c411f31/R/theme.r#L530-L533

* This might need an extra logical branch for `rel`-`rel` and `rel`-`unit` elements  

https://github.com/tidyverse/ggplot2/blob/7e6d1259237d9a2b48b8156e62ada2c47c411f31/R/theme.r#L665-L668

* Don't allow `rel` objects as 'root'-nodes in the element tree. I think the most appropriate spot to do this would be in `validate_element()`.

https://github.com/tidyverse/ggplot2/blob/40f67518a8d0ee8d7b6a1d1851c206656864fac8/R/theme-elements.r#L508

Thanks for considering!

title: Case of poor error message in PR #3659
description:
This is an issue against PR #3659, which is currently on hold pending the next minor ggplot2 release. I'm filing this so I won't forget. This should probably be fixed before the PR gets merged.

In a nutshell, in some cases `coord_sf()` encounters numeric issues when trying to calculate plot limits and errors out. This is fine, but the error message should inform the user how to work around this problem (by setting `default_crs = NULL`). Also, these numeric issues probably shouldn't arise when `lims_method = "geometry_bbox"`, but I haven't checked this yet carefully. Reprex below.

``` r
library(sf)
library(ggplot2)

grid <- st_sf(st_make_grid(what = 'polygons'))

# Robinson, works
ggplot(grid) + geom_sf() + coord_sf(crs = st_crs(54030))
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/vcVQpA8.png)

``` r

# Mollweide, doesn't work, that's Ok but error message is poor
ggplot(grid) + geom_sf() + coord_sf(crs = st_crs(54009))
#> Error: Scale limits cannot be mapped onto spatial coordinates.

# Mollweide, doesn't work, but probably should
ggplot(grid) + geom_sf() +
  coord_sf(crs = st_crs(54009), lims_method = "geometry_bbox")
#> Error: Scale limits cannot be mapped onto spatial coordinates.

# Mollweide, works
ggplot(grid) + geom_sf() +
  coord_sf(crs = st_crs(54009), default_crs = NULL)
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/Tjywl5t.png)

<sup>Created on 2020-04-11 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v0.3.0)</sup>

title: Legend keys from geom_sf() change upon repeat printing of the same plot
description:
I'm having a super weird issue with `ggsave` and, after [sharing it at RStudio community](https://community.rstudio.com/t/legend-keys-from-geom-sf-in-pdfs-created-using-ggsave-dont-match-what-is-displayed-in-the-plots-window-nor-the-output-from-rstudios-export/60722/4), Mara Averick suggested I open an issue here. So here I am 😅 

Basically, the legends of plots I generate using `ggsave` do not match what is displayed in RStudio's "Plots" window nor the legends of plots I generate using RStudio's "Export" option. This is happening for maps created using `geom_sf`.

Here's an example:

``` r
library(rnaturalearth)
library(ggplot2)

world <-
  rnaturalearth::ne_countries(scale = "medium", returnclass = "sf") # creates a r object  called "world" with spatial data

ggplot2::ggplot(data = world) + #starts plot with "world" as its data
  geom_sf(aes(color = continent), show.legend = "point") # draws map with colored continent outlines
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/ViGt452.png)

<sup>Created on 2020-04-10 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v0.3.0)</sup>

As you can see, the map above has points as its legend key. That is the output I wanted to get, however, when I use `ggsave("ggsave_test.pdf")` to save the map as a pdf file this is what I get:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/39991049/79004721-a3470a80-7b55-11ea-8af3-7185905ef36b.png)

The weird thing is that this problem seems to be exclusive to ggsave since saving the plot using RStudio's "Export" functionality or knitting a Rmarkdown document result in the plot having points as its legend key.

This happens for .ps, .pdf, .jpeg, .tiff, .png, .bmp, and .svg files both when leaving `ggsave()`'s plot argument  blank (e.g., when it uses `last_plot()` like in the reprex above), and when using the saved map as the argument for plot. There's an exception though I used `purrr::walk` to test the different file formats and the .eps file that was generated using the named map as ggsave()'s "plot" argument has the points as its key ! The plots generated using ggsave(filename = here::here("ggsave_no_loop.eps"), plot = map), and `purrr::walk` without the named map as plot's argument have the squares as their keys though.

I think this might be a macOS-specific issue (or even something that is happening only in my computer) because this problem doesn't happen in rstudio.cloud.

Cheers and thanks for your amazing work!

title: Axis labelling issue with coord_sf()
description:
This apparent bug is related to a previous feature request that was fixed in 2018 https://github.com/tidyverse/ggplot2/issues/2846 but has appeared in the recent ggplot2 release (3.3.0). 

When using coord_sf() with the label_graticule argument specified, strange axis labelling artefacts sometimes appear on the opposing axes. As far as I can tell the issue only arises when expand = F and when the dataset being plotted contains lots of features that intersect the edge of the plotting region. I have run into it when plotting rasters as in the reprex or when plotting dense simple feature polygon objects using geom_sf. I have made similar maps using previous releases and not run into this issue so I can only think it must be a bug that is crept into newer versions.

This combination of settings (expand = F and graticule labelling other than default) is quite common in cartography so it would be good to work out what is causing this behaviour.

```r
library(ggplot2); library(raster)

# Create raster

data = raster(extent(-18.7, -10, -12, -4),nrow=960,ncol=1044,vals = 1:(960*1044),
              crs=crs("+init=epsg:4326"))

# Convert to data frame for plotting

data = as.data.frame(as(data,'SpatialPixelsDataFrame'))

# Create plot

plot = 
  ggplot()+
  geom_raster(data=data,aes(x=x,y=y,fill=layer)) 
  
# Plot with labelling issues

plot + coord_sf(expand=F,crs=4326,label_graticule = 'NW')

# Plot without labelling issues

plot + coord_sf(expand=T,crs=4326,label_graticule = 'NW')

plot + coord_sf(expand=F,crs=4326)
```
