title: ggplot2 2.2.0 seems to break gtable::gtable_add_grob
description:
In plots with nested facet categories, ggplot2 repeats the facet label for the "outer" category, rather than having a single spanning facet across all the sub-categories. I have some code that I've been using to cover the outer facets with a single spanning facet strip using `gtable_add_grob` from the `gtable` package. However this code no longer works with ggplot2 2.2.0 (see below for details on what goes wrong).  Below is a reproducible example (based on my answer to [this SO question](http://stackoverflow.com/questions/36968581/ggplot2-boxplot-with-colors-and-text-labels-mapped-to-combination-of-two-catego/36971938#36971938)). I wanted to see if this is a bug and if there's a way around the problem (other than reinstalling ggplot2 2.1.0 when I want to create spanning facet strips). 

```
# Data
densityAGRLKA = structure(list(location = structure(c(1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 
    1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 1L, 1L, 
    1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 
    2L, 2L), .Label = c("SF", "SS"), class = "factor"), species = structure(c(1L, 
    1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 
    1L, 1L, 1L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 
    2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L), .Label = c("AGR", "LKA"), class = "factor"), 
        position = structure(c(1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 
        2L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 
        1L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 
        2L), .Label = c("top", "bottom"), class = "factor"), density = c(0.41, 
        0.41, 0.43, 0.33, 0.35, 0.43, 0.34, 0.46, 0.32, 0.32, 0.4, 
        0.4, 0.45, 0.34, 0.39, 0.39, 0.31, 0.38, 0.48, 0.3, 0.42, 
        0.34, 0.35, 0.4, 0.38, 0.42, 0.36, 0.34, 0.46, 0.38, 0.36, 
        0.39, 0.38, 0.39, 0.39, 0.39, 0.36, 0.39, 0.51, 0.38)), .Names = c("location", 
    "species", "position", "density"), row.names = c(NA, -40L), class = "data.frame")

# Install ggplot2 2.1.0 from local file 
# install.packages("ggplot2_2.1.0.tar.gz", repos=NULL, type="source")

library(ggplot2)
library(grid)
library(gtable)

# Dodge width
pd = position_dodge(0.7)

## Initital ggplot2 plot
p=ggplot(densityAGRLKA, aes("", density)) + 
  geom_boxplot(width=0.7, position=pd) + 
  theme_bw() +
  facet_grid(. ~ species + location +  position) +
  theme(panel.margin=unit(0,"lines"),
        strip.background=element_rect(color="grey30", fill="grey90"),
        panel.border=element_rect(color="grey90"),
        axis.ticks.x=element_blank()) +
  labs(x="")
```

Here's what the original plot looks like:

![original plot](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/436817/20499324/e35f6a48-afe5-11e6-9391-cca1448df42f.png)

Now, let's place spanning strips over the original facet strips.
```
pg = ggplotGrob(p)

# Add spanning strip labels for species
pos = c(4,11)    
for (i in 1:2) {
  pg <- gtable_add_grob(pg, 
                        list(rectGrob(gp=gpar(col="grey50", fill="grey90")),
                             textGrob(unique(densityAGRLKA$species)[i], 
                                      gp=gpar(cex=0.8))), 3,pos[i],3,pos[i]+7,
                        name=c("a","b"))
}

# Add spanning strip labels for location
pos=c(4,7,11,15)
for (i in 1:4) {
  pg = gtable_add_grob(pg, 
                       list(rectGrob(gp = gpar(col="grey50", fill="grey90")),
                            textGrob(rep(unique(densityAGRLKA$location),2)[i], 
                                     gp=gpar(cex=0.8))), 4,pos[i],4,pos[i]+3,
                       name = c("c", "d"))
}

# Draw the plot
grid.draw(pg)
```
Here's what the plot looks like after adding spanning facet strips with ggplot2 2.1.0. This represents the original (desired) behavior of the code above:

![add spanning strips with ggplot 2 1](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/436817/20499371/15f13e32-afe6-11e6-95e2-1cadc909d143.png)

```
# Now detach ggplot2 2.1.0 and install ggplot2 2.2.0
#detach(package:ggplot2, unload=TRUE)
#install.packages("ggplot2")
#library(ggplot2)
```
After installing and loading ggplot2 2.2.0 I ran the code above again. Below is what the plot looks like. Actually, I made one small change to the plot code before creating the graph below: I added `clip="off"` in both calls to `gtable_add_grob`. Without that change, the plot below would look exactly the same as the original, unaltered plot. 

![add spanning strips with ggplot 2 2](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/436817/20499484/871ba3f4-afe6-11e6-902b-c0eb85a0dd6b.png)

I'm not sure why, but `gtable_add_grob` seems to be placing the labels correctly in the horizontal dimension while ignoring the vertical placement arguments. Also, the `rectGrob` isn't showing up at all. Is this a bug, or does ggplot2 2.2.0  require a different workflow to make changes like this?

title: Warning when unsetting an aesthetic that's not used by a geom
description:
If you add a geom that uses a different data set, and it does *not* use an aesthetic set in the `ggplot()` call,

In the example below, I'm adding a `geom_linerange()` which uses a different data set from the one specified in the `ggplot()` call. The linerange doesn't have a `y` aesthetic. Its data set, `d2`, also doesn't have the `yval` column which was used in the aesthetic mapping for `y` at the top level.

If I map `aes(y=NULL)` in the `geom_linerange`, it gives a warning that it's ignoring `y`. If I don't map `y`, then it errors because it still tries to evaluate the `y=yval` mapping even though it's not used for that geom.

```R
library(ggplot2)

d <- data.frame(
  xval = 1:2,
  yval = 1:2
)

d2 <- data.frame(
  xval = 3:4,
  yval2 = 3:4
)

p <- ggplot(d, aes(x=xval, y=yval)) +
  geom_point()

p + geom_linerange(aes(y = NULL, ymin = yval2, ymax = yval2+1), data = d2)
#> Warning: Ignoring unknown aesthetics: y

p + geom_linerange(aes(ymin = yval2, ymax = yval2+1), data = d2)
#> Error in eval(expr, envir, enclos) : object 'yval' not found
```

title: Ordering within facets
description:
[This post](https://drsimonj.svbtle.com/ordering-categories-within-ggplot2-facets) discusses a method for differently ordering categories that appear in multiple facets with different values on a continuous variable. As far as I'm aware, there isn't a simple method for achieving this, and @dgrtwo suggested it could be useful for others to have a neat wrapper function or new stat option to handle it.

Here's a small reproducible example to explain the problem:

``` r
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)

d <- data.frame(
  f = rep(c("f1", "f2"), each = 3),
  x = rep(c("a", "b", "c"), 2),
  y = c(1, 2, 3, 3, 2, 1)
)

# No easy way to order categories within facets
ggplot(d, aes(x, y)) +
  geom_col() +
  facet_wrap(~ f)
```

![unnamed-chunk-1-1](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/11235783/20249159/91f185a4-aa47-11e6-9b94-9085cf1082a2.png)


``` r
# This will handle the ordering
d <- d %>% 
  ungroup() %>%   # As a precaution / handle in a separate .grouped_df method
  arrange(f, y) %>%   # arrange by facet variables and continuous values
  mutate(.r = row_number()) # Add a row number variable

ggplot(d, aes(.r, y)) +  # Use .r instead of x
  geom_col() +
  facet_wrap(~ f, scales = "free") +  # Should free scales (though could be left to user)
  scale_x_continuous(  # This handles replacement of .r for x
    breaks = d$.r,     # notice need to reuse data frame
    labels = d$x
  )
```

![unnamed-chunk-1-2](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/11235783/20249161/9b346884-aa47-11e6-89ce-8b89e507697e.png)

Although this example handles bars, it seems generally applicable to other geoms (e.g., points). Some options for making this readily accessible for users:

- Include a wrapper function for the data ordering, and leave the plotting up to them.
- Add an option in the `facet` functions.
- Add something like an `order_by` argument to `scale_x/y_discrete`

I've created [new fork](https://github.com/drsimonj/ggplot2) to see what works.

title: Different positioning for different factors
description:
Let's start with some data to illustrate the issue:

``` r
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)

dt <- data.frame(
  y = c(0.1, 0.2, 0.5, 0.6, 0.2, 0.45, 0.8, 0.85),
  x = c("A", "A", "A", "A", "B", "B", "B", "B"),
  c = factor(c(1, 1, 2, 2, 1, 1, 2, 2)),
  s = factor(c(1, 2, 1, 2, 1, 2, 1, 2))
)
```

As you can see, there are several values per category `x`, and two factors `c` and `s`. Let's produce a basic plot:

``` r
p <- ggplot(dt, aes(x, y, color = c)) + theme_bw()
p + geom_point(aes(shape = s), size = 3)
```

![rplot](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/4542928/19777751/f2af7152-9c79-11e6-9925-c6031fdcdf1a.png)

The problem here is that I would like to dodge by colour `c`, but stack by shape `s`. If I'm not mistaken, currently this is not possible. If you specify `position_dodge()`, dodging is performed for all factors, colour and shape in this case, which is not what I want:

``` r
pos = position_dodge(0.7)
p + geom_point(aes(shape = s), size = 3, pos = pos)
```

![rplot](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/4542928/19777930/b15941aa-9c7a-11e6-8c52-17f428047689.png)

The point here is that I want to produce a stem plot, e.g.:

``` r
lims <- dt %>%
  group_by(x, c) %>%
  summarise(yend = max(y), y = min(y))

p + geom_point(aes(shape = s), size = 3) +
  geom_segment(aes(xend = x, yend = yend, y = 0), data = lims, alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_segment(aes(xend = x, yend = yend), data = lims)
```

![rplot](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/4542928/19778052/508af124-9c7b-11e6-98fe-23d8cb5f2e7f.png)

But I want to keep stacking for shapes and introduce dodging for colours. Obviously, if we specify position as before, it's a total mess:

``` r
p + geom_point(aes(shape = s), size = 3, pos = pos) +
  geom_segment(aes(xend = x, yend = yend, y = 0), data = lims, alpha = 0.3, pos = pos) +
  geom_segment(aes(xend = x, yend = yend), data = lims, pos = pos)
```

title: Cannot pass check.aes through geom_* to layer
description:
My colorplaner ggplot2 extension involves a scale which accepts an aesthetic unknown to the layer and maps that aesthetic to one the layer accepts (specifically, a secondary color/fill mapping translated through a bivariate color scale to `color` or `fill`). 

With the changes in befc4d0 for issue #1585, a warning is now generated if that mapping is created at the layer level:

``` R
library(ggplot2)
library(colorplaner)
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = drat, y = mpg)) +
  geom_point(aes(color = hp, color2 = disp)) +
  scale_color_colorplane()
```

```
Warning: Ignoring unknown aesthetics: color2
```

In this instance the warning is untrue, as the scale interprets color2 and the plot is generated as expected. However, since the layers are ignorant of their scales, I cannot figure out a solution to inform the layers of the scale's handling of the aesthetic to avoid this warning. This isn't a show stopper as the mapping can simply be done at the plot level or the warning can be ignored, but it could certainly introduce confusion to users. 

The `layer` function now includes a `check.aes` parameter option to skip this checking, but it does not seem possible to pass that parameter through the standard `geom_*` constructors, as the `...` arguments to `geom_*` get wrapped up in a `params` list passed on to `layer` (e.g. in `geom_point` [here](https://github.com/hadley/ggplot2/blob/master/R/geom-point.r#L113)).

``` R
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = drat, y = mpg)) +
  geom_point(aes(color = hp, unknown_aes = disp), check.aes = FALSE)
```

```
Warning: Ignoring unknown parameters: check.aes
Warning: Ignoring unknown aesthetics: unknown_aes
```

Would you consider a PR that altered `layer()` to look for and honor `check.aes` and `check.param` within its `params` argument?

title: qplot() error with parameters 'span' or 'method'
description:
One issue with qplot() discovered recently.
Following code from vignette (http://docs.ggplot2.org/dev/vignettes/qplot.html) causes and error "Error: Unknown parameters: span"

```
set.seed(1410) # Make the sample reproducible 
dsmall <- diamonds[sample(nrow(diamonds), 100), ]
qplot(carat, price, data = dsmall, geom = c("point", "smooth"), span = 1)
```

The same error is for the 'method' parameter or other.
Example below from the same vignette causes an error "Error: Unknown parameters: method, formula"

```
library(mgcv)
qplot(carat, price, data = dsmall, geom = c("point", "smooth"), method = "gam", formula = y ~ s(x))

```

The source of error is inside the following loop of the qplot() code {after debug(qplot)}:

```
  for (g in geom) {
    params <- arguments[setdiff(names(arguments), c(aes_names, 
      argnames))]
    params <- lapply(params, eval, parent.frame())
    p <- p + do.call(paste0("geom_", g), params) ### THIS LINE CAUSES AN ERROR
  }
```

For some reason(?) in that loop all extra parameters being applied to all geoms including "point", which is incorrect.

This issue is for version 2.1.0 of 'ggplot2', but for 1.0.1 that does not appear.

Regards,
Igor Magdeev

title: facet_grid with an expression cannot have margins

title: Adjusting title and caption to the left side of a whole picture
description:
I have a question on the plot created with ggplot2 package. Let's say we have such a plot:

```
df = data.frame(
  numbers = seq(1,5),
  labels = c(
    "Brand",
    "Good Brand",
    "The Best Brand",
    "The Best Brand Today",
    "The Best Brand This Month"
  )
)
df = df[order(-df$numbers),]
plot = ggplot(data = df, aes(x=labels, y=numbers))+
  geom_bar(stat="identity", fill='orange')+
  coord_flip()+
  labs(
    title = "Exemplary title",
    caption = "Exemplary caption 1\nExemplary caption number 2"
  )+
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = -0.5),
    plot.caption = element_text(hjust = -0.5),
    panel.spacing = unit(c(0,0,0,20), "cm")
  )
plot
```

Is there any better way to align title and caption to the left side of a picture (not plot, but picture, so in this case there where "The best brand in the world" starts), than making negative vjust values for title and caption? 

It is not really the best solution for two reasons:
- if caption has \n character, it is formatted very strangely and seems to be dependent on caption length,
- the title length can change, and therefore the vjust values can change too, so they cannot be constant

title: With facets, data order differs in vectors vs. data frame columns
description:
This is from rstudio/shiny#1432.

In this example, it plots small points on top of large points. The large points get their data from a vector. The small points get their data from a data frame column. The contents of the vector and df column are the same, containing 31 FALSEs and 1 TRUE, so there should be one small red point plotted at the same location as one large red point. But that's not what happens.

``` R
# We'll pick out one of the 32 points 
selected <- rep(FALSE, 32)
selected[32] <- TRUE

# Add that as a column to the data frame
mtc <- mtcars
mtc$sel <- selected

ggplot(mtc, aes(x = cyl,y = mpg)) +
  # Plot large points using the vector
  geom_point(aes(color = selected), size = 5, alpha = 0.4) +
  # Plot small points using the data frame column
  geom_point(aes(color = sel)) +
  facet_grid(. ~ gear) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("black", "red"))
```

![image](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/86978/19502115/30559c22-9570-11e6-8d05-cdc40a917830.png)

Without facets, this problem doesn't seem to happen. And when using a faceting variable with just two levels (`am`, or `carb`), it also doesn't seem to happen.

```
library(shiny)

    iris %>%
      ggplot(aes(x = Sepal.Length

  })

  observeEvent(input$point_Brush, {
    brushedPoints(iris, input$point_Brush)
  })

}

ui <- fluidPage(
  fluidRow(
    plotOutput("distPlot"
               , brush = "point_Brush")

)

shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)
```

title: calling theme_set within a function has side effects outside of the function
description:
Currently, calling `theme_set` within a function will change the theme for plots created outside of that function. For example if I do this

``` r
library(ggplot2)
f <- function() {
  theme_set(theme_classic())
  ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = mpg, y = wt)) + geom_point()
}
f()
```

then the plot looks like I would expect. However I wouldn't expect `theme_classic` to now be the theme for all plots created _outside_ of `f`. For example if I call `f` and then afterwards execute

``` r
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = disp)) + geom_histogram()
```

it will still use `theme_classic` despite the fact that `theme_classic` was set _inside_ the function `f`. Another consequence of this is that if `theme_set` is called inside a package then it seems to affect plots created by other packages unless they are explicitly overriding the theme. 

Anyway, if this is the intended behavior of `theme_set` then I suggest at least documenting it, as I don't see a mention of it at `help("theme_set")`. 

Thanks!

P.S. I know in my example I could define `f` differently (e.g. with `+ theme_classic()` at the end instead of using `theme_set()`)

title: Horizontal bar graphs: Match default stack order in legend as well
description:
According to the [v2.2.0 announcement](https://blog.rstudio.org/2016/09/30/ggplot2-2-2-0-coming-soon/): "position_stack() and position_fill() now stack values in the reverse order of the grouping, which makes the default stack order match the legend." IMHO this should also be true for horizontal bar graphs.

``` r
df <- data.frame(
  x = factor(c(1, 1, 2, 2)),
  y = c(1, 3, 2, 1),
  grp = c("a", "b", "a", "b")
)

ggplot(data = df, aes((x), y, fill = (grp), label = y)) +
  geom_col() +
  geom_text(position = "stack_point") + 
  theme(legend.position = "bottom") +
  coord_flip()
```

![horizontal_bar_graph_order](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/1423562/19145097/90b24b00-8bad-11e6-925f-3a3c53cbdfe4.png)

`position = "stack_point"` borrowed from #1821.

title: Consider using viridis for default continuous color scale

I would consider making viridis the default continuous color scale, or at least making it an option within ggplot2.

title: Add the possibilty for show.legend to be a vector
description:
In `geom_*` functions, the `show.legend` parameter can be either TRUE or FALSE and applies to the whole layer.

When TRUE (the default), lines appear in the legends for `factor(vs)` (`colour`) and `factor(am)` (`linetype`):

``` r
library(ggplot2)

ggplot(mtcars) +
  geom_point(aes(mpg, qsec, colour = factor(vs), shape = factor(am))) + 
  geom_line(aes(mpg, qsec, colour = factor(vs), linetype = factor(am)))
```

![image](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/5540005/18944932/52acf86c-8628-11e6-8b7a-c010900c31ba.png)

When FALSE, lines do not appear in the legend at all:

``` r
ggplot(mtcars) +
  geom_point(aes(mpg, qsec, colour = factor(vs), shape = factor(am))) + 
  geom_line(aes(mpg, qsec, colour = factor(vs), linetype = factor(am)), show.legend = FALSE)
```

![image](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/5540005/18944970/89ab8a40-8628-11e6-8f4f-736dc91bc764.png)

The idea would be to provide a named logical vector to `show.legend` in order to specify which aesthetic are shown in the legend for this layer, like so, where lines appear in the legend for `factor(am)` but not for `factor(vs)`:

``` r
ggplot(mtcars) +
    geom_point(aes(mpg, qsec, colour = factor(vs), shape = factor(am))) + 
    geom_line(aes(mpg, qsec, colour = factor(vs), linetype = factor(am)), 
              show.legend = c(colour = FALSE))
```

![image](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/5540005/18945081/08bf9aec-8629-11e6-9fe6-676fcbe1230e.png)

Please let me know if you think this could be a useful addition. I tried my hand at implementing this ([see here](https://github.com/Tutuchan/ggplot2/commit/c573efa42cab1fab3429b76599121bb633cf54b0)) and this works (except when using `color` instead of `colour`) but I'm sure there is a better way if you decide to implement it.

title: I'm confusing about width(height) argument in geom_jitter()
description:
"width(height)" argument in geom_jitter() is described as [belows.](http://docs.ggplot2.org/current/geom_jitter.html)

> ### **width**
> 
> Amount of vertical and horizontal jitter. The jitter is added in both positive and negative directions, so the total spread is `twice the value specified here`. If omitted, `defaults to 40% of the resolution of the data`: this means the `jitter values will occupy 80%` of the implied bins.

So, I expected `geom_jitter()` and `geom_jitter(width = 0.4)` will produce same plot and `"width = 0.4"` spreads points across a range `"base ± resolution * 0.4"`. but the results are not.

```
> p <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(gear, mpg))
> p + geom_jitter()  ## jitter range is 3 ± 0.4
```

![default](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/22344554/18808390/d0bca7a6-829b-11e6-8b67-10d54c0ea107.png)

```

  stat_summary_bin(fun.y=mean, bins=10, size=5, geom="point", colour="red")
```

It seems like there could be a bug in `stat_summary_bin`, because, as shown in the code below, two y values (from the two rows with the highest x-values) are excluded from the binning and end up in an `NA` bin, which is the one plotted to the right of the data bins in the plot above. title: Add box around text elements
description:
Specifically, I want to be able to add a box around axis and plot labels similar to those in facets. The facet details are set with the `strip*` elements which include `strip.background` which allows using `element_rect` to set things including a background color. `title*` and `axis.title*` elements,  do not allow `background` or allow setting a fill color.

However, the `debug` option _does_ set a background, showing that it is relatively straightforward to do, though handling edge cases may be tricky.

The motivating example is in response to this [Stack Overflow question](http://stackoverflow.com/questions/39246219/r-ggplot-multiple-grouping-in-x-axis) where I [answered ](http://stackoverflow.com/questions/39246219/r-ggplot-multiple-grouping-in-x-axis/39249251#39249251) using `cowplot` but would have liked to use a box behind each of the x-axis titles to more clearly denote their grouping. This would be more important with more groups (e.g., if each set had 4 elements, it may not be clear which belong where).

One solution would be to extend faceting to nest multiple layers, but that seems very difficult to conceive of a consistent grammar to ensure proper nesting in all cases. Alternatively, it should be possible to either add a `title.background`, `axis.title.background`, `axis.title.background.y`, and `axis.title.background.x`  elements.

Or, more simply to extend `element_text` to allow a `fill` option, though this may cause other ripples that I am unaware of.

I will try to fiddle with the last approach, but if anyone has suggestions (or has already worked on this), please let me know. Similarly, if this is a bad idea or already implemented in a more elegant way that I am just missing, please let me know.

Code to create the plot:

```
library(ggplot2)
library(cowplot)
library(dplyr)

#return to default theme
theme_set(theme_gray())

df <- read.table(text = "X    year  month  sum
10   2016  1      450
10   2016  2      670
10   2017  1      200
11   2016  1      460
11   2017  2      500", header = T)

# Notice the variable type for month and year
df$month <- as.factor(df$month)
df$year <- as.factor(df$year)
df$X <- as.factor(df$X)


# Save y limits to get same scale
myYlims <- c(0, ceiling(max(df$sum)/100)*100)


# Generate each plot
x10 <-
  ggplot(df %>%
           filter(X == 10)
         , aes(x = month, y = sum)) + geom_bar(stat = "identity") + 
  facet_grid(~ year,
             switch = "x") +
  panel_border() +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = myYlims) +
  xlab("X = 10")


x11 <-
  ggplot(df %>%
           filter(X == 11)
         , aes(x = month, y = sum)) + geom_bar(stat = "identity") + 
  facet_grid(~ year,
             switch = "x") +
  panel_border() +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = myYlims) +
  xlab("X = 11")


# Put the plots together
plot_grid(x10
          , x11 +
            theme(axis.title.y = element_blank()
                  , axis.text.y = element_blank()
                  , axis.ticks.y = element_blank()
            )
          , rel_widths = c(1.1,1)
)
```

And code to create it with the `debug` option showing the box behind the titles:

```
plot_grid(x10 +
            theme(axis.title.x = element_text(debug = TRUE))
          , x11 +
            theme(axis.title.y = element_blank()
                  , axis.text.y = element_blank()
                  , axis.ticks.y = element_blank()
                  , axis.title.x = element_text(debug = TRUE)
            )
          , rel_widths = c(1.1,1)
          )
```

title: geom_smooth assumes that the LHS of its model formula is just y
description:
`predictdf`, which is called by `stat_smooth`, returns a data frame with a sequence of `x` values, and the model predictions as the column `y`. It thereby assumes that `y` is what's on the left-hand side of the model formula. The following example thus produces an unexpected result:

``` R
x <- 0:3
qplot(x, 1 + x) + geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y - 1 ~ x + 0)
```

To get the correct result, the inverse function of the LHS with respect to y needs to be applied to the model prediction. It is, however, not in general possible to determine this inverse function; in fact, the LHS might not be invertible at all. I would therefore propose to emit a warning when the LHS of the `formula` parameter to `stat_smooth` is not just `y`, and require the user to specify the inverse function (e. g., for the above example, something like `geom_smooth(..., inv = function (pred) (pred + 1)`).

I'm also wondering if there are use cases for other variables than `y` on the LHS (in which case the inverse function would need to return a data frame), but this concern is probably artificial.

title: non-standard params / geom-specific metadata
description:
Hello, this is continuing the discussion from https://github.com/hadley/ggplot2/pull/1649 and https://github.com/hadley/ggplot2/issues/1585 our equivalent animint issue is https://github.com/tdhock/animint/issues/159

For https://github.com/tdhock/animint we need some way of specifying `chunk_vars` which is a geom-specific parameter that has nothing to do with how it appears. With old ggplot2 (pre-2.0) the following was working fine

``` r
ggplot()+
  geom_point(aes(Sepal.Length, Petal.Length, showSelected=Species),
    data=iris, 
    chunk_vars=character())
```

With current ggplot2 that now results in an error

```
Error: Unknown parameters: chunk_vars
```

Basically we just need a way for ggplot2 to store that information in the geom, ideally without throwing any errors/warnings/messages. The use case is described by @faizan-khan-iit 's excellent test case from his PR https://github.com/hadley/ggplot2/pull/1649/commits/017b0f3d753a93458e89a67c40593574b82491b5 -- we want the geom to store whatever information is provided in those non-standard parameters, so it can be accessed later by our animint code.

One way to achieve this would be to use Faizan's `validate_params=FALSE` method https://github.com/hadley/ggplot2/pull/1649 but that PR was rejected by @hadley 

Let me propose another way:

``` r
l <- geom_point(aes(Sepal.Length, Petal.Length, showSelected=Species), 
    data=iris, 
    meta=list(chunk_vars=character()))
```

`meta` should be recognized by ggplot2 as a special meta-data parameter (no warnings or messages about meta being an unknown parameter). whatever was specified as `meta` should be accessible via `l$meta` Comments?

title: Add option for "impartial binning" for histograms
description:
Traditionally (i.e., in `hist()`) one must choose between left-leaning and right-leaning binning with `right = FALSE` or `right = TRUE`.  A more balanced option would be to allow `right = 0.5`.  Under this option, data values exactly on a bin border would count has 0.5 in the bin to the left and 0.5 in the bin to the right.

Naive implementation is easy: 

``` r
newcounts <- 
  right       * hist(..., right =  TRUE)$counts + 
  (1 - right) * hist(..., right = FALSE)$counts
```

This would work for other values of `right` a well, although it is less clear that other values are useful.  Setting `right = TRUE` or `right = FALSE` still works as before (although less efficiently).

title: Objects useful in ggplot2 extensions that are not currently exported
description:
I'm working on a ggplot2 extension called [colorplaner](https://github.com/wmurphyrd/colorplaner) that allows for visualization of two variables in a single plotted color through color space projections. 
The extension includes a new scale ggproto with two constructor functions, a new guide S3 class with methods, and two new aesthetics. 

Basing my code of off existing ggplot2 code, I've come across several objects in ggplot2 that are quite useful but are not currently exported:
- RangeContinuous
- check_breaks_labels
- element_render
- ggname
- is.waive

They are mostly convenience wrappers that I could recreate, but there could be value in keeping them synchronized with ggplot2, and, of course, accessing them via `:::` triggers a note in R CMD check. Would you consider a pull request to make these exported objects? Or perhaps I could make the case to CRAN that it's acceptable as the package is an extension of the one of which it is poking around in the private namespace. 
## New aesthetics

Given that my scale combines two variables into a single aesthetic mapping, I needed a way to access that second variable from within the Scale's map_df method. The best option I came up with that kept the syntax and behavior consistent with the rest of ggplot2 was to add two new options for aesthetics, `colour2` and `fill2`. Doing so required modifying `ggplot2:::.all_aesthetics` (and `ggplot2:::.base_to_ggplot` to enable the `color2` alias), which I do in in my package's [onLoad](https://github.com/wmurphyrd/colorplaner/blob/master/R/zzz.R) function via `unlockBinding` and `assign`, but this leads to another CMD check note for potentially unsafe code. Would you consider a pull request with a function that enables the addition of new aesthetics?

Thanks!

title: Add asymmetrical `expand` argument to continuous and discrete scales
description:
This is a feature request for an asymmetrical `expand` argument to the `scale_continuous` and `scale_discrete` scales. A typical use case would be for bar plots that touch the _x_ axis but still have some space above them. For example

```
ggplot(mtcars) + 
  geom_bar(aes(x = cyl))
```

has some space above the bars, but also an annoying spaces below it. Now,

```
ggplot(mtcars) + 
  geom_bar(aes(x = cyl)) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0, 0))
```

gets rid of the space below the bars, but also the space above the bars. To keep the space above the bars, one has to use a hack with a manually calculated value:

```
ggplot(mtcars) + 
  geom_bar(aes(x = cyl)) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0, 0)) +
  annotate("blank", x = 6, y = 14.7)
```

(And this doesn’t work well with more complicated plots, e.g. involving facets with `free_y` &c.)

Suggested feature/syntax: Change the `expand` argument from

```
expand = c(a, b)
```

to

```
expand = c(a, b, c, d)
```

where `a` is the multiplier for the lower limit, `b` is the additive term for the lower limit, and `c` and `d` are the corresponding multiplier and additive term for the upper limit. If `c` is missing, use the value of `a`, and if `d` is missing, use the value of `b`. This way, all old code would continue to work.

See http://stackoverflow.com/questions/34623780/asymmetric-expansion-of-limits-ggplot2-2-0 for more information. This post also has suggested code for an asymmetrical `expand` feature, but this does not work for complicated facet grids, nor with `coord_flip()`.

Here's the rationale for [the new docs from yhat](http://blog.yhat.com/posts/new-ggplot.html):

> One thing we realized with previously released of ggplot was that the documentation wasn't right. We added docs for every geom, tried making function docstrings more descriptive, and even making the docs prettier. Unfortunately, none of this really worked. What we realized was that while we were adding more documentation, it was all API driven (i.e. describing how individual functions worked). When what people really needed help with was how to do particular tasks using ggplot (i.e. "How do I make a histogram?").
> 
> So with the new release we're taking a more task-oriented approach to our docs. That means lots of "How To's", loads of examples, and very visual docs. The new docs use jupyter notebooks, which makes it really easy to contribute examples and update for new releases changes.

title: Strange scale_*_datetime / breaks / date_breaks timezone offset (cf. #824)
description:
When setting `breaks` in a `scale_x_datetime` (or `scale_y_datetime`), ticks on the axis end up shifted by a certain number of hours.

Issue previously described and workaround suggested at: https://github.com/hadley/ggplot2/issues/824

Workaround: set the timezone explicitly in every use of as.POSIX\* function.

Example: the following code generates shifted graphs:

```
library(ggplot2)
library(scales)

mydata <- ... as.POSIXct("12:34:56", format = "%H:%M:%S")) ...

ggplot(mydata, ...) +
   scale_y_datetime(limits = c(as.POSIXct("00:00:00", format = "%H:%M:%S"),
                              as.POSIXct("23:59:59", format = "%H:%M:%S")),
                   breaks = seq(as.POSIXct("00:00:00", format = "%H:%M:%S"),
                                as.POSIXct("24:00:00", format = "%H:%M:%S"),
                                6*3600),
                   labels = date_format("%H:%M")) + 
   ...
```

The following variant generates correct graphs (assuming using the local timezone is correct):

```
mydata <- ... as.POSIXct("12:34:56", format = "%H:%M:%S", tz=Sys.timezone())) ...

ggplot(mydata, ...) +
   scale_y_datetime(limits = c(as.POSIXct("00:00:00", format = "%H:%M:%S", tz=Sys.timezone()),
                              as.POSIXct("23:59:59", format = "%H:%M:%S", tz=Sys.timezone())),
                   breaks = seq(as.POSIXct("00:00:00", format = "%H:%M:%S", tz=Sys.timezone()),
                                as.POSIXct("24:00:00", format = "%H:%M:%S", tz=Sys.timezone()),
                                6*3600),
                   labels = date_format("%H:%M", tz=Sys.timezone())) + 
...
```

title: Use same smoother by default in all facets
description:
Currently, the default smoother depends on the number of points (loess for <=1000 observations, gam for >1000).  When used in in conjunction with faceting, this calculation is done for each facet separately. That means that different facets can use different smoothers within the same plot, invalidating (or at least making more tenuous) comparison of curves between the facets.

Please enforce a single default-smoother selection across all facets in a plot.

title: Logarithmic data in a heatmap & accessing the grobs of ggplot2 legends
description:
# Logarithmic data in a heatmap & accessing the grobs of ggplot2 legends
## my question:

Is there still a nice way to convert all the graphic objects of the ggplot2 to a gTree for editing?
## my suggestion:

I use a logarithmic scale in more than half of the figures I produce during my research so I would love to have the support for this transformation on the whole real line in the plots. And of course I'm also willingly to contribute for this.
## the problem

Lets assume we want to plot data ranging from negative to positive values drawn from a long tailed distribution using a heatmap.

``` r
library( ggplot2 )
library( extRemes )
series.length <- 40
x.data <- y.data <- 1 : series.length
intensity.data <- extRemes::revd( n = series.length^ 2, 0, 100, -.2, type = "GEV" )

plot.data <- data.frame( x = expand.grid( x.data, y.data )[ , 1 ],
                        y = expand.grid( x.data, y.data )[ , 2 ],
                        intensity = intensity.data )
ggplot( data = plot.data, aes( x = x, y = y, fill = intensity ) ) + geom_tile()
```

Usually the bulk of the data is quite interesting but the plot is dominated by the bigger values. Therefore its common to plot them data using a logarithmic scale.
## solution using the alpha value

Since its not possible to perform the logarithm on negative data one has to use the absolute value or have to plot the positive and the negative part separately (using distinct sets of colors.) One way of doing this I found in forums and blogs is using the alpha value of a block in the heatmap to encode the information.

``` r
plot.data.2 <- plot.data
plot.data.2$sign <- "pos"
plot.data.2$sign[ plot.data.2$intensity < 0 ] <- "neg"
plot.data.2$intensity <- abs( plot.data.2$intensity )
ggplot( data = plot.data.2, aes( x = x, y = y, alpha = intensity, fill = sign ) ) + geom_tile() +
    scale_alpha( trans = "log" ) + scale_fill_manual( values = c( "red", "blue" ) )

```

**Issue:**  
- This is not really the most beautiful way of representing the data  
- Its more complicated because there are two legends now  
- The legend for the alpha value is misleading since its a continuous quantity and not a discrete one (and I don't know how to change this)
## my solution by combining two plots

Instead I perform two different plots: one logarithmic for the positive values while setting all negative to NA and one for the absolute values of the negative data while setting all positive to NA. Then I combine all fill values after removing the NA contributions and finally I "combine" the legends using different viewports.

``` r
## Plot of the positive values
plot.data.pos <- plot.data.neg <- plot.data
plot.data.pos$intensity[ plot.data.pos$intensity < 0 ] <- NA
plot.data.neg$intensity[ plot.data.neg$intensity > 0 ] <- NA
plot.data.neg$intensity <- abs( plot.data.neg$intensity ) 
gg1 <- ggplot( data = plot.data.pos, aes( x = x, y = y, fill = intensity ) ) + geom_tile() +
    scale_fill_gradientn( trans = "log", colours = RColorBrewer::brewer.pal( 6, "Blues" ),
                         na.value = "#000000", label = function( x ) {
                             options( digits = 2 )
                             format( x, scientific = TRUE ) } )
##3 Plot of the negative values
gg2 <- ggplot( data = plot.data.neg, aes( x = x, y = y, fill = intensity ) ) + geom_tile() +
    scale_fill_gradientn( trans = "log", colours = RColorBrewer::brewer.pal( 6, "Reds" ),
                         na.value = "#000000", label = function( x ) {
                             options( digits = 2 )
                             format( -x, scientific = TRUE ) } ) +
    guides( fill = guide_colourbar( reverse = TRUE, title = element_blank() ) )
ggcomb <- gg1 + guides( fill = FALSE )

## combining the fills of the two plots
ggcomb.build <- ggplot_build( ggcomb )
gg2.build <- ggplot_build( gg2 )
ggcomb.fill <- ggcomb.build$data[[ 1 ]]$fill # Fill values for all boxes in the heatmap
gg2.fill <- gg2.build$data[[ 1 ]]$fill
ggcomb.fill[ ggcomb.fill == "#000000" ] <- gg2.fill[ gg2.fill != "#000000" ] #combination
ggcomb.build$data[[ 1 ]]$fill <- ggcomb.fill
ggcomb <- ggplot_gtable( ggcomb.build )

## extracting the legends
legend.1 <- ggplotGrob( gg1 )$grobs[[ 8 ]]
legend.2 <- ggplot_gtable( gg2.build )$grobs[[ 8 ]]

## plotting both the legends and the combined heatmap
grid.newpage()
top.viewport <- viewport( 
    layout = grid.layout( 4, 2, width = unit( c( 1, 5 ), c( "null", "lines" ) ),
                         height = unit( c( 1, 7, 7, 1 ),
                                       c( "null", "lines", "lines", "null" ) ) ) )
heatmap.vp <- viewport( layout.pos.col = 1, layout.pos.row = 1 : 4,
                       name = "heatmap.vp" )
legend.1.vp <- viewport( layout.pos.col = 2, layout.pos.row = 2, name = "legend.1.vp" )
legend.2.vp <- viewport( layout.pos.col = 2, layout.pos.row = 3, name = "legend.2.vp" )
pushViewport( vpTree( top.viewport, vpList( heatmap.vp, legend.1.vp, legend.2.vp ) ) )
seekViewport( "heatmap.vp" )
grid.draw( ggcomb )
seekViewport( "legend.1.vp" )
grid.draw( legend.1 )
seekViewport( "legend.2.vp" )
grid.draw( legend.2 )

```

Looks quite good up to this point and certainly better than the alpha value solution.
## accessing the grobs of the legends

But one thing is bothering me: _I would love to have a solid scale in the legend_.

I tried a lot using ggplotGrob() and read a lot about the underlying grid grob concept. But unfortunately the grobs in the ggplot2 plot are not nicely represented as a gTree object so I can't just take the legend of the negative plot and place it seamlessly below the plot of the positive data.

I found this [https://github.com/hadley/ggplot2/wiki/Editing-raw-grid-objects-from-a-ggplot](description for editing the raw objects) but its deprecated and does not work anymore.

Cheers,
Philipp

![image](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/509878/15122624/f98a7b56-15ed-11e6-8a91-7f5e09233366.png)

(there are others out there with that y-axis-title style and also x-axis ones on lower-right but inside)

this is becoming a new "thing" and—while it's not hard to do with `geom_text|label()` might there be an appetite for

Opening up a discussion more than anything else.

title: geom_contour throws error when ggplot aes uses shape
description:
Hi,
the following code

```
library(ggplot2)

testPts <- transform(expand.grid(x=1:10,y=1:5),z=sin(x*y))
testPts$z2 <- as.numeric(testPts$z > 0.5)
testPts$z3 <- as.factor(testPts$z2)

ggplot(data=testPts, aes(x, y, z=z, colour=z, shape=z3)) + geom_point() + 
  geom_contour(data=testPts, aes(x, y, z=z2), colour="blue")
```

produces the error

```
Warning messages:
1: Not possible to generate contour data 
2: In grDevices::contourLines(x = sort(unique(data$x)), y = sort(unique(data$y)),  :
  all z values are equal
3: Not possible to generate contour data 
```

while the following code (with shape=NULL) works fine

```
ggplot(data=testPts, aes(x, y, z=z, colour=z, shape=z3)) + geom_point() + 
  geom_contour(data=testPts, aes(x, y, z=z2, shape=NULL), colour="blue")
```

When I detected the error, I had different data in ggplot and geom_contour. Using testPts in both is just for simplification.
Watch out for the different z-Values in both.
I think geom_contour should work regardless of the shape of ggplot. At least the error message is confusing.
Best Regards
Hans

title: data used in geom_text with geom specific aes is longer than it should be?
description:
The following code is should print a label once, but it seems that it prints the label as many times as the original passed in data.frame was long.

``` R
data = data.frame(x=seq(1:400))

library("ggplot2")
temp <- paste("Deuterium~D", "[", "alpha", "]")

p <- ggplot( data=data) +
  geom_text(aes( 656, 0.5, label = temp), parse=TRUE)
p  + coord_cartesian(xlim=c(0,4000), ylim=c(0.0,1.0)) 
p
```

title: Design query - connectograms
description:
Hello,
I'm exploring designs for connectogram plots. ggbio does the right kind of thing but is tightly bound to the various bioconductor structures. I'd like to implement the same kind of capabilities for more general data. I've seen some discussion about connectograms and polar plots, but the results are not as nice.

The ggbio approach has functions that transform the data and then returns calls to the various geoms. This approach means that the geoms have access to the circular versions of the data and can figure out the scales, but it doesn't seem to be nice from the ggplot design point of view.

However, as it is necessary to transform the data to draw the circular segments, it seems difficult to fit the concept into a geom. I've done some experiments, but the problem is the axes are derived from the original data. I can see that there may be an avenue via adding a coordinate transform, but thought I'd make this query to see if you have any advice or know of similar examples.

Thanks

title: [Feature Request] different scales by facet
description:
This feature request first shows a ggplot2 limitation through an example and then it proposes a syntax change to the `scale_*` functions to overcome the scale limitation. The syntax change is designed so it feels natural to ggplot2 users. No implementation is provided, as I don't know if this syntax has chances to be merged and I would need some pointers to tackle the implementation as cleanly as possible. Discussion/help/comments are welcome.
## Current ggplot2 limitation

Faceted plots in ggplot2 apparently require the same scale parameters. This means that it is impossible to plot a percentage (`scale_y_continuous(labels=scales::percent_format())`) and a scientific number (`scale_y_continuous(labels=scales::scientific_format())`) on the same axis but different facet.

This is not a [new issue (2010)](https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/ggplot2/cDzL_yHew0I) but I have not seen any solution on that thread.

This issue is better described in an example:

``` r
library(dplyr)
library(scales)
library(ggplot2)

# Simple tidy data frame, with 4 subjects. We measure three variables on each
# subject (namely: SomeValue, Percent and Scientific).
mydf <- dplyr::data_frame(Subject=rep(c("Alice", "Bob", "Charlie", "Diane"), each=3),
                          Magnitude=rep(c("SomeValue", "Percent", "Scientific"), times=4),
                          Value=c(c(170,0.6,2.7E-4),
                                  c(180, 0.8, 2.5E-4),
                                  c(160, 0.71, 3.2E-4),
                                  c(159, 0.62, 3E-4)),
                          Gender=rep(c("Female", "Male", "Male", "Female"), each=3))

# This is how the df looks like:
head(mydf)
#  Subject  Magnitude   Value Gender
#1   Alice  SomeValue 1.7e+02 Female
#2   Alice    Percent 6.0e-01 Female
#3   Alice Scientific 2.7e-04 Female
#4     Bob  SomeValue 1.8e+02   Male
#5     Bob    Percent 8.0e-01   Male
#6     Bob Scientific 2.5e-04   Male

# Here the percent (top) is well written, the other ones don't make sense
ggplot(mydf) +
  geom_point(aes(x=Subject, y=Value, color=Gender)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels=scales::percent_format()) +
  #scale_y_continuous(labels=waiver()) +
  #scale_y_continuous(labels=scales::scientific_format()) +
  facet_grid(Magnitude~., scales = "free" )
```

![f1](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/75441/14569824/4427febe-0341-11e6-9796-cd896b20c93c.png)
# Proposal

The syntax I would like to suggest is to allow to pass `data` and `mapping` parameters to the scale functions (here `scale_y_continuous`) that would map the scale arguments to each facet.

``` r
# Proposed solution syntax. Define a data frame with the facet variable
# and the arguments we want to use:
myscales <- dplyr::data_frame(Magnitude = c("SomeValue", 
                                            "Percent",
                                            "Scientific"),
                              labels = list(waiver(),
                                            scales::percent_format(),
                                            scales::scientific_format()))
head(myscales)
# Source: local data frame [3 x 2]
#
#   Magnitude      labels
#1  SomeValue <S3:waiver>
#2    Percent   <fnct[1]>
#3 Scientific   <fnct[1]>

# Change scale_y_continuous to accept data and aes:
ggplot(mydf) +
  geom_point(aes(x=Subject, y=Value, color=Gender)) +
  scale_y_continuous(data=myscales, mapping=aes(labels=labels)) + # Needs implementation
  facet_grid(Magnitude~., scales = "free" )
```
- I find this syntax familiar (like `geom_*` functions) and tidy.
- I think it is backwards compatible with the existing arguments.
- I do not know how hard it may be its implementation given the current ggplot2 design.

title: annotate() won't expand when position aesthetics are length 1
description:
Min reprex:

```
ggplot() + 
  annotate("text", x = 1, y = 1, label = c("a", "b"))
# Error: Aesthetics must be either length 1 or the same as the data (1): label
```

I am not sure whether it is intentional or not, but it seems the test for lengths only includes the position vectors, when it is reasonable that non position vectors may vary. (Also the error message can be a bit opaque.)

I encountered this issue when debugging some code where the distinction between position and non-position vectors in this test wasn't clear. But a possible genuine application could be a compass rose:

`ggplot() + annotate("text", x = 0, y = 0, label = c("N", "S", "E", "W"), hjust = c(0.5, 0.5, 0, 1), vjust = c(0, 1, 0.5, 0.5))`

title: X axis doesn't appear below facet_wrap plot with uneven number of facets
description:
When drawing a plot with facet_wrap. If there is an uneven number of facets, the x axis is not drawn for facets which do not touch the "floor" of the plotting area. For example 

```
ggplot(airquality, aes(x = Day, y = Temp)) +
    facet_wrap(~Month) + 
    geom_line()
```

![airquality_facet_wrap](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/5647397/14382482/6cfef90e-fd8e-11e5-98ea-be37fbe4149c.png)

It's possible to add an axis under all plots by setting the scales argument to "free_x". 

```
ggplot(airquality, aes(x = Day, y = Temp)) +
    facet_wrap(~Month, scales = "free_x") + 
    geom_line()
```

![airquatlity_facet_wrap_free_x](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/5647397/14382542/da62460e-fd8e-11e5-8aa3-6379a7157fac.png)

But it's not possible to add an x axis only for the last dangling plot alone. This axis could be located in two places, right below the dangling plot: 

![airquality_facet_wrap_dangling_above](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/5647397/14382827/06edbe18-fd91-11e5-9de8-d95a02dbf388.png)

or at the bottom of the plotting area:

![airquality_facet_wrap_dangling_below](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/5647397/14382832/0dbe0f36-fd91-11e5-9377-f01093405ea3.png)

A workaround was given in [this Stackoverflow answer](http://stackoverflow.com/a/13316126/2641825). The author said a suggestion could be submitted here. 2 years after those comments were made on Stackoverflow, no suggestion has been submitted here on github. Considering the number of votes on the workaround answer, the issue still attracts interest. I thought I'd request your feedback. Could this feature be implemented, with minimal change to ggplot2, or is this out of the question?

title: stat_bin_2d creates an (almost) unkillable legend.
description:
Using stat_bin_2d to summarise and plot points creates _TWO_ guides - one for size (as expected), and one for colour (not expected)

`
ggplot(data=mtcars, aes(cyl, am)) + 
  stat_bin_2d(aes (size=..count..), geom='point')
`

An attempt to turn off the guide for both colour and size  aesthetic only removes the size guide, but not the colour guide.
`
ggplot(data=mtcars, aes(cyl, am)) + 
  stat_bin_2d(aes (size=..count..), geom='point', show.legend=FALSE)
`

Disabling via 'guides()' finally does the trick.
`
ggplot(data=mtcars, aes(cyl, am)) + 
  stat_bin_2d(aes (size=..count..), geom='point', show.legend=FALSE) + 
  guides(fill=FALSE)
`

title: Facets break grouping of data points
description:
Using facets seems to ignore the correct grouping of data points for variables in the global environment:

Generate data (x, y), two distinct groups:

``` R
library(ggplot2)
n = 10
x = c(rnorm(n), rnorm(n, 5))
y = c(rnorm(n), rnorm(n, 5))
group = rep(c("a", "b"), each = n)
```

Randomize the order of data points and assignment to the respective groups:

``` R
idx = sample.int(length(x))
x_s = x[idx]
y_s = y[idx]
group_s = group[idx]
```

Irrespective of the order of data points, I would expect to get a plot where color and facets distinguish the two groups of data points:

![expected](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/302566/14234121/cf11d536-f9d2-11e5-9289-704cc6b208c0.png)

This is returned both by

``` R
qplot(x, y, color = group, facets = ~group)
```

``` R
df = data.frame(x = y_s, y = y_s, group = group_s)
qplot(x, y, color = group, facets = ~group, data = df)
```

However, the assignment is incorrect when the "shuffled" data is taken from the global environment: 

``` R
qplot(x_s, y_s, color = group_s, facets = ~group_s)
```

![observed](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/302566/14234123/d73f0800-f9d2-11e5-8e81-f1d5eadf6e9b.png)

Using facets causes the problem here, color has just been added in the examples for better illustration and can also be omitted for reproducing the example. It seems to me that the ordering of the facet variable is not correctly taken into account in the last example. The issue is reproducible with ggplot2 2.1.0 and the latest github master.

title: [Feature Request] allow customized spacing for legend items
description:
Consider adding two-ish arguments to guide(guide_legend()) that allow the
users to control the spacing between
1. the key and the label and
2. between key-label pairs

The second request is discussed here:
[stackoverflow: change spacing between legend items](http://stackoverflow.com/questions/11366964/is-there-a-way-to-change-the-spacing-between-legend-items-in-ggplot2)

Here is a working example:

``` R
# build silly data.frame
temp <- data.frame("year"=rep(2000:2010, 2), 
"category"=c(rep("puppies", 11), rep("kittens", 11)), 
"smiles"=c(ceiling(runif(11)*100), ceiling(runif(11)*80)))

# stacked area plot
ggplot(temp, aes(x=year, y=smiles)) + geom_area(aes(group=category, fill=category), position="stack") + 
ggtitle("Which Critter Gets the Most Smiles?") + xlab("Year") + ylab("Smiles") + labs(fill="Critter") + 
scale_color_discrete(name="Smiles") +
guides(fill=guide_legend(title.position="top", keywidth=0.2, keyheight=0.2, default.unit="inch")) +
theme(legend.text = element_text(size=10), legend.title = element_text(size=12), legend.position="bottom", legend.title.align=0.5)
```

Each key and legend label are fairly close to one another and it would be great to add some padding in between. More importantly, the key-label pairs are somewhat squished together. The winning stackoverflow answer is to add additional spaces to the end of the kitten elements: "kitten" -> "kitten<4 spaces>". While this hack works, in addressing the second issue it does not seem optimal.

title: Document behavior of fill order in geom_bar when stat = "identity"
description:
One of the most commonly asked questions about ggplot is how to order categorical aesthetics, and the answer is has traditionally been to specify the order in the factor levels.

With the most recent version this has changed for (at least) the case of `geom_bar` when `stat = "identity"` and either `position = "stack"` or `position = "fill"`. Instead, to ensure that the filled segments in a stacked/filled bar plot are in a specified order we must now have the data frame sorted in the desired order.

This should probably at least be documented in the Details section of `?geom_bar`, with a brief note along the lines of:

> To adjust the order of the levels of the fill aesthetic when using `stat = "identity"` and either `position = "stack"` or `position = "fill"` the data itself must be arranged in the desired order. Adjusting the order of the factor levels no longer has any effect in these cases.

Here's a very minimal example demonstrating this behavior:

```
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)

dat <- data.frame(x = rep(1:2,each = 3),
                 y = 1:6,
                 f = rep(letters[1:3],times = 2))
dat$f1 <- with(dat,factor(f,levels = c('c','b','a')))

dat

#Original
ggplot() +
    geom_bar(data = dat,
             aes(x = factor(x),y = y,fill = f),
             stat = "identity",
             position = "stack")

#Fill colors have changed, but not order of segments
ggplot() +
    geom_bar(data = dat,
             aes(x = factor(x),y = y,fill = f1),
             stat = "identity",
             position = "stack")

#Reorder data frame
dat <- arrange(dat,x,desc(f))
dat

#Now the order changed
ggplot() +
    geom_bar(data = dat,
             aes(x = factor(x),y = y,fill = f),
             stat = "identity",
             position = "stack")
```

The same behavior occurs when `position = "fill"`.

title: Allow geoms to ignore some set aesthetics
description:
Let us say I want to combine a few geoms to make a specific plot, I can define such a function:

``` r
library("ggplot2")

d <- data.frame(x=rnorm(10), y=rnorm(10), a=letters[1:10])

my_plot <- function(data, mapping, ...) {
  ggplot() +
    geom_line(data=data, mapping=mapping, ...) +
    geom_point(data=data, mapping=mapping, ...)
}

my_plot(d, aes(x=x, y=y))
```

But then, if I want to change the linetype, `geom_point` throws an error because `linetype` is meaningless for it:

``` r
my_plot(d, aes(x=x, y=y), linetype="dashed")
```

```
Error: Unknown parameters: linetype
```

If I recall correctly, this was just silently ignored in the past. Interestingly, mapped aesthetics do not throw this error:

``` r
my_plot(d, aes(x=x, y=y, linetype="dashed"))
```

But the result is pretty useless of course ;-). A more useful example would be

``` r
my_plot <- function(data, mapping, ...) {
  ggplot() +
    geom_line(data=data, mapping=mapping, ...) +
    geom_point(data=data, mapping=mapping, ...) +
    geom_text(data=data, mapping=mapping, ...)
}
my_plot(d, aes(x=x, y=y, label=a))
```

Still moving the text up is not possible after the fact, with something like:

``` r
my_plot(d, aes(x=x, y=y, label=a), vjust=0)
```

I understand the rationale in telling the user explicitly about useless aesthetics, _but_:
- I think throwing an _error_ is a bit too much, a warning would be enough. Stopping the execution of the function makes it very cumbersome to use ggplot programmatically to build new visualisations (the "proper" way may be to build new geoms but this requires a lot of sophistication for a simple goal).
- Alternatively (or in addition) there should be a way to easily bypass the warning/errors, through an argument, FALSE by default (if a warning is used, the person creating the function can also wrap the call in `suppressWarnings` and that would help).
- This should be consistent between _set_ and _mapped_ aesthetics (but probably ignore useless _inherited_ aesthetics without warning).

PS: The rationale for this comment is that I often combine geoms in `autoplot`  but want to retain the flexibility of mapping/setting aesthetics from the higher level function.

title: NAs should be excluded from the level of discrete X-axis by default
description:
When the variable for `x` is character, `NA`s are not treated as a break of X axis. But when the variable is factor, `NA`s are included.

``` r
library(ggplot2)

set.seed(1)
d <- c("A", "B", NA)
x <- sample(d, size = 100, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.7, 0.2, 0.1))
y <- rnorm(100)
df <- data.frame(x, y)

ggplot(df) + geom_boxplot(aes(x, y), na.rm = TRUE)

ggplot(df) + geom_boxplot(aes(as.character(x), y), na.rm = TRUE)
```

![na_included](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/1978793/13749315/23048e20-ea44-11e5-96a3-722a2d8e120b.png) ![na_not_included](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/1978793/13749319/25cdc0a4-ea44-11e5-974a-e73b9efb4664.png)

I feel this behaviour is inconsistent. `NA`s should be included only when `NA` is intentionally included in the level of the factor variable.

``` r
levels(df$x)
[1] "A" "B"
```

I guess this is simply because `scales:::clevels()` treats them differently. But, I'm wondering if this is by design... Why do we have to force `NA`s included, while we can include `NA` in the factor level by ourselves?

``` r
set.seed(1)
d <- c("A", "B", NA)
x <- sample(d, size = 100, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.7, 0.2, 0.1))

scales:::clevels(x, drop = FALSE)
#> [1] "A" "B"

scales:::clevels(as.factor(x), drop = FALSE)
#> [1] "A" "B" NA 
```

Is it possible to eliminate NA from factor X-axis by default? (But I'm afraid this suggestion is too late and many people may already rely on this behaviour)

title: Possible bug in default method for geom_smooth
description:
It looks like the default method in geom_smooth is chosen by the number of rows in dataframe, not by the number of rows of data used to create the smoothed line. The example below should clarify the problem.
# Generate some noisy time series

set.seed(1)
z = data.frame("Index"=1:101, "Person"=rep(letters[1:10], each=101), "Distance"=as.vector(replicate(10, rnorm(101) + cumsum(rnorm(101)))))
# Plot smoothed lines for ALL of the time series
# geom_smooth uses method gam

library(ggplot2)
ggplot(data=z, aes(x=Index, y=Distance)) + geom_smooth() + facet_wrap(~Person)
# Plot smoothed lines for 9 out of 10 of the time series (so fewer than 1000 rows in the data)
# geom_smooth uses method loess

win.graph()
ggplot(data=subset(z, Person!="j"), aes(x=Index, y=Distance)) + geom_smooth() + facet_wrap(~Person, ncol=4)

Notice that the smoothed lines look different in the two charts. That's because if you use geom_smooth on the whole dataframe z, then it defaults to method gam, even though each facet where we are drawing the smoothed line has far fewer than 1000 rows of data. If you look at a subset of z with only 909 rows, it defaults to loess. 

Once you see what is going on this problem is easy to correct (just specify the method in the geom_smooth function) but it took me a long time to figure out. Is it possible for the default method used by geom_smooth to be based on the # of rows of data actually used for the line, not for all the dataframe i.e. taking faceting and grouping into account? It might save someone some trouble in the future.

title: stat_summary error when trying to pass function argument as parameter, rather than hard-coding
description:
I'm getting an error when I try to pass a parameter into the `round` function within `stat_summary` (even though the analogous code works with, say, `geom_text`). Here's an example:

```
# Fake data
set.seed(5)
dat = data.frame(group=rep(c("A","B"),each=10), val=rnorm(20))

# Set the number of decimal places for value labels using a parameter, rather than hard-coding it:
places = 2

ggplot(dat, aes(group, val)) +
  stat_summary(fun.y=mean, geom="text", aes(label=round(..y.., places)))
```

> Error in eval(expr, envir, enclos) : object 'places' not found

The following two examples work fine, however.

```
ggplot(dat, aes(group, val)) +
  stat_summary(fun.y=mean, geom="text", aes(label=round(..y.., 2)))

ggplot(dat, aes(group, val)) +
  geom_text(aes(label=round(val, places)))
```

I ran into this problem while trying to write a ggplot function. At first I thought the problem involved ggplot not getting the parameter from the function environment, but the example above suggests that's not the issue. For completeness, below is a simplified example of the function, along with the error message. The function works fine if I hard-code the `digits` argument to `round`, rather than trying to pass the `places` parameter.

```
pp = function(data, group, var, places=2, e=1.5) {
  ggplot(data, aes_string(group, var)) +
    geom_boxplot() +
    stat_summary(fun.y=mean, geom="text", aes(label=round(..y.., places))) +
    scale_y_continuous(limits = e * range(data[,var]))
}

pp(dat, "group","val")
```

> Error in eval(expr, envir, enclos) : object 'places' not found

[I asked this question on StackOverflow](http://stackoverflow.com/questions/35806038/ggplot2-stat-summary-throws-error-when-trying-to-pass-function-argument-as-para) and user @alistaire diagnosed this as a non-standard evaluation issue. Here is the fix he came up with:

```
eval(substitute(ggplot(dat, aes(group, val)) +
                  stat_summary(fun.y=mean, geom="text", aes(label=round(..y.., places))), 
                list(places = places)))
```

This works, but I assume it can't be intended that `eval(substitute...` is necessary to pass a parameter to `stat_summary`. So I thought I'd post this here as an issue to see if it's a bug, if I'm doing something wrong, or if there's a better way to deal with this issue.

title: %>% operator in ggplot2
description:
Dplyr and ggplot2 are often used jointly. This makes existence of two functions that _seem_ to work similarly be confusing for some users (see https://stackoverflow.com/questions/35332861/what-is-the-difference-between-the-operator-in-ggplot2-and-the-operato). As ggplot2 user I also noticed that from time to time I write `%>%` instead of `+` when using ggplot2.

Why not define another alias for `+` in form:

`"%>%.gg" <- +.gg`

Similar approach was taken in dplyr where `summarise` and `summarize` can be used for the same function because of such user mistakes.

The linked SO thread also suggests that at this moment behaviour of `%>%` with gg objects is ambiguous and so such action should not interfere with any valid ggplot2 user behaviour.

```
summarySE <- function(data=NULL, measurevar, groupvars=NULL, na.rm=FALSE,
                      conf.interval=.95, .drop=TRUE) {
  library(plyr)

  length2 <- function (x, na.rm=FALSE) {
    if (na.rm) sum(!is.na(x))
    else       length(x)
  }

  datac <- ddply(data, groupvars, .drop=.drop,
                 .fun = function(xx, col) {
                   c(N    = length2(xx[[col]], na.rm=na.rm),
                     mean = mean   (xx[[col]], na.rm=na.rm),
                     sd   = sd     (xx[[col]], na.rm=na.rm)
                   )
                 },
                 measurevar
  )

  datac <- rename(datac, c("mean" = measurevar))

  datac$se <- datac$sd / sqrt(datac$N)  # Calculate standard error of the mean

  ciMult <- qt(conf.interval/2 + .5, datac$N-1)
  datac$ci <- datac$se * ciMult

  return(datac)
}
```

title: Class of gtable heights/widths is inconsistent across facet types
description:
In v1.0.1 `ggplotGrob(some_ggplot)$heights` was always a `unit.list` and I was able to use it to [calculate dimensions of fixed-aspect plots](https://github.com/infotroph/DeLuciatoR/blob/master/man/get_dims.Rd) as a workaround for #1163. 

In v2.0.0, the class of `heights` & `widths` depends how the plot is facetted:

```
p <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(wt,mpg))
class(ggplotGrob(p + facet_null())$heights)
# [1] "unit.list" "unit" 
class(ggplotGrob(p + facet_wrap(~cyl))$heights)
# [1] "unit"
class(ggplotGrob(p + facet_grid(.~cyl))$heights)
# [1] "unit"
```

I realize this isn't really API-supported territory, but it does provide (maybe the only?) access to rendered plot dimensions and I suggest keeping it accessible, and making it consistent between facet types, if that's practical.

title: Warnings with geom_vline()  when xintercept value has a name
description:
When using a named value for the xintercept of a vline there are warnings  thrown. I think this is because xintercept is used for both. I found it because of using quantiles, but it's a more general issue that there is a name assigned.

Minimal example:

```
#quartile1 <- quantile(mpg$cty, probs=c(.25)
quartile1 <-14
names(quartile1)<-"25%"

#generates warning
ggplot(mpg, aes(cty)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 1) +
  geom_vline(aes ( xintercept  = quartile1))

names(quartile1) <- NULL
#no warning
ggplot(mpg, aes(cty)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 1) +
  geom_vline(aes ( xintercept  = quartile1))

```

The warning generated is:
Warning message:

```
In data.frame(xintercept = 14, PANEL = c(1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L,  :
  row names were found from a short variable and have been discarded

```

At https://github.com/hadley/ggplot2/blob/master/R/geom-vline.r#L42 and L43 you end up with the duplicated row name.

This is similar to https://github.com/hadley/ggplot2/issues/1369 but not exactly the same since in that instance the names were created differently and it is always about quantiles, in this instance anytime there is a name there will be this warning.

title: Add subtitle object
description:
Would it be possible to add a subtitle object à la `ggtitle`? Right now, the approaches I've seen to add subtitles are  
- adding `\n` in the title text, but
  - they can't be themed differently, as typical for a subtitle;
- hacking with `atop`, but
  - some formatting (e.g. justification) is hard,
  - it's inconsistent, erroring out sometimes but not always, and
  - syntax is not obvious;
- using `annotation_custom` and `grid` to create grobs for title and subtitle, but
  - it requires more code than most plots.  

None of the approaches are really consistent with ggplot's style of plotting by adding simple objects.

Thus, given this is a very common task while plotting, would it be possible to  
- add a themable `ggsubtitle` object with reasonable default formatting, or
- allow inline control of `ggtitle`'s theme so two could be arranged suitably?

As ever, thank you for making R awesome.

title: RShiny mouse-click does not work with facet_grid
description:
Hi, after ggplot2 updated from ver 1.0.1 to 2.0.0, I found that interative facet_grid ggplot in shiny app is not working as expected as before. Below is an example of ggplot2 calendar heatmap. The data generation (which is not essential to this problem) is referenced from here: http://www.r-bloggers.com/ggplot2-time-series-heatmaps/  

Running this script with ggplot2 ver 1.0.1 works perfectly - when clicking anywhere on the plot, x and y coordinates are prompted. However with ver 2.0.0, no coordinates are shown. If commenting out the line of `facet_grid(year~monthf) +`, then it works again.

Any help is appreciated!

``` R
require(quantmod)
require(ggplot2)
require(reshape2)
require(plyr)
require(scales)
library(shiny)

#This function is only to produce data
getData = function(){
  # Download some Data, e.g. the CBOE VIX 
  getSymbols("^VIX",src="yahoo")

  # Make a dataframe
  dat<-data.frame(date=index(VIX),VIX)
  #cut
  dat <- dat[dat$date>as.Date("2015-01-01"),]

  # We will facet by year ~ month, and each subgraph will
  # show week-of-month versus weekday
  # the year is simple
  dat$year<-as.numeric(as.POSIXlt(dat$date)$year+1900)
  # the month too 
  dat$month<-as.numeric(as.POSIXlt(dat$date)$mon+1)
  # but turn months into ordered facors to control the appearance/ordering in the presentation
  dat$monthf<-factor(dat$month,levels=as.character(1:12),labels=c("Jan","Feb","Mar","Apr","May","Jun","Jul","Aug","Sep","Oct","Nov","Dec"),ordered=TRUE)
  # the day of week is again easily found
  dat$weekday = as.POSIXlt(dat$date)$wday
  # again turn into factors to control appearance/abbreviation and ordering
  # I use the reverse function rev here to order the week top down in the graph
  # you can cut it out to reverse week order
  dat$weekdayf<-factor(dat$weekday,levels=rev(1:7),labels=rev(c("Mon","Tue","Wed","Thu","Fri","Sat","Sun")),ordered=TRUE)
  # the monthweek part is a bit trickier 
  # first a factor which cuts the data into month chunks
  dat$yearmonth<-as.yearmon(dat$date)
  dat$yearmonthf<-factor(dat$yearmonth)
  # then find the "week of year" for each day
  dat$week <- as.numeric(format(dat$date,"%W"))
  # and now for each monthblock we normalize the week to start at 1 
  dat<-ddply(dat,.(yearmonthf),transform,monthweek=1+week-min(week))

  return(dat)

}

#######################################
#Shiny Server
server = function(input,output){
  data = getData()
  output$myplot = renderPlot({
    ggplot(data, aes(monthweek, weekdayf, fill = VIX.Close)) +
      geom_tile(colour = "white") + 
 ## >>>>> The following line makes the interactive plot not working w/ ggplot2 2.0.0
      facet_grid(year~monthf) +
 ## <<<<<
      scale_fill_gradient(low="red", high="yellow")
  })
  output$x = renderText(input$myplot_click$x)
  output$y = renderText(input$myplot_click$y)
}

#Shiny UI
ui = fluidPage(
  mainPanel(
    fluidRow(
      plotOutput("myplot" ,click = "myplot_click")
    ),
    fluidRow(
      verbatimTextOutput("x"), 
      verbatimTextOutput("y")
    )

  )
)

shinyApp(ui=ui,server=server)

```

title: Feature request: Function to combine distinct plots on same x-axis

Hi,
Apologies if this has already been discussed, but for time series and genomic plot amongst other things it is very convenient to be able to combine multiple disparate plots on exactly the same x-axis.

http://www.exegetic.biz/blog/2015/05/r-recipe-aligning-axes-in-ggplot2/

title: breaking change: alpha now impacts the line of stat_ based geoms.
description:
This has changed following #1371, and I think (personally) that this is the wrong decision. 
Pros: it's slightly more 'natural' to have alpha impacting both the line and fill (?)
Cons: the line texture is modified by the alpha parameter in a way that is irreversible, and thus you need a different geom for the common use case (to me) of having a solid line with a transparent filling.
Here is an example:

```
ggplot(diamonds %>% filter(cut %in% c("Very Good", "Ideal")), aes(x = price, fill = cut)) + theme_bw() + 
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 1000) +
  geom_density(aes(x = price, y = ..count.. * 1000), color = "NA", alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_density(aes(x = price, y = ..count.. * 1000), color = "black", fill = NA) +
  facet_grid(cut ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y")
```

I would vote for reverting this behavior, as I'm pretty sure it's breaking more graphing code now than it would if reverted for 2.1.

The downside of the old behavior is that you need to change the color directly if you want something lighter.

title: Examples using geom_smooth(), particularly method.args...
description:
Hello, 
    Further to feedback and an email, I have included below some code that has the potential to be used as examples for geom_smooth() particularly using method.args. 
    If useful that's great. If you want me to change or develop these I could do that - suggestions welcome. 
Best wishes, 
Paul

```
library(ggplot2)

# example of plotting tranforming data within the aesthetics
# and using geom_smooth with lm method. 
ggplot(msleep, aes(log(brainwt), log(bodywt))) +
  geom_point(na.rm = TRUE) +
  geom_smooth(method="lm")


# example of plot from the msleep dataset 
ggplot(msleep, aes(sleep_rem, sleep_total)) +
  geom_point()

# draw plot with geom_smooth defaults
# because h n < 1000 default smoothing method is loess.
ggplot(msleep, aes(sleep_rem, sleep_total)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth()
# line is feasable but doesn't make a huge amount of sense. 

# we can try applying the linear model (lm) method
ggplot(msleep, aes(sleep_rem, sleep_total)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm")
# it works but it's not a great fit...

# check a non linear least squares method (nls)
# note the use of the method.args
ggplot(msleep, aes(sleep_rem, sleep_total)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "nls", 
              se = FALSE, 
              method.args = list(formula = y ~ sleepMax * x / (halfREM + x), 
                                start = list(sleepMax = 22, halfREM = 1.5)))


# extended example using data from enzymes

# the data (from Dr C Bennett, University of Bath, http://www.jbc.org/content/285/44/33701.full)
enz <- c("WT","WT","WT","WT","WT","WT","WT","WT","WT","WT", "WT","WT","WT",
         "mutant","mutant","mutant","mutant","mutant","mutant", "mutant","mutant")
substrateConc <- c(2.00, 1.00, 0.60, 0.50, 0.40, 0.30, 0.20, 0.10, 0.09, 0.08, 0.06, 0.04, 0.02, 
         0.05, 0.10, 0.20, 0.30, 0.40, 0.50, 1.00, 2.00)
velocity <- c(59.01, 58.29, 54.17, 51.82, 49.76, 45.15, 36.88, 26.10, 23.50, 22.26, 
         16.45, 13.67, 6.14, 11.8, 19.9, 30.3, 36.6, 40.2, 42.1, 47.8, 50.0)

# assemble the data into a data.frame
enzdata <- data.frame(enz, substrateConc, velocity)

# first simple plot with just the points
ggplot(data=enzdata,        
       aes(x=substrateConc,            
           y=velocity,            
       colour = enz)) +  
       geom_point()             

# add the lines with geom_smooth, nls method and method.args
ggplot(data=enzdata,        
       aes(x=substrateConc,            
           y=velocity,            
           colour = enz)) +  
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "nls",
              se = FALSE,
              size = 0.5,
              method.args = list(formula = y ~ Vmax * x / (Km + x), 
                                start = list(Vmax = 50, Km = 0.2)))

# add facet_wrap to create two graphs if you prefer...
ggplot(data=enzdata,        
       aes(x=substrateConc,            
           y=velocity,            
           colour = enz)) +  
  geom_point() +
  facet_wrap(~enz) + 
  geom_smooth(method = "nls",
              se = FALSE,
              size = 0.5,
              method.args = list(formula = y ~ Vmax * x / (Km + x), 
                                 start = list(Vmax = 50, Km = 0.2))) 
```

title: `subset` argument broken for all geoms in v2
description:
The following code was working with ggplot2 v1.X but does not longer with v2

```
require(ggplot2)
require(plyr)

ggplot(iris, aes(Sepal.Length, Sepal.Width)) + geom_point(subset=.(Species=="setosa"))
```

The reported error is `Error: Unknown parameters: subset`. The same problem occurs all of all other geoms.

Digging through the ggplot sources, it seems that in `R/geom-point.r:129` the subset argument becomes an element of the `params` list. However in `R/layer.r:22` it's still a separate argument. So simply changing `R/layer.r:75` to   use `subset = params$subset,` instead of `subset = subset,' might fix the problem.

I've noticed the deprecation warning for the `subset` argument in `R/layer.r:9`. However I could not find what the new suggested way should look like. It was/is a very useful element of the ggplot API that I used to define custom DSLs (e.g. by using unevaluated layer definitions as function arguments that were internally used to build plots).

title: partially named values in scales
description:
If I understand current behavior correctly, the values vector in a scale function is matched by name if there are (any) names and by position otherwise.  Would you consider matching by names when the name is present and by position among unnamed items when the name isn't there?

I'm imagining a use case like this:

``` r
scale_colour_discrete <- 
  function(values = c(male = "skyblue", female = "pink", "navy", "red", "green", "purple"), ...) {
    scale_color_manual(values = values, ...)
  }
```

The idea is that this would use blue and pink for male and female, but use navy, red, green, purple for other levels.  In the context of a given document, one could expand this to fix colors for levels that will occur in many contexts but still make it possible to plot other data without having to keep changing/specifying the scale function.

Of course, this idea should work for other things (like fill, size, alpha, etc.) as well.

PS.  Redefining `scale_colour_discrete()` like this should really be documented somewhere.
